10:4.headline: A hammer named for the holes it punches
10:4.body: The idol makers fix the metal on with nails and מקבות, hammers. Metzudat Zion says the hammer is called this because its head is sharp, for punching (נקב) holes in stone. It is the same tool Yael used on Sisera.

sources.quote: הוא הפטיש כמו ותשם את המקבת בידה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a hammer, as in Judges 4:21 where Yael took the hammer in her hand.

sources.quote: ויקרא כן ע״ש שראשו א׳ חד לנקוב בו האבנים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is named so because one end of its head is sharp, for boring holes in stones.

sources.quote: וּמַקָּבוֹת. קוֹרְנָס
sources.says: Rashi says מקבות are hammers.

10:8.headline: Not 'they burn' but 'they are brutish'
10:8.body: בער usually means to burn. Here, Rashi and Metzudat Zion say it means to be dull and foolish, like the 'brutish man' of Psalms. Malbim says the בער lacks knowledge, while the כסיל, the fool in the same verse, may know but is led by desire.

sources.quote: יִבְעֲרוּ לְשׁוֹן שְׁטוּת, וְכֵן וְיִכְסָלוּ
sources.says: Rashi says יבערו is a word for foolishness, and so is ויכסלו.

sources.quote: יבערו. מלשון בער ושוטה וכן איש בער לא ידע
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from בער, a fool, as in 'a brutish man does not know' in Psalms 92.

sources.quote: הבערות הוא מחסרון מדע, והכסיל הוא לפעמים חכם ויודע רק נרדף מן התאוה
sources.says: Malbim says brutishness is a lack of knowledge, while the fool is sometimes wise and knowing but chased by desire.

10:9.headline: Gold from a place called Uphaz, or gold refined pure?
10:9.body: The idols are covered with זהב מאופז. The Aramaic Targum reads it as a place, Ophir, famous for gold. Metzudat Zion reads it as a kind of fine gold. Malbim says the goldsmith refines it until it becomes like פז, pure gold.

sources.quote: וְדַהֲבָא מֵאוֹפִיר
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'and gold from Ophir'.

sources.quote: מאופז. מין זהב טוב וכן בכתם אופז
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a kind of good gold, as in Daniel 10.

sources.quote: כי יצרף ויזקק את הזהב עד שישוב להיות כפז
sources.says: Malbim says the smith refines and purifies the gold until it becomes like fine gold.

10:10.headline: God is called 'true' because He lives to keep His word
10:10.body: The idols are a lie, but God is אלהים אמת, a true God. Rashi explains why: He lives forever, so He can make His words come true. A person may promise and then die or grow weak before he can do it.

sources.quote: לְכָךְ יָכוֹל לְאַמֵּת דְּבָרָיו
sources.says: Rashi says because God is living and King forever, He is able to make His words come true.

sources.quote: אוֹמֵר לַעֲשׂוֹת, וּמֵת אוֹ תָּשַׁשׁ כֹּחוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says a person of flesh and blood says he will do something, then dies or loses his strength.

sources.quote: אלה האלהים שעושין לעבדם הם שקר והם מתים
sources.says: Radak says the gods people make to serve are a lie and dead, but God alone is truly God.

10:11.headline: Two Aramaic words for 'earth' in one verse
10:11.body: The verse says 'earth' twice, first ארקא and then ארעא. ארקא appears nowhere else in the Bible. Malbim says ארעא comes from 'below', while ארקא comes from 'running', the earth in motion. Radak cites the sages, who list ארקא as one of the earth's four names.

sources.quote: תרגום של ארץ הוא ארעא, שהוא מענין תחתית
sources.says: Malbim says ארעא, the usual Aramaic for earth, comes from the idea of 'below'.

sources.quote: והעתק של ארץ מענין מרוצה הוא ארקא
sources.says: Malbim says ארקא is the word for earth taken from the idea of running.

sources.quote: ובדברי רז"ל ארבע שמות נקראו לה כנגד ארבע תקופותיה ארץ תבל אדמה ארקא
sources.says: Radak says the sages taught the earth has four names, matching its four seasons, and ארקא is one.

10:19.headline: Not 'inheritance' here, but 'grievous'
10:19.body: נחלה usually means an inheritance. Here the commentators read it from חלי, sickness: 'my wound is grievous'. Radak says it means painful.

sources.quote: נַחְלָה. לְשׁוֹן חוֹלִי
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word for sickness.

sources.quote: נחלה פירוש נכאבת כלומר מכה קשה היא
sources.says: Radak says it means painful, a severe wound.

10:21.headline: The kings did not 'succeed', not just 'understand'
10:21.body: השכילו usually means to be wise. Rashi and Radak read it here as to succeed, as when David 'succeeded in all his ways'. Metzudat David links the two: one who succeeds looks like he acts with wisdom.

sources.quote: לֹא הִשְׂכִּילוּ. לֹא הִצְלִיחוּ בְּמַלְכוּתָם
sources.says: Rashi says it means they did not succeed in their reign.

sources.quote: לא השכילו. לא הצליחו כמו ויהי דוד בכל דרכיו משכיל
sources.says: Radak says it means they did not succeed, as in 'David succeeded in all his ways'.

sources.quote: לא הצליחו על כי המצליח נראה שעושה דבריו בהשכל
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means succeed, because one who succeeds seems to act with wisdom.

11:4.headline: Egypt is called a furnace that refined Israel like gold
11:4.body: A כּוּר is the pot where metal is melted to burn off its waste. Radak and the Metzudat David say the hard years in Egypt purified Israel the way a furnace refines silver and gold.

sources.quote: שהיו הם במצרף הצרוף כמו שצורפין הכסף והזהב בכור
sources.says: Radak says they were in a refining pot, the way silver and gold are refined in a furnace.

sources.quote: הוא הכלי שצורפין בו הזהב
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says a כור is the vessel used to refine gold.

sources.quote: נצרפתם שם בצרוף הצרות כמו שצורפין זהב בכור ברזל
sources.says: The Metzudat David says they were refined there by suffering, as gold is refined in an iron furnace.

11:7.headline: A verb built on 'witness' here means 'I warned'
11:7.body: הַעִדֹתִי comes from עֵד, a witness. Rashi and the Metzudat Zion say it means 'I warned you', because a warning was usually given in front of witnesses so no one could deny it.

sources.quote: הָעֵד הַעִדֹתִי. לְשׁוֹן הַתְרָאָה
sources.says: Rashi says the phrase means warning.

sources.quote: ענין התראה כי ע״פ רוב מתרין בעדים לבל יכחשו
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says it means warning, since warnings are usually given before witnesses so that people cannot deny them.

sources.quote: שֶׁסְּתָם הַתְרָאָה מַתְרֶה בוֹ בִּפְנֵי עֵדִים, וְכֵן הַעִדֹתִי בַּאֲבוֹתֵיכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says an ordinary warning is given before witnesses, and cites this verse as an example.

11:15.headline: Who is the 'beloved' in God's house? The commentators disagree
11:15.body: Rashi says God is speaking and the beloved is Israel, His treasured people. Radak says the prophet is speaking and calls God his beloved, and he cites a midrash where God says it to Abraham, who came to the Temple to plead for his children.

sources.quote: מָה לְעַם סְגֻלָּתִי לָבֹא עוֹד בְּבֵיתִי
sources.says: Rashi says it means: what right has My treasured people to come into My house any more.

sources.quote: קרא האל ידידי לפי שהוא היה מאוהבי האל
sources.says: Radak says the prophet called God 'my beloved' because he was one of those who loved God.

sources.quote: לאברהם עומד בבית המקדש ואמר לו מה לידידי בביתי
sources.says: Radak cites a midrash in which God finds Abraham standing in the Temple and says to him, 'What is my beloved doing in my house?'

11:15.headline: 'Holy flesh': sacrifices, circumcision, or holy people?
11:15.body: The Metzudat David says the holy flesh is the sacrifices, which God no longer wants. Rashi says it is circumcision, which they had dropped, and Radak brings a reading that it means the holy people, who have left.

sources.quote: הקרבנות שאתה מקריב שמה יעברו ממך כי אינני חפץ בהם
sources.says: The Metzudat David says the sacrifices you offer there will pass from you, because God does not want them.

sources.quote: אַף הַמִּילָה בִּטְּלוּ מִבְּשָׂרָם
sources.says: Rashi says they even removed circumcision from their flesh.

sources.quote: החסידים אנשי קדש עברו מעליך
sources.says: Radak brings a reading that the pious, the holy people, have left you.

11:16.headline: Why God once called Judah a fresh olive tree
11:16.body: Radak says an olive stays green all year, like Israel's success while it did God's will, and its oil honors God and people. Rashi elsewhere uses this verse to show that the tribe of Judah is called an olive.

sources.quote: המשילה לזית לפי שהוא רענן כל זמן וכל ימות השנה עליו לחים
sources.says: Radak says the prophet compares her to an olive because it is fresh all year and its leaves stay moist.

sources.quote: דומים לפרי זית אשר בדשנו והוא שמנו יכבדו אלהים ואנשים
sources.says: Radak says their good deeds were like the olive, whose oil honors God and people.

sources.quote: הַבָּא מִשֵּׁבֶט יְהוּדָה שֶׁנִּקְרָא זַיִת
sources.says: Rashi says the olive in the fable is a man from the tribe of Judah, which is called an olive.

11:16.headline: A rare word for the roar of a crowd, built from 'word'
11:16.body: הֲמוּלָּה appears only here and in Ezekiel. Rashi says it is the noise of a great army; Radak and Malbim tie it to מִלָּה, a word, so it is the sound of many voices at once.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן שָׁאוֹן עַם רַב שֶׁיָּבֹא עֲלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it means the uproar of a large people that will come against them.

sources.quote: ופי' המולה כמו מלה כמו אין מלה בלשוני
sources.says: Radak says המולה is like מלה, a word, as in 'there is no word on my tongue'.

sources.quote: משורש מלל ודבור, ובא על מלולים רבים
sources.says: Malbim says it comes from the root for speech and means many voices talking.

11:16.headline: The branches that will break are the high ones
11:16.body: Radak says דָּלִיּוֹת, branches, comes from the word for lifting up, as in 'You have lifted me up'. So even the highest branches will break, a picture of Jerusalem and the Temple.

sources.quote: מלשון ארוממך ה' כי דליתני שפירושו רוממתני
sources.says: Radak says the word comes from 'I will exalt You, Lord, for You have lifted me up'.

sources.quote: שאפילו הענפים הרמים ישברו והוא משל על ירושלם ובית המקדש
sources.says: Radak says even the high branches will be broken, a picture of Jerusalem and the Temple.

sources.quote: ענפים גדולים
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says the word means large branches.

11:19.headline: 'Like a lamb, an aluf': lamb and ox, or prize lamb?
11:19.body: Rashi reports two old readings: Dunash says it means 'a lamb and an ox' led to slaughter, while Menahem says it is 'a great lamb', and Targum Jonathan agrees with 'a chosen lamb'. Malbim reads it as a tame lamb that trusts its owner and follows him.

sources.quote: דּוּנָשׁ וִיהוּדָה בֶּן קוּרִישׁ פֵּתְרוּהוּ: כְּכֶבֶשׂ וּפָר אֲשֶׁר יוּבַל לִטְבוֹחַ
sources.says: Rashi says Dunash and Yehuda ben Kuraysh read it as a lamb and a bull led to slaughter.

sources.quote: וּמְנַחֵם פֵּתֵר כֶּבֶשׂ אַלּוּף – כֶּבֶשׂ גָּדוֹל
sources.says: Rashi says Menahem reads it as a great lamb, and Targum Jonathan supports him.

sources.quote: כְּאִימַר בְּחִיר
sources.says: Targum Jonathan translates it as a chosen lamb.

sources.quote: והייתי דומה לכבש המלומד ללכת אחרי בעליו
sources.says: Malbim says Jeremiah was like a lamb trained to follow its owner.

11:19.headline: 'Let us destroy the tree in his bread' means poison
11:19.body: Targum Jonathan and Radak read it as a plot to put poison in Jeremiah's food: the 'tree' is a deadly plant. Malbim says they wanted a quiet death, because a prophet killed openly is remembered as a martyr.

sources.quote: נִרְמֵי סַמָא דְמוֹתָא בְּמֵיכְלֵיהּ
sources.says: Targum Jonathan translates: let us throw a deadly drug into his food.

sources.quote: ועץ פירוש עץ מות כלומר עץ שהוא סם המות
sources.says: Radak says the tree means a tree of death, that is, a deadly poison.

sources.quote: כי הנביא הנהרג ע"י חרב, שמו נזכר בכל דור שנהרג על קידוש השם
sources.says: Malbim says a prophet killed by the sword is remembered in every generation as dying for God, so they planned a hidden death.

11:23.headline: 'No remnant' for Anathoth, yet 128 of its men came home
11:23.body: Radak notes that 128 men of Anathoth returned from Babylon. He explains that when the city fell its people repented, so some survived after all.

sources.quote: עשו תשובה והיתה להם שארית וכן אמרו רז"ל וכן מצאנו בשוב גלות בבל אנשי ענתות מאה ועשרים ושמונה
sources.says: Radak says they repented and so had a remnant, and that 128 men of Anathoth returned from the Babylonian exile.

12:1.headline: Jeremiah takes God to court while granting that God is right
12:1.body: Jeremiah grants that God is right, yet he will argue 'judgments' with Him like a man in court. Malbim explains the two words: a ריב is a claim in an unclear case, like a good man who suffers, but a משפט is a clear case, like the wicked who prosper.

sources.quote: ההבדל בין ריב ובין משפט, שריב הוא טענת הבעלי דינים, ובדבר שאינו מבורר, והמשפט הוא בדבר מבורר
sources.says: Malbim says a ריב is a claim in a matter that is not clear, while a משפט is about a clear matter, such as the wicked who prosper.

sources.quote: אך אדבר עמך כאדם הנשפט על חברו ונושא ונותן בטענות הנדונין כי אני נבוך בזה
sources.says: Radak says Jeremiah will argue with God like a man in a lawsuit, because he is confused by this.

sources.quote: אַךְ חָפֵץ אֲנִי לְדַבֵּר מִשְׁפָּטִים אוֹתָךְ, לְהוֹדִיעֵנִי דַּרְכֶּךָ
sources.says: Rashi says Jeremiah knows God will be right, but wants to argue in order to learn God's ways.

12:2.headline: Near in their mouths, far from their kidneys: lips without the heart
12:2.body: The kidneys stand for a person's inner thoughts. Maimonides uses this verse twice: for one who says God is One without understanding it, and for one who prays with moving lips while thinking about his business.

sources.quote: אבל רחוק אתה ממחשבות כליותיהם ולא יאמינו בך באמת
sources.says: The Metzudat David says God is far from the thoughts of their kidneys, and they do not truly believe.

sources.quote: לא ממי שאומר זאת בפיו ואינו מצייר לו משמעות
sources.says: Maimonides applies the verse to one who says God is One with his mouth but does not grasp what it means.

sources.quote: ואם אתה מתפלל בהנעת שפתיך כאשר אתה פונה אל הקיר וחושב על משאך ומתנך
sources.says: Maimonides applies the verse to one who prays with his lips while thinking about his business.

12:3.headline: 'Make them holy' for slaughter means set them aside
12:3.body: הקדש usually means to make holy. Rashi and the Metzudat Zion say here it means to prepare or set aside, as in Joel's קדשו קהל, 'call an assembly'.

sources.quote: וְהַקְדִּישֵׁם. הַזְמִינֵם
sources.says: Rashi says it means prepare them.

sources.quote: והקדישם. ענין הזמנה כמו קדשו קהל
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says it means preparing, as in 'קדשו קהל'.

12:5.headline: 'The pride of the Jordan': lion country, or swelling waves?
12:5.body: Rashi and the Metzudat Zion say גאון הירדן is the high ground by the Jordan where lions live. Radak reads it as the place where the Jordan's waves rise up, an image for the princes of Judah.

sources.quote: וּגְאוֹן הַיַּרְדֵּן מָשָׁל הוּא, לְפִי שֶׁהוּא מְקוֹם אֲרָיוֹת וּנְמֵרִים
sources.says: Rashi says it is a figure of speech, because it is a place of lions and leopards.

sources.quote: ככר המעולה הסמוך לירדן ושם היה מקום האריות
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says it is the high plain near the Jordan where the lions lived.

sources.quote: כלומר במקום שמתגאין גלי הירדן
sources.says: Radak says it is the place where the Jordan's waves rise high, a figure for the princes of Judah.

12:6.headline: 'Full' behind you: a crowd, or a word meaning its opposite?
12:6.body: Rashi says מלא means a gathered crowd chasing Jeremiah. Radak reports that Rabbeinu Hai read it as a word said by its opposite, meaning 'lacking', the way a blind man is politely called 'much light'.

sources.quote: קָרְאוּ אַחֲרֶיךָ מָלֵא. קְבוּצַת אֲנָשִׁים
sources.says: Rashi says מלא means a gathering of people.

sources.quote: ורבינו האי פירש מלא מן המלות שמפרשין אותן בהפכן כלומר חסר בכל דבר
sources.says: Radak reports Rabbeinu Hai's view that מלא is said in place of its opposite and means lacking in everything.

12:7.headline: God did not just leave His house; He let it go
12:7.body: Malbim says עזב is to leave and walk away, while נטש is stronger: to put a thing out of your hands. The Land's holiness is lasting, so God had to cast it off in deed and hand it to its enemies.

sources.quote: העזיבה מציין שעוזבו והולך לו, והנטישה הוא שמוציא הדבר מרשותו בפועל, והוא יותר מן עזיבה
sources.says: Malbim says leaving means walking away, while נטישה means actually putting the thing out of one's possession, which is more than leaving.

12:9.headline: A 'dyed' bird: stained with blood, or so bright others attack it?
12:9.body: Rashi first reads צבוע as a bird stained with blood. In his second reading, and in the Metzudat David, it is a many-colored bird that the other birds hate and gather to attack, as the nations gather on Israel.

sources.quote: הֲכִי הֵם עוֹף צָבוּעַ, מְגֹאָל בְּדָם
sources.says: Rashi first asks: are they a bird stained with blood, that other birds gather on it?

sources.quote: כעיט הצבוע בעלת גוונים השנואה לכל העופות
sources.says: The Metzudat David says it is a many-colored bird hated by all other birds, which gather around to eat it.

12:11.headline: The land mourns 'on Me': before God, or blaming Him?
12:11.body: Rashi reads עלי as 'before Me'. Radak and Malbim read it as mourning against God, as if He alone had made her desolate.

sources.quote: אָבְלָה עָלַי. לְפָנַי
sources.says: Rashi says עלי means before Me.

sources.quote: התאבלה עלי על שממותיה לאמר שאני השימותיה
sources.says: Radak says she mourned to God over her ruins, saying that He made her desolate.

sources.quote: הנה היא מתאבלת עלי כאילו אני עשיתי לה כל זאת
sources.says: Malbim says she mourns against God as if He did all this to her, though the cause was that no one took it to heart.

12:14.headline: God calls Israel's hostile neighbors 'My neighbors'
12:14.body: Rashi lists them: Egypt, Ammon, Moab, Tyre and Sidon. Radak says God calls them His own neighbors because Israel is His field and vineyard, so whoever borders Israel borders Him.

sources.quote: מִצְרַיִם, עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב וְצוֹר וְצִידוֹן, שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁכֵנֵי אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says these are Egypt, Ammon, Moab, Tyre and Sidon, the neighbors of the Land of Israel who harmed it.

sources.quote: ואמר שכני כי ישראל הם חלקתו וכרמו והנה הם שכניו
sources.says: Radak says God says 'My neighbors' because Israel is His field and vineyard, so the nations around it are His neighbors.

13:1.headline: אזור is a tight belt that braces the loins
13:1.body: Malbim's word list says אזור is not the general belt (חגור) or the priest's אבנט. It is a belt tied tight to brace the loins, a picture of might.

sources.quote: אבל אזור הוא חגור מיוחד לחזק בו את מתניו והיה אוסרו בחוזק, והוא ציור הגבורה
sources.says: Malbim says אזור is a special belt for bracing the loins, tied tight, and it is a picture of might.

sources.quote: וכמו שהאזור סימן הגבורה כן היו לתהלה
sources.says: Malbim says the belt is a sign of might, and that matches Israel being made a praise (תהלה).

13:10.headline: שרירות may be tied to seeing: what the heart sees and wants
13:10.body: Metzudat Zion glosses it as במראה, in what is seen. Metzudat David says it is what their heart shows them and craves, and Jonathan has "the thought of their heart".

sources.quote: בשררות. במראה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion glosses בשררות as "in what is seen".

sources.quote: במה שלבם מראה להם ומתאוה לה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is what their heart shows them and craves.

sources.quote: דְאָזְלִין בָּתַר הִרְהוּר לִבְּהוֹן
sources.says: Jonathan translates it as going after the thought of their heart.

13:12.headline: נבל: a clay jar to Rashi, a wineskin to Metzudat Zion
13:12.body: Rashi calls it a clay vessel for wine, and Metzudat Zion calls it a wineskin (נאד). Malbim says it is clay made only for wine, which the clay soaks up, and is not the same as the skin words.

sources.quote: כְּלִי חֶרֶס הוּא, וְעָשׂוּי לְהַכְנִיס בּוֹ יָיִן
sources.says: Rashi says a נבל is a clay vessel, made to hold wine.

sources.quote: נאד היין וכן ונבל יין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נבל is a wineskin, like "a skin of wine" in 1 Samuel 1.

sources.quote: שם נבל נבדל מן נאד, חמת, אוב, הנרדפים עמו, שהוא מיוחד רק ליין, וחמת ונאד, נמצא חמת מים, ונאד החלב, והוא מחרס אשר החרס בולע היין אל תוכו
sources.says: Malbim says נבל differs from the skin words, is only for wine, and is clay that soaks up the wine.

13:14.headline: ונפצתים means to smash, as a clay jar is smashed
13:14.body: Rashi says it means dashing one against another until they break into fine pieces, like a potter's vessel. Malbim says נפץ is breaking apart one solid piece, and the word is borrowed for a people scattered.

sources.quote: אַכֶּה זֶה עַל זֶה, עַד שֶׁיִּשָּׁבְרוּ חֲתִיכוֹת דַּקּוֹת; כְּמוֹ ״כִּכְלִי יוֹצֵר תְּנַפְּצֵם
sources.says: Rashi says it means striking one against another until they break into fine pieces, like a potter's vessel.

sources.quote: ובא עליו פעל נפץ, שבא על פיזור חלקים של דבר מתדבק מקשה אחת, והושאל על נפוץ העם ופרוד חבורם
sources.says: Malbim says נפץ is breaking one solid piece into parts, and it is borrowed for a people scattered and parted.

13:14.headline: Three words for pity: חמל, חוס and רחם each mean something different
13:14.body: Malbim says רחם is pity for a person only. חוס is sparing something because it is useful, and חמל is sparing it because it is whole and good in itself.

sources.quote: הרחמים לא יהיה רק על האדם, וחמלה וחוס יהיה גם על שאר דברים כמ"ש (ישעיה י"ג) וההבדל בין חוס ובין חמל, חוסה תהיה מצד צרכו אל הדבר, כמו ועיניכם אל תחוס על כליכם, והחמלה תהיה מצד הדבר עצמו שרואה שהוא שלם וטוב וחומל מהשחיתו מצד עצמו
sources.says: Malbim says רחם is only for people, חוס is sparing because the thing is needed, and חמל is sparing because the thing is whole and good in itself.

13:16.headline: Maimonides: כבוד can mean a created light, God's essence, or praise
13:16.body: In the Guide, כבוד has three senses: a created light God places somewhere, God's own essence, and praise. He gives this verse, "give the Lord your God כבוד", as his example of praise.

sources.quote: יש שהכוונה בו היא האור הנברא שה' משרה במקום מסוים
sources.says: Maimonides says one sense of כבוד is the created light that God rests in a place.

sources.quote: ויש שהכוונה בו היא עצמותו יתעלה ואמיתתו
sources.says: Maimonides says another sense of כבוד is God's own essence.

sources.quote: כי השיבוח נקרא כבוד; נאמר: "תְּנוּ לַה' אֱלֹהֵיכֶם כָּבוֹד
sources.says: Maimonides says praise is called כבוד, and gives "give the Lord your God כבוד" as his example.

13:18.headline: השפילו: "sit low", or "lower your thrones and sit on the ground"
13:18.body: Radak gives two readings. It may be a verb that stays with the subject, sit down low, or a verb that acts on something, lower your thrones and sit on the ground.

sources.quote: כאילו אמר שבו בשפל, כי השפילו פעל עומד כמו כי השפילו ותאמר גוה או יהיה פעל יוצא ופירושו השפילו כסאכם ושבו על הקרקע
sources.says: Radak says השפילו is either like "sit low", or means lower your thrones and sit on the ground.

sources.quote: שבו במקום שפל מוטה לארץ ואל תשבו על כסאות
sources.says: Metzudat David says to sit in a low place near the ground, and not on thrones.

13:18.headline: מראשותיכם: what rests at your head, your greatness, or your rule
13:18.body: Malbim says it is what lies around the head, and Metzudat Zion says it is your greatness, from ראש. Radak says it names rule and kingdom.

sources.quote: מה שמונח סביב ראשו
sources.says: Malbim says מראשותיכם is what is placed around the head.

sources.quote: מלשון ראש ור״ל גדולתכם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from ראש and means your greatness.

sources.quote: והוא שם לרשות ולממלכה
sources.says: Radak says it is a word for rule and kingdom.

13:19.headline: שלומים may mean peace, complete, or repayment
13:19.body: Rashi gives two readings: Jehoiachin went out in peace and did not fight, or it means payment for their sins, as Jonathan has it. Metzudat David reads it as a complete exile.

sources.quote: לֹא יִלָּחֵם יְהוֹיָכִין, כִּי לְשָׁלוֹם יֵצֵא
sources.says: Rashi says Jehoiachin will not fight, since he will go out in peace.

sources.quote: שְׁלוֹמִים גרדונאמינ״ץ בְּלַעַז, כְּלוֹמַר: תַּשְׁלוּם עֲוֹנָם; וְכֵן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״אִיתְקַבְּלוּ תּוֹשְׁלַמַת חוֹבֵיהוֹן
sources.says: Rashi gives a second reading, payment for their sins, and says Jonathan translates it that way.

sources.quote: ר״ל גלות שלימה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means a complete exile.

13:27.headline: Three words for adultery: the act, the open show, the buried thought
13:27.body: Malbim says נאוף is the act itself, and זמת is the thought sunk deep into it. In his larger comment he reads the verse as act, public show and deep thought.

sources.quote: הנאוף הוא פעולת הנאוף עצמו והזנות היא היציאה להפקר (כנ"ל ג' ח'). וזמת הזנות היא השתקעות המחשבה בזנות
sources.says: Malbim says נאוף is the act itself, זנות is going out to a free-for-all, and זמת is the thought sunk into it.

sources.quote: וגם זמת זנותך שהם המחשבות העמוקות שיש לך אל הזנות, המעשה והמחשבה והפרסום
sources.says: Malbim says זמת is the deep thoughts toward it, and lists the act, the thought and the public show.

13:27.headline: מצהלותיך is the neighing of a horse, used for lust
13:27.body: Rashi ties it to "like the neighing of lustful horses" in Jeremiah 5:8. Malbim says the word is borrowed from a horse's neigh at the time of lust.

sources.quote: כְּצַהֲלַת סוּסִים נוֹאֲפִים
sources.says: Rashi says it is like the neighing of lustful horses.

sources.quote: הושאל מצהלת הסוס בעת הזנות
sources.says: Malbim says the word is borrowed from a horse's neigh at the time of lust.

14:2.headline: שעריה may mean its gates or its fortified cities
14:2.body: Radak reads it as the city gates, which stand empty or where the elders no longer sit. Malbim says it means the fortified cities.

sources.quote: אין יוצא ואין בא בהם או ששבתו הזקנים משבת בשערים כמו שאמר זקנים משער שבתו
sources.says: Radak says the gates are empty because no one goes in or out, or because the elders stopped sitting in the gates.

sources.quote: שעריה אומללו הם הערים הבצורות
sources.says: Malbim says שעריה means the fortified cities.

14:2.headline: וצוחת is a great outcry, one that leaves the throat dry
14:2.body: Rashi reads it as a cry, like "from the mountaintops they shout". Malbim says it is a great, strange outcry that shouts the throat dry and hoarse.

sources.quote: צַעֲקַת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, כְּמוֹ ״מֵרֹאשׁ הָרִים יִצְוָחוּ
sources.says: Rashi says it is the cry of Jerusalem, like "from the mountaintops they shout" in Isaiah 42:11.

sources.quote: היא הזעקה הגדולה המשונה עד שגרונו צחה צמא ונחר מרוב זעקתו
sources.says: Malbim says it is the great, strange outcry, until the throat is dry and hoarse from shouting.

14:3.headline: בשו and הכלמו differ: shame from yourself, shame from others
14:3.body: The verse puts two shame words side by side. Malbim says בושה comes from within, and כלימה comes from other people.

sources.quote: בושה מעצמו וכלימה מאחרים
sources.says: Malbim says בושה comes from oneself and כלימה comes from others.

14:5.headline: דשא is the green covering of the land; עשב is one plant
14:5.body: The verse says there was no דשא, and the next verse says there was no עשב. Malbim says the land clothed in grass is called דשא, while one particular plant is called עשב.

sources.quote: לבישת הארץ בעשבים נקרא דשא, ועשב מיוחד נקרא עשב
sources.says: Malbim says the land's covering of grasses is called דשא, and a particular plant is called עשב.

14:8.headline: מקוה is the one we hope in; תקוה is hope itself
14:8.body: Malbim says מקוה is not the same word as תקוה. מקוה is the one through whom people hope for something, and תקוה is the hope itself.

sources.quote: יש הבדל בינו ובין תקוה, שמקוה היא שע"י יקוו לאיזה דבר שכן הוראת השמות שמ"ם בראשם, ותקוה הוא שם המופשט של התקוה בעצמה
sources.says: Malbim says מקוה differs from תקוה: מקוה is the one people hope through, and תקוה is hope itself.

14:8.headline: Why Jonathan does not say God is "like a stranger"
14:8.body: Radak says the Targums keep human traits away from the Creator. So Jonathan turns "why will You be like a stranger" into a line about Israel: we are like settlers in the land.

sources.quote: אונקלוס מתרגם התורה ויונתן בן עוזיאל מתרגם ספרי הנביאים רחוק מעל הבורא יחסי התארים וענין הפסוק גם כן ואשר אחריו הסב יונתן הדבר הנאמר על האל על ישראל
sources.says: Radak says Onkelos and Jonathan keep the Creator far from human traits, and that Jonathan turns what is said of God into a line about Israel.

sources.quote: וַאֲנַחְנָא כְּתוֹתָבִין בְּאַרְעָא
sources.says: Jonathan has "we are like settlers in the land" in place of God being like a stranger.

14:9.headline: נדהם appears only here, and each commentator reads it differently
14:9.body: Rashi says it means pulling the hand back from war, and gives a French word for it. Radak's father ties it to an Arabic word for a heart covered over by sickness, and Malbim says it is a person whose senses have stopped.

sources.quote: מוֹשֵׁךְ יָדוֹ מִן הַמִּלְחָמָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means pulling one's hand back from war, and gives the French word.

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי ז"ל כתב כי מפרש אותו מן הערבי למי שהוא מכוסה לב מחלי מדהום
sources.says: Radak quotes his father, who explains the word from Arabic, for someone whose heart is covered over by sickness.

sources.quote: אין לו ריע, וענינו אדם שנתבטלו חושיו והרגשותיו
sources.says: Malbim says the word has no parallel and means a person whose senses and feelings have shut down.

14:9.headline: תנחנו: Rashi says abandon, Malbim says leave us stuck in trouble
14:9.body: Rashi explains it as "abandon us", as in Lamentations 5. Malbim says it cannot mean abandon here, since God is among us, so the plea is "do not leave us in trouble".

sources.quote: פֵּירוּשׁוֹ כְּמוֹ ״תַּעַזְבֵנוּ
sources.says: Rashi says it means the same as "abandon us" in Lamentations 5:20.

sources.quote: לא יכול לאמר אל תעזבנו, כי לא עזב אותנו והוא בתוכנו, רק הבקשה בל יניח אותנו בצרה
sources.says: Malbim says it cannot mean "do not abandon us", since He is in our midst, so it asks that He not leave us in our trouble.

14:12.headline: רנתם: a cry for Radak, the opening songs of prayer for Malbim
14:12.body: Radak says רנה here means a cry, like "rise, cry out (רני) in the night". Malbim says it is the singing and praise that come first, before the prayer itself.

sources.quote: אל רנתם פי' אל צעקתם כמו קומי רני בלילה
sources.says: Radak says אל רנתם means to their cry, like "rise, cry out in the night".

sources.quote: הרנה קודמת אל התפלה שיקדימו תחלה שירות ותשבחות
sources.says: Malbim says the singing comes before the prayer, with songs and praise first.

14:14.headline: אליל, "idol", also means "nothing": an empty claim
14:14.body: Rashi ties it to אל, "no", so it is a thing that is not. Radak says the prophets' claim that no sword or famine would come was exactly that: nothing.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן אַל, דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says אליל comes from אל, a thing that is not.

sources.quote: ואליל הוא דבר שאינו וזה שהם אומרים חרב ורעב לא יהיה זהו דבר שאינו
sources.says: Radak says אליל is a thing that is not, and the prophets' claim that there would be no sword or famine is such a thing.

14:18.headline: סחרו: went around seeking rescue, or went around trading
14:18.body: The root means going around, and it is also the word for a merchant. Rashi says they went around looking for rescue, and Jonathan reads it as going about their trade.

sources.quote: סָבְבוּ לְבַקֵּשׁ הַצָּלָה
sources.says: Rashi says they went around to look for rescue.

sources.quote: ענין סבוב ועל שם זה נקרא התגר בשם סוחר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the root means going around, and the trader is called סוחר because he goes around after goods.

sources.quote: אִתְפְּנִיאוּ לִסְחוֹרְתְּהוֹן
sources.says: Jonathan translates it as they turned to their trade.

14:19.headline: מאס and געל both mean "reject", but they are not the same
14:19.body: Malbim says מאיסה is the opposite of choosing, while גיעול is the opposite of clinging in love. One can feel גועל without rejecting, and the verse uses געלה for Zion because the Presence dwells there.

sources.quote: המאיסה היא הפך הבחירה, בחרתיך ולא מאסתיך (ישעיהו מ״א:ט׳) והגיעול נפש, הוא הפך הדיבוק והאהבה
sources.says: Malbim says מאיסה is the opposite of choosing, and גיעול is the opposite of clinging and love.

sources.quote: וע"כ על ציון ששם מקום השכינה תפס לשון געילת נפש
sources.says: Malbim says the verse uses the language of loathing for Zion because it is the place of the Presence.

14:20.headline: Three words for wrongdoing: רשענו, עון, חטאנו
14:20.body: Radak says each word covers a different kind of wrong. רשענו is rebellions, עון is deliberate sins, and חטאנו is accidental ones.

sources.quote: וזכר בפסוק המרדים והוא שאמר רשענו וזכר הזדונות והוא שאמר עון וזכר גם כן השגגות והוא שאמר כי חטאנו לך
sources.says: Radak says רשענו is rebellions, עון is deliberate sins, and חטאנו is accidental ones.

sources.quote: והחטא הוא השוגג
sources.says: Malbim also says חטא is the unintended sin.

14:21.headline: כסא כבודך: the Temple, Jerusalem, or Israel carved on the throne
14:21.body: Rashi says the throne of glory is the Temple, and a midrash says it is Israel, who are engraved on that throne. Radak says it is Jerusalem.

sources.quote: בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ (פסחים ה.), וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה (תנחומא, במדבר כב): יִשְׂרָאֵל הַחֲקוּקִים בְּכִסֵּא כְבוֹדֶךָ
sources.says: Rashi says the throne of glory is the Temple, and quotes a midrash that it is Israel, engraved on the throne of glory.

sources.quote: כי כסא כבודך הוא ירושלם
sources.says: Radak says the throne of glory is Jerusalem.

15:4.headline: Punished for Manasseh, or for not repenting as he did?
15:4.body: The verse says the people will suffer בגלל מנשה, because of King Manasseh. Radak says Manasseh led Judah into evil, and Metzudat David says they held on to his deeds. The Targum reads it another way: because they did not repent as Manasseh did.

sources.quote: עַל דְלָא תָבוּ כִּמְנַשֶׁה בַר יְחִזְקִיָה
sources.says: The Targum says 'because they did not repent like Manasseh son of Hezekiah'.

sources.quote: כי הוא הנהיג את יהודה במעשים רעים
sources.says: Radak says Manasseh led Judah in evil deeds.

sources.quote: בעבור שאחזו במעשה מנשה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is because they held on to Manasseh's deeds.

15:5.headline: Who will come to comfort you? The mourners' gesture
15:5.body: ינוד is what people do for a mourner. Rashi says it means to lament. Metzudat David says comforters nod their heads at the mourner. Radak says the word fits because comforters leave their homes and come from all sides.

sources.quote: יָנוּד. יְקוֹנֵן
sources.says: Rashi says ינוד means to lament.

sources.quote: ואין מי ינודד בראש עליך כדרך המנחמים
sources.says: Metzudat David says no one will shake his head over you, as comforters do.

sources.quote: לפי שהמנחמים נדין ממקומן זה מפה וזה מפה לנחם האבל
sources.says: Radak says the word is used because comforters move from their places, from here and there, to comfort the mourner.

15:7.headline: Scattered like grain tossed from a winnowing fork
15:7.body: A מזרה is the tool used to toss grain into the wind. Rashi says God scatters the people this way so they do not all go into exile in one place. Malbim says the chaff blown away stands for those sent into exile.

sources.quote: שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ כֻּלָּן גּוֹלִין לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד
sources.says: Rashi says it is so they will not all be exiled to one place.

sources.quote: הוא הכלי שזורין בו התבואה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the tool used to winnow grain.

sources.quote: כן הלכו הפסולת לגולה
sources.says: Malbim says, like chaff, the worthless went into exile.

15:8.headline: Not 'city' but 'enemy'? Three readings of עיר
15:8.body: God says He brought עיר on her suddenly. Rashi reads it as the troops of a city, and adds that some read it as 'enemy', as in 1 Samuel 28:16. Metzudat Zion reads 'enemy'. Malbim reads it from ערוה, exposure: she was put to shame.

sources.quote: הִשְׁכַּנְתִּי עֲלֵיהֶם פִּתְאֹם גְּיָסוֹת שֶׁל עִיר
sources.says: Rashi says God suddenly settled the troops of a city upon them.

sources.quote: וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִים עִיר – לְשׁוֹן שׂוֹנֵא
sources.says: Rashi says some explain עיר as 'enemy'.

sources.quote: עיר. ענין שונא כמו ויהי ערך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means enemy, as in 1 Samuel 28:16.

sources.quote: ולדעתי מענין גילוי ערוה
sources.says: Malbim says in his view it comes from exposing nakedness.

15:9.headline: Shame so deep you want to bury your face
15:9.body: בושה וחפרה are two words for shame. Malbim says חפר is the stronger one: a person digs (חפר) a hole to hide his face. Rashi says it means shame, and Radak says the two words repeat one idea.

sources.quote: חפר גדול מן בושה שחופר פנים בטמון
sources.says: Malbim says חפר is greater than בושה: one digs to hide his face.

sources.quote: וְחָפֵרָה. לְשׁוֹן בּוֹשֶׁת
sources.says: Rashi says it means shame.

sources.quote: בושה וחפרה. כפל ענין במלות שונות
sources.says: Radak says the two words repeat the same idea.

15:10.headline: One word that both curses and shames
15:10.body: Jeremiah says everyone מקללוני. Radak says the word is built from two roots at once: קלל, to curse, and קלה, to disgrace. The prophet packs two ideas into one word to keep it short and elegant. Malbim and Metzudat Zion agree.

sources.quote: הורכבה המלה משני שרשים מן קלל ומן קלה
sources.says: Radak says the word is built from two roots, קלל and קלה.

sources.quote: ואמר במלה אחת שני ענינים לקצר הלשון ולצחותו
sources.says: Radak says the prophet said two things in one word to keep the language short and elegant.

sources.quote: מורכב מן קללה ומן קלון
sources.says: Malbim says it is made of קללה, curse, and קלון, disgrace.

sources.quote: הוא מלשון קללה ומלשון קלון ובזיון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from cursing and from disgrace.

15:15.headline: Do not take me: hurry my justice, or keep me alive
15:15.body: Jeremiah asks, אל לארך אפך תקחני. Rashi and the Targum read it: do not put off my cause through Your patience, but avenge me quickly. Radak reads it: even if You are patient with them, do not take my life before I see Your justice.

sources.quote: אַל תִּקַּח אֶת רִיבִי לְהַנִּיחוֹ לְאֹרֶךְ אַפְּךָ, אֶלָּא מַהֵר וְהִנָּקֶם לִי
sources.says: Rashi says it means do not take my cause and leave it to Your patience, but hurry and avenge me.

sources.quote: לָא תִתֵּן אַרְכָּא לְעוּלְבָּנִי
sources.says: The Targum says 'do not give extra time to those who shame me'.

sources.quote: אם תאריך אפך עליהם אל תקחני כלומר אל תמיתני כדי שאראה נקמתך מהם
sources.says: Radak says: if You are patient with them, do not take me, that is, do not let me die, so I may see Your justice on them.

15:19.headline: Precious from worthless: a glutton, or something cheap
15:19.body: God tells Jeremiah to bring out יקר מזולל, the precious from the זולל. Metzudat Zion reads זולל as a glutton, as in 'a glutton and a drunkard' (Deuteronomy 21:20). Malbim says it also means despised, the opposite of יקר. Rashi says it means turning a wicked man into a worthy one.

sources.quote: ענין הרבות האכילה ורדיפת התאוות וכן זולל וסובא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means overeating and chasing desires, as in 'a glutton and a drunkard'.

sources.quote: משתתף עם כל מכבדיה הזילוה, שזה הפך יקר, ועם זולל וסובא
sources.says: Malbim says it shares a root with 'they despised her', the opposite of precious, and with 'glutton'.

sources.quote: אִם תּוֹצִיא אָדָם הָגוּן מֵאָדָם רָשָׁע
sources.says: Rashi says it means bringing out a worthy person from a wicked one.

15:19.headline: 'You will be as My mouth': the prophet's word will stand
15:19.body: God tells Jeremiah כפי תהיה, 'you will be like My mouth'. Rashi says: I make a decree and you can cancel it. Radak says whatever Jeremiah decrees will stand as if God said it. Radak adds that some read it as 'as I told you'.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֲנִי גּוֹזֵר גְּזֵירָה וְאַתָּה מְבַטְּלָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says: I make a decree and you cancel it.

sources.quote: כפי תהיה מה שתגזר ותאמר יתקיים כאילו אני אומר אותו
sources.says: Radak says whatever you decree and say will stand as if God said it.

sources.quote: ויש מפרשים כפי תהיה כמאמרי תהיה כמו שאמרתי לך
sources.says: Radak says some explain it as 'it will be as I said to you'.

16:5.headline: 'Do not nod to them': the comforter's shake of the head
16:5.body: The verb means to move or sway. Metzudat David says comforters would shake their heads at mourners. Rashi says it means to lament.

sources.quote: דרך המנחמים לנודד בראש
sources.says: Metzudat David says comforters would shake their heads.

sources.quote: תָּנֹד. תְּקוֹנֵן
sources.says: Rashi says it means to lament.

16:7.headline: Breaking bread for mourners, or spreading hands in grief?
16:7.body: Rashi says יפרסו means breaking bread: people fed mourners their first meal and said the blessing over bread for them. Radak says it may mean spreading the hands in grief, as in 'Zion spreads out her hands'.

sources.quote: שֶׁמַּבְרִין אֶת הָאֲבֵלִים בָּרְחָבָה וּפוֹרְסִין לָהֶם בִּרְכַּת הַמּוֹצִיא
sources.says: Rashi says it means breaking bread, since people fed mourners and said the blessing over bread for them.

sources.quote: וענינו כמו פרשה ציון בידיה פרישת הידים באבל
sources.says: Radak says it means spreading the hands in mourning, and brings his father's view that it means breaking bread.

16:12.headline: Following what the heart 'sees': a word read as looking
16:12.body: Metzudat Zion links שררות to seeing and gazing. Each man follows what his bad heart shows him and wants. The Targum renders it 'the thoughts of his heart'.

sources.quote: שרירות. ענין ראיה והבטה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means seeing and looking.

sources.quote: אחר מה שלבו הרע מראה לו ומתאוה לה
sources.says: Metzudat David says each one follows what his evil heart shows him and craves.

sources.quote: בָּתַר הִרְהוּר לִבֵּיהּ בִּישָׁא
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'after the thoughts of his evil heart'.

16:14.headline: 'Therefore' read as an oath to bring them home
16:14.body: לכן usually means therefore. Rashi reads it here as an oath: even though you betrayed me, I have sworn to redeem you.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן שְׁבוּעָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבְּגַדְתֶּם בִּי, שְׁבוּעָה הִיא בְּיָדִי שֶׁאֶגְאוֹל אֶתְכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the word is an oath: though you betrayed me, I have sworn to redeem you.

16:14.headline: Will people stop recalling the Exodus? The sages disagree
16:14.body: The verse says people will no longer swear by the God who brought Israel out of Egypt. Rashi cites the sages: the Exodus is not erased, it becomes second to the final redemption. Radak notes that some sages said it would not be recalled at all.

sources.quote: לֹא שֶׁתֵּעָקֵר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם מִמְּקוֹמָהּ, אֶלָּא גְּאֻלָּה אַחֲרוֹנָה עִקָּר וִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם טָפֵל לָהּ
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages: the Exodus is not uprooted, but the final redemption becomes the main thing and the Exodus secondary.

sources.quote: יש אומרים שלא יזכרו יציאת מצרים כל עיקר ויש אומרים שיזכרו אלא שיהא שעבוד מלכיות עיקר
sources.says: Radak says the sages disagree: some say the Exodus will not be mentioned at all, others that it will be mentioned but as secondary.

16:17.headline: Fully hidden versus tucked out of sight
16:17.body: The verse uses two words for hiding. Malbim says נסתר is fully hidden. נצפן is right in front of you but off to the side, where the eye does not catch it.

sources.quote: והצפון אינו נסתר רק שעומד מן הצד שאין העין רואהו
sources.says: Malbim says what is tzafun is not fully hidden, only standing to the side where the eye does not see it.

17:1.headline: A 'fingernail' used as a pen
17:1.body: צפרן is a fingernail, but here it is a writing tool. Metzudat Zion says people cut with their nails, so a cutting pen is called a nail, and Radak cites a midrash about a nail of iron used to carve.

sources.quote: ולפי שדרך האדם לחתוך בצפרניו קרא לעט בלשון צפורן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says that since people cut with their fingernails, the verse calls the pen a nail.

sources.quote: וכן הוא אומר במדרש נטל צפורן של ברזל וחקק בו
sources.says: Radak says the nail stands for a carving tool, and cites a midrash that speaks of taking an iron nail and carving with it.

17:2.headline: They long for their altars like parents miss their children
17:2.body: כזכר בניהם can mean "as they remember their children": Rashi says they missed their altars the way a parent longs for a son. Radak notes another reading, that זכר means an offering, so the verse speaks of children burned to idols, but he prefers the first.

sources.quote: כְּאָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ גַּעְגּוּעִין עַל בְּנוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says they remembered their altars like a person who longs for his son.

sources.quote: ויש מפרשים כזכר ענין הקטרה כמו אזכרתה לה' כלומר שהיו מעבירים בניהם באש והראשון נכון
sources.says: Radak says some read זכר as an offering, meaning they passed their children through fire, but the first reading is correct.

17:3.headline: 'My mountain' or 'you mountain-dwellers'?
17:3.body: הררי could be "my mountain" or a word for mountain people. Malbim reads "My mountain," Mount Zion standing in a ruined field, while Rashi reads "mountain-dwellers," the way ערבי means one who lives in the desert plain.

sources.quote: ולכן את הר שלי העומד בשדה, הוא הר ציון
sources.says: Malbim says it means My mountain standing in the field, Mount Zion.

sources.quote: כָּל סְבִיב הָעִיר מִישׁוֹר, שָׂדֶה. וְלָשׁוֹן הֲרָרִי
sources.says: Rashi says Jerusalem sits on a mountain with flat land around it, and הררי is formed like ערבי, a person who lives in the plain.

sources.quote: לפי שהיו עובדים על ההרים קרא ישראל הררי
sources.says: Radak says Israel is called by the word for mountains because they worshipped idols on the mountains.

17:4.headline: You never let the land rest, so now it will rest without you
17:4.body: ושמטתה uses the word of the שמיטה, the seventh year when fields must lie fallow. The commentators say Judah ignored that law, so the land will now get its rest by force while the people are in exile.

sources.quote: עַל כָּרְחֲךָ תִּשְׁמַט אַרְצְךָ אֶת אֲשֶׁר לֹא שָׁבְתָה בְּשַׁבְּתוֹתֵיכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says your land will rest against your will, making up for the rest years you did not keep.

sources.quote: שתשמט מנחלתך לפי שלא שמטת אותה בהיותך בה
sources.says: Radak says you will be released from your land because you did not release it while you lived there.

sources.quote: וזה בגמול שלא שמטו בשביעית
sources.says: Metzudat David says this is the payback for not letting the land rest in the seventh year.

17:4.headline: A fire lit in God's nose
17:4.body: אף means nose, and also anger, which flares in the nostrils. Rashi reads "you lit a fire in My nostrils," and Maimonides lists this verse among the places where the prophets speak of God's senses as a figure of speech.

sources.quote: יְקַדְתֶּם בִּנְחִירַי
sources.says: Rashi explains it as "you have kindled in My nostrils."

sources.quote: אברי החישה המיוחסים לו
sources.says: Maimonides lists "you have kindled a fire in My nose" among the sense organs the prophets attribute to God.

17:5.headline: Trusting in man: farming through the seventh year
17:5.body: Rashi ties this curse to the verse before: the man who trusts in people is the farmer who sows in the seventh year, sure his own work will feed him. His heart turns from God, who had promised a blessing to carry him through that year.

sources.quote: בַּחֲרִישׁוֹ וּקְצִירוֹ, לוֹמַר: אֶזְרַע בַּשְּׁבִיעִית וְאֹכַל
sources.says: Rashi says he trusts in his own ploughing and harvest, saying I will sow in the seventh year and eat.

sources.quote: שֶׁהִבְטִיחוֹ: ״וְצִוִּיתִי אֶת בִּרְכָתִי לָכֶם״
sources.says: Rashi says his heart turns from God, who had promised to command His blessing for them.

sources.quote: כי אם לא יסור לבו מה' אינו רע אם יבטח באדם שיעזרהו
sources.says: Radak adds that relying on a person for help is not wrong, as long as the heart does not turn from God.

17:6.headline: A lonely tree, or a thorny desert plant?
17:6.body: ערער appears only here and in Jeremiah 48. Rashi reads it as a lone tree, from ערירי, childless, while Radak cites Rav Hai Gaon that it is a plant thorny outside with edible fruit inside.

sources.quote: כְּעֵץ יְחִידִי; לְשׁוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it is like a lone tree, from the word for childless, and also brings Menachem's view that it is the name of a kind of forest tree.

sources.quote: מענין ערירי, אילן העומד ערירי ובלתי מוליד
sources.says: Malbim says it comes from the word for childless: a tree standing alone that bears no young.

sources.quote: ופירש רב האי ז"ל עכבית הוא קוץ מבחוץ ומבפנים פרי נאכל ונקרא ערער
sources.says: Radak cites Rav Hai Gaon that the plant in the Targum is thorny outside with edible fruit inside, and is called ערער.

17:8.headline: A stream named for what it makes grow
17:8.body: יובל here is a stream. Malbim suggests it is water that makes plants yield, and links it to יבול, produce.

sources.quote: וי"ל שפי' מים המוכנים להפריא הצמחים ולתת יבולם, ומשתתף עם יבול
sources.says: Malbim suggests it means water ready to make plants fruitful and give their yield, and that it shares a root with יבול.

sources.quote: פלגי מים כמו על יבלי מים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means streams of water.

17:9.headline: The heart is crooked, with the root of Jacob's name
17:9.body: עקב here means crooked and deceitful. Radak and Ibn Ezra hear the same root in the name Yaakov, where Esau said his brother had cheated him.

sources.quote: כי הלב עקוב יותר מכל דבר כלומר מרמה
sources.says: Radak says the heart is more crooked than anything, meaning deceitful.

sources.quote: כִּי יַעֲקֹב יֵשׁ בּוֹ שְׁנֵי עִנְיָנִים: מִן עָקֵב וּמִרְמָה
sources.says: Radak says the name Yaakov holds two meanings, heel and deceit, and cites this verse for deceit.

sources.quote: והעקוב הפך המישור
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Esau's word may come from this verse's word, and that crooked is the opposite of straight.

17:9.headline: The heart is sick, and the word for human means frail
17:9.body: אנש here means gravely ill, and Rashi reads it that way. Metzudat Zion notes that אנוש, a human being, comes from this same word for weakness, and Malbim reads it as the human heart, always ready to turn.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן חֹלִי, וְחָלְיוֹ הוּא זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word for sickness.

sources.quote: הוא שם משמות האדם ויורה על חולשו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says אנוש is one of the names for a person and points to human weakness, citing this verse.

sources.quote: והלב עצמו לב אנושי המוכן להתהפך בכל רגע ורגע
sources.says: Malbim reads it as a human heart, ready to change from moment to moment.

17:11.headline: The 'caller' bird that raises chicks that are not its own
17:11.body: קרא, "caller," is a bird that sits on another bird's eggs and calls the chicks after it. When they grow they leave it, and so, says the verse, wealth gained unjustly leaves its owner.

sources.quote: הַקּוֹרֵא הַזֶּה מוֹשֵׁךְ אַחֲרָיו אֶפְרוֹחִים שֶׁלֹּא יָלָד
sources.says: Rashi says this bird draws after it chicks it did not hatch, and once grown they do not follow it.

sources.quote: והוא רובץ על ביצי עוף אחר ומחמם אותם
sources.says: Radak says the bird sits on another bird's eggs and warms them, but the chicks abandon it.

sources.quote: עוֹף שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ קוֹרֵא
sources.says: Rashi says it is a bird whose name is קורא, which chases after other birds' nests and sits on their eggs.

17:12.headline: Why the Temple is called God's throne
17:12.body: כסא is a seat, a throne. Maimonides says the Temple is called God's throne because, like a king's throne, it shows the greatness of the One who appeared there, and Rashi says the heavenly throne lines up with the Temple.

sources.quote: כיוון שהוא מורה על גדולתו של מי שהתגלה בו והשרה עליו את אורו ואת כבודו
sources.says: Maimonides says the Temple is called a throne because it points to the greatness of the One who revealed Himself there and rested His light and glory on it.

sources.quote: וּמְכֻוָּן כְּנֶגֶד מִקְדָּשֵׁנוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the throne of glory has stood since creation and lines up with our Temple.

17:13.headline: God is Israel's hope, or Israel's pool of purity
17:13.body: מקוה can mean hope, and it can mean a pool of water. Radak and the Targum read "hope of Israel," and Radak notes others who read "Israel's pool of purity," though he prefers hope.

sources.quote: מקוה ענין תקוה וכן תרגם יונתן סבור ישראל ויש מפרשין כמו מקוה מים כלומר שאתה מקוה טהרה לישראל והראשון נכון
sources.says: Radak says מקוה means hope, as the Targum has it, while some read it as a pool of water, a pool of purity for Israel; he holds the first is right.

sources.quote: סִבּוּר יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: The Targum renders it "the hope of Israel."

17:16.headline: 'I did not hurry,' or 'I did not hold back'?
17:16.body: אצתי usually means "I hurried." Rashi reads: I did not hurry You to bring the disaster, but he notes that the Targum takes the opposite sense: I did not hold back from bringing them Your message.

sources.quote: לֹא מִהַרְתִּי לְזָרֶזְךָ לַהֲבִיאָם
sources.says: Rashi says Jeremiah did not press God to bring the punishment, and instead pleaded for mercy on them.

sources.quote: וּלְפִי הַתַּרְגּוּם יִהְיֶה אַצְתִּי – לְשׁוֹן עִכּוּב
sources.says: Rashi says that by the Targum, the word means holding back: Jeremiah did not hold back from delivering God's message.

sources.quote: וַאֲנָא לָא עַכְּבֵית עַל מֵימְרָךְ
sources.says: The Targum says "I did not hold back from Your word."

17:22.headline: 'Out of your houses' means out past the city gates
17:22.body: The verse forbids carrying out of your houses on Shabbat. Radak says this means out past the city gates, because Jerusalem's gates were locked at night, so inside the walls was not counted as public ground.

sources.quote: ומה שאמר ולא תוציאו משא מבתיכם ביום השבת ר"ל חוץ לעיר
sources.says: Radak says "do not carry out of your houses" means carrying outside the city.

sources.quote: כי ירושלם דלתותיה נעולות בלילה ואין חייבין עליה משום רשות הרבים
sources.says: Radak explains that Jerusalem's doors were locked at night, so carrying within it did not break the rule about public ground.

sources.quote: וי"ל שהזהיר גם על הכרמלית ששלמה גזר עירובין
sources.says: Malbim cites Radak, then suggests the warning may also cover in-between areas, under the carrying rules the sages say Solomon enacted.

18:3.headline: "On the stones" means on the potter's special work-tool
18:3.body: The word אבנים means a pair of stones, but here the commentators say it is the potter's own tool. Metzudat Zion compares the stones used at a birth in Exodus. Rashi and Radak cite the Aramaic translation, which says סדנא.

sources.quote: ״עַל סַדְנָא״ (תרגום יונתן)
sources.says: Rashi says Targum Jonathan renders "on the stones" as "on a sadna".

sources.quote: וְהָא הוּא עָבִיד עֱבִידְתָּא עַל סְדָנָא
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders the verse as "and behold he was doing work on a sedana".

sources.quote: האבנים. כן שם הכלי המיוחד ליוצר חרס לעשות עליו מלאכתו ודומה לו וראיתן על האבנים (שמות א׳:ט״ז) שהוא המיוחד אל היולדת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says האבנים is the name of the tool special to the potter for doing his work on, and it is like "and you see them on the stones" in Exodus, which is special to a woman giving birth.

sources.quote: האבנים. כלי היוצר שעושה עליו הכלים מחומר אשר בידו ויונתן תרגם סדנא
sources.says: Radak says האבנים is the potter's tool on which he makes vessels from the clay in his hand, and that Jonathan translated it sadna.

18:4.headline: A different vessel, or the same one made right?
18:4.body: The potter makes "another vessel" from the spoiled clay. Metzudat David and Radak say it differs from the first. Malbim says it is another vessel but not a different design: it is what the potter first meant to make.

sources.quote: וחזר היוצר ועשה מהחומר ההוא כלי אחר משונה מן הראשון כפי אשר ישר בעיניו
sources.says: Metzudat David says the potter went back and made from that clay another vessel, different from the first, as seemed right to him.

sources.quote: כלי זה ואחר כך כלי אחר חדש שלא ידמה לראשון
sources.says: Radak says the potter makes this vessel and then another, new vessel that does not resemble the first.

sources.quote: כי עשה מן החומר כלי אחר ולא בצורה אחרת רק כאשר ישר בעיני היוצר לעשות בתחלה
sources.says: Malbim says he made another vessel from the clay, not in another shape, but as the potter had first meant to make it.

18:8.headline: "I thought" for evil, "I said" for good: why the difference?
18:8.body: When God relents about a punishment, the verse says "I thought". About a blessing, it says "I said". Radak notes this hint. Malbim says God drops even the thought of harm, but of the good only what He said, since the plan to do good remains.

sources.quote: ויש רמז בענין הזה כי ברעה אמר חשבתי ובטובה אמר אמרתי
sources.says: Radak says there is a hint here, that about the evil it says "I thought" and about the good it says "I said".

sources.quote: כי בענין הרע מתנחם גם על המחשבה בענין שהרעה תתבטל לגמרי, אבל בענין הטוב מתנחם רק מן האמירה לא מן המחשבה כי מחשבת ההטבה נשארה גם עתה
sources.says: Malbim says that about evil God relents even of the thought, so the evil is fully cancelled, but about the good He relents only of the saying and not of the thought, since the thought of doing good remains even now.

18:10.headline: Why אותו, "him", after "do good"?
18:10.body: The Hebrew says "to do good him", not "to him". Radak says the word stands for "to", as in "whom have you told words" in Job. Malbim says the odd wording hints that God relents in order to make the person himself good and bring him back.

sources.quote: להיטיב אותו. כמו להטיב לו וכן את מי הגדת מלין כמו למי
sources.says: Radak says "lehetiv oto" is like "lehetiv lo", and so "et mi higgadta milin" is like "lemi".

sources.quote: וזה רמז במ"ש להיטיב אותו שהיל"ל להיטיב לו, שר"ל בכונת הנמשל שמתנחם על הטובה ותכלית ההתנחמות הוא כדי להיטיב את האיש ולהחזירו למוטב
sources.says: Malbim says the wording "to do good him", where it should say "to him", hints that God relents of the good so as to make the man himself good and bring him back.

18:11.headline: The word "potter" is reused: God "forms" evil against them
18:11.body: The verse says "I am a yotzer against you with evil", using the potter's own word. Radak says God uses it because He just spoke of the potter, who makes one vessel and then a new one, so He will form new evil after evil. Metzudat Zion says it means creating or renewing.

sources.quote: מחדש ואמר בזה הלשון לפי שזכר בפרשת יוצר כלי חרש שהוא מחדש הכלים ועושה כלי זה ואחר כך כלי אחר חדש שלא ידמה לראשון כן אחדש עליכם רעה אחר רעה
sources.says: Radak says it means renewing, and that the verse uses this word because it spoke of the potter, who renews vessels, making this one and then another new one unlike the first, so God will renew evil upon them, evil after evil.

sources.quote: יוצר. בורא ומחדש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says יוצר means one who creates and renews.

sources.quote: הנני יוצר עליכם רעה, ה' מכין עליכם גזרה רעה
sources.says: Malbim says "I am forming evil against you" means God is preparing an evil decree against them.

18:11.headline: "Your ways and your deeds" name two different things
18:11.body: Malbim says דרכים are habits and traits of the soul, and מעללים are the actions that grow out of them. So the call to repent covers both thought and action.

sources.quote: הדרכים הם המנהגים ודרכי הנפש, והמעללים הם הפעולות הצומחות מתכונות הנפש
sources.says: Malbim says "the ways" are the habits and ways of the soul, and "the deeds" are the actions that grow from the traits of the soul.

sources.quote: והיטיבו דרכיכם הם דרכי הנפש והמדות, ומעלליכם הם הפעולות היוצאות ע"י הדרכים, ר"ל תטיבו המחשבה והמעשה
sources.says: Malbim says "improve your ways" means the ways of the soul and its traits, and "your deeds" are the actions that come out through those ways, meaning improve thought and action.

sources.quote: מעלליכם. מעשיכם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says מעלליכם means your deeds.

18:12.headline: "Stubbornness" is tied to what the heart "sees"
18:12.body: Metzudat Zion says שרירות comes from the sense of looking. Metzudat David reads it as each person doing what his evil heart shows him and craves. The Aramaic translation renders it the "thought of his evil heart".

sources.quote: שרירות. ענין ראיה והבטה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says שרירות has the sense of seeing and looking.

sources.quote: נעשה כל איש כפי מה שמראה לו לבו הרע ומתאוה לה
sources.says: Metzudat David says each man will do as his evil heart shows him and he desires.

sources.quote: וּגְבַר הִרְהוּר לִבֵּיהּ בִּישָׁא נַעְבֵּיד
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "and each man, the thought of his evil heart, we will do".

18:14.headline: "Zarim" waters: foreign, rushing, or loathsome?
18:14.body: Rashi gives two readings: rushing waters, from zerem, or loathsome waters, from the word for strange things. He also cites "I dug and drank strange waters" in Kings. Metzudat Zion and Radak say "foreign": waters that come from far away. Malbim reads it as rushing water.

sources.quote: (זָרִים לְלָשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן הוּא לְשׁוֹן זֶרֶם; לְלָשׁוֹן שֵׁנִי הוּא לָשׁוֹן זָרוֹת, כְּלוֹמַר מַיִם מְאוּסִים)
sources.says: Rashi says that on the first reading זרים is from zerem, and on the second from the word for strange things, meaning loathsome waters.

sources.quote: זָרִים הֵם נוֹבְעִים, וְזֶה יוֹכִיחַ: ״אֲנִי קַרְתִּי וְשָׁתִיתִי מַיִם זָרִים״ (מלכים ב יט:כד)
sources.says: Rashi says they well up strangely, and as proof cites "I dug and drank strange waters" in Second Kings.

sources.quote: זרים. מל׳ זר ונכרי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says זרים is from the word for strange and foreign.

sources.quote: וקראם זרים לפי שהם באים ממקום זר ורחוק
sources.says: Radak says he called them strange because they come from a strange and far place.

sources.quote: זרים.  כמו זרם, כמ"ש (ישעיה א'), מים של זרם שוטף
sources.says: Malbim says זרים is like zerem, rushing water.

18:14.headline: "Uproot" here means "abandon": a tav for a tet
18:14.body: נתש usually means to uproot. Metzudat Zion and Radak say ינתשו is the same as ינטשו, with a tav for a tet, meaning to abandon. Radak says the two letters come from the same place in the mouth.

sources.quote: ינתשו. כמו ינטשו בטי״ת כי דטלנ״ת מתחלף כמו שיבואו בענין אחד טעה ותעה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ינתשו is like ינטשו with a tet, since the letters dalet, tet, lamed, nun and tav interchange, as in "ta'ah" and "ta'ah".

sources.quote: ינתשו. בתי"ו כמו בטי"ת שהיא נטישה ועזיבה כי הטי"ת והתי"ו ממוצא אחד ויבאו בענין אחד כמו טעה ותעה
sources.says: Radak says ינתשו is with a tav like with a tet, meaning leaving and abandoning, since tet and tav come from one place and are used in one sense, like "ta'ah" and "ta'ah".

18:15.headline: Three words for "path": the same, or different?
18:15.body: Metzudat Zion says שבילי and נתיבות mean the same: a way or track. Malbim says they differ: a derech is a public road, a nativ is for one person, and a shevil is the spot where one foot falls, smaller than a nativ.

sources.quote: שבילי. נתיבות עניינם אחד ענין אורח ומעגל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says "shevilei" and "nativot" have one meaning, a way and a track.

sources.quote: דרך הוא הדרך הרבים והנתיב הוא ליחיד. ושביל הונח על מקום הנחת פרסת רגל היחיד והוא קטן מנתיב
sources.says: Malbim says a derech is the public road and a nativ is for the individual, and a shevil is named for the place where one person's foot rests and is smaller than a nativ.

18:15.headline: Who made them stumble? The subject is missing
18:15.body: The verse says "and [they] made them stumble" without saying who. Radak says a word is left out, like "the informer" in "and [the informer] told Jacob". He says the ones who make them stumble are the false prophets.

sources.quote: כי שכחוני, ויכשילום. חסר המכשילים וכן ויגד ליעקב ויגד המגיד והמכשילים הם נביאי השקר
sources.says: Radak says "those who cause stumbling" is missing, as in "and it was told to Jacob" meaning the informer told, and that those who cause stumbling are the false prophets.

18:17.headline: "I will see them": God shows them His back, not His face
18:17.body: The verse says "I will see them" on the day of their disaster. Rashi says it means "and I will not save them". Radak says it is measure for measure: they turned their back to God, so He turns His back to them, hiding His face.

sources.quote: אֶרְאֵם. וְלֹא אוֹשִׁיעֵם
sources.says: Rashi says "ereem" means "and I will not save them".

sources.quote: מדה כנגד מדה כמו שהם פנו אלי ערף ולא פנים כן אפנה להם ערף ולא פנים אראם
sources.says: Radak says it is measure for measure: as they turned to me the back and not the face, so I will turn to them the back and not the face, and I will show them.

sources.quote: ביום בא אידם אסתיר פני מהם ואראה להם העורף
sources.says: Metzudat David says that on the day their disaster comes I will hide my face from them and show them the back.

18:21.headline: "Pour them out" by the sword: the word means flowing
18:21.body: והגרם comes from the sense of flowing or pouring. Rashi compares "my eye flows" in Lamentations and "like waters poured down" in Micah. Radak says it speaks of the sword because of the blood that flows.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן ״עֵינִי נִגְּרָה״ (איכה ג:מט), ״כַּמַּיִם הַמּוּגָרִים״ (מיכה א:ד)
sources.says: Rashi says it is the language of "my eye flows" in Lamentations and "like waters poured down" in Micah.

sources.quote: והגירם. ענין הזלה ושפיכה וכן יגירהו על ידי חרב (תהילים ס״ג:י״א)
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says והגירם means flowing and pouring, as in "they pour him out by the hands of the sword" in Psalms.

sources.quote: נאמר לשון הגרה בחרב מפני הדם הנגר וכן יגרהו על ידי חרב
sources.says: Radak says the word for pouring is used with the sword because of the blood that flows, as in "they pour him out by the sword".

18:21.headline: "Slain by death": killed by the Angel of Death, or by plague?
18:21.body: Rashi says the husbands will be killed by the Angel of Death. Radak says they will die of plague. Malbim says the word "killed" is used only for an unusual death that resembles being killed by someone.

sources.quote: וְאַנְשֵׁיהֶם. שֶׁל הָאַלְמָנוֹת, יִהְיוּ הֲרֻגֵי מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת
sources.says: Rashi says "and their men" means the widows' husbands, will be slain by the Angel of Death.

sources.quote: שיהיו הרוגי מות כלומר שימותו בדבר
sources.says: Radak says "slain by death" means they will die of plague.

sources.quote: לשון הריגה אינו בא על מיתה טבעיית רק על מיתה משונה שדומה כנהרג ע"י אחר
sources.says: Malbim says the language of "killing" does not apply to natural death, only to an unusual death that is like being killed by another.

18:22.headline: "They dug a pit": a trap, poison, or an accusation?
18:22.body: Metzudat David reads it as a pit dug to catch him, meaning plots. Radak says the pit and the traps were poison they planned to feed him. Rashi says it means they accused him of adultery with a married woman, since "a deep pit is a harlot" in Proverbs.

sources.quote: כרו שוחה. חפרו בור ללכדני ר״ל יעצו עלי רעות
sources.says: Metzudat David says "they dug a pit" means they dug a hole to trap me, meaning they plotted evil against me.

sources.quote: כי כרו שוחה. כתוב ביו"ד וקרי בוי"ו שוחה והשוחה והפחים הוא סם המות שחשבו להאכילו
sources.says: Radak says it is written with a yod and read with a vav, and that the pit and the traps are the poison they planned to feed him.

sources.quote: שֶׁחֲשָׁדוּהוּ מֵאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״כִּי שׁוּחָה עֲמֻקָּה זוֹנָה״ (משלי כג:כז)
sources.says: Rashi says it means they suspected him of adultery with a married woman, as it says "for a harlot is a deep pit".

18:23.headline: "Do not wipe out": addressed to God, or about the sin?
18:23.body: Radak and Metzudat David read תמחי as "you shall not erase", said to God, so the sin stays on record to be repaid. Rashi reads it as "let it not be erased", about the sin, which is feminine, and explains the extra yod.

sources.quote: אַל תֶּמְחִי. אַל תְּהִי מְחוּיָה. וּלְפִי שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן נְקֵבָה נָתַן בּוֹ יוֹ״ד
sources.says: Rashi says "al temchi" means "do not be wiped out", and since it is a feminine form it has a yod.

sources.quote: אל תמחי. כמו אל תמחה היו"ד במקום ה"א למ"ד הפעל כמו צור ילדך תשי
sources.says: Radak says "al timchi" is like "al timcheh", with the yod in place of the he at the end of the verb, like "the Rock who bore you you forgot".

sources.quote: אל תמחוק חטאתם מלפניך כי יהיו כתובים לזכרון למען יקבלו גמול
sources.says: Metzudat David says do not erase their sins from before you, so that they stay written as a reminder, so that they receive their repayment.

19:1.headline: The jug is named for the gurgle it makes when poured
19:1.body: Metzudat Zion says a בקבוק has a narrow mouth, and pouring from it sounds like "bak-buk". Malbim adds that honey hardens inside such a jug, so the only way to get it out is to break the jug, which is the picture Jeremiah will act out.

sources.quote: כן שם הכלי שפיה צר על כי בעת ישופך ממנה נשמע כעין קול בקבק
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says this is the name of a vessel with a narrow mouth, because when it is poured out a sound like "bakbuk" is heard.

sources.quote: הוא כלי שנותנים לתוכו דבש ופיו צר, ואחר שנקפא הדבש בתוכו א"א להוציאו רק ע"י שבירת הכלי
sources.says: Malbim says it is a narrow-mouthed vessel for honey, and once the honey hardens inside it can only be taken out by breaking the vessel.

19:2.headline: The Gate of Shards, or the Gate of the Sun
19:2.body: Rashi and Metzudat David read חרס as a broken pot shard: this is the gate where people threw their broken pottery. Radak quotes the sages, who read חרס as the sun, a gate facing the sunrise, and Malbim ties that to sun worship in this valley.

sources.quote: שַׁעַר הָאַשְׁפּוֹת (נחמיה ב:יג), שֶׁשָּׁם זוֹרְקִין חֲרָסִים הַנִּשְׁבָּרִים
sources.says: Rashi says it is the Dung Gate of Nehemiah, where people throw broken shards.

sources.quote: שער החרסית שהוא מכוון כנגד זריחת החמה היך מה דתימא האומר לחרס ולא יזרח
sources.says: Radak quotes the sages that it is called the Charsit Gate because it faces the sunrise, as in the verse "who commands the sun (חרס) and it does not rise".

sources.quote: אשר פתח שער החרסית שער המזרח, כי עבודת המולך היה מיוחדת לשמש כנודע
sources.says: Malbim says the Charsit Gate is the east gate, because the worship of Molech was tied to the sun.

19:3.headline: Ears that ring like cymbals at the news
19:3.body: Rashi links the word to מצלתים, cymbals, so the ears will ring. Metzudat Zion and Radak say it means to shake or quiver, as lips quiver in Habakkuk.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן ״מְצִלְתַּיִם״ (נחמיה יב:כז); ״בְּצִלְצְלֵי שָׁמַע״
sources.says: Rashi says the word comes from "cymbals" and "loud cymbals".

sources.quote: ענין תנועת הרעש וכן לקול צללו שפתי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a shaking motion, like "my lips quivered at the sound".

sources.quote: ונאמר זה הלשון באזנים ובשפתים כמו לקול צללו שפתי
sources.says: Radak says this word is used of both ears and lips, as in "my lips quivered at the sound".

19:5.headline: Never commanded, never said, never thought: the sages name three stories
19:5.body: Malbim quotes the sages, who match each phrase to a child offered up: Mesha king of Moab, Jephthah's daughter, and the binding of Isaac. The Aramaic translation reads the three phrases as not in My Torah, not through My prophets, and not My will.

sources.quote: לא צויתי למישע מלך מואב ולא דברתי ליפתח ולא עלתה על לבי זה עקדת יצחק
sources.says: Malbim quotes the sages: "I did not command" refers to Mesha king of Moab, "I did not speak" to Jephthah, and "it did not come into My heart" to the binding of Isaac.

sources.quote: דְלָא פַקְדֵית בְּאוֹרַיְתִי וּדְלָא שְׁלָחֵית בְּיַד עַבְדֵי נְבִיַיָא וְלָא רַעֲוָא קָדָמָי
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "which I did not command in My Torah, and did not send by My servants the prophets, and it was not My will".

19:6.headline: Topheth is named for drums that drowned out a burning child
19:6.body: Metzudat David says the place was called Topheth from תופים, drums. They beat drums there so a father would not hear his son groan in the fire and feel pity.

sources.quote: בית הבמות קראו תופת לפי שהיו מקישים שם בתופים לבל ישמע האב בנהימת הבן כשהוא נשרף ויכמרו רחמיו
sources.says: Metzudat David says the altar site was called Topheth because they beat drums there, so the father would not hear his burning son's groans and feel pity.

19:6.headline: Ben Hinnom read as the groan of the son
19:6.body: Metzudat David reads בן הנם as "the son's groan", from נהימה, groaning. He says the valley got this name from the cries of the child who was burned there.

sources.quote: הגיא שעמד בו בית הבמות קראו בן הנם ע״ש נהימת הבן הנשרף
sources.says: Metzudat David says the valley holding the altars was called Ben Hinnom after the groaning of the burned son.

19:7.headline: "I will empty out" was chosen to echo the jug, בקבוק
19:7.body: The verb means to empty, and Rashi and Metzudat Zion say it was picked because it sounds like בקבוק, the jug Jeremiah is holding. Malbim says a jug is made to be emptied, and so God will empty out Judah's plans.

sources.quote: וְעַל שֵׁם בַּקְבּוּק שֶׁהוּא מְדַבֵּר בּוֹ, לָקַח לְשׁוֹנוֹ כֵּן
sources.says: Rashi says it means "I will empty", and the prophet chose this word because of the jug he is speaking about.

sources.quote: ענין ריקות כמו הבוק תבוק הארץ (ישעיהו כ״ד:ג׳) והוא לשון נופל על לשון בקבוק
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means emptiness, and it is a word that plays on the word בקבוק.

sources.quote: על זה מורה שם בקבוק שעשוי להריק הדבר מתוכו כן אריק עצת יהודה
sources.says: Malbim says the name בקבוק points to this: it is made to pour out what is inside, so God will empty out Judah's counsel.

19:9.headline: Eating a neighbor's flesh, or plundering a neighbor's goods?
19:9.body: The verse says people will eat their children and each other in the siege. The Aramaic translation keeps the children but turns "each will eat his neighbor's flesh" into "each will plunder his relative's goods".

sources.quote: וּגְבַר נִכְסֵי קָרִיבֵיהּ יִבְזוּן
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders the phrase "and a man will plunder the property of his relative".

19:11.headline: A broken pot that cannot be "healed"
19:11.body: The word is from רפואה, healing, though spelled with ה. Metzudat Zion and Radak say it is used here in a borrowed sense, to mend a broken thing, as Elijah "healed" the broken altar.

sources.quote: הוא מלשון רפואה ועם כי היא בה״א ור״ל לתקנה ואמר בל׳ שאלה וכן וירפא את מזבח ה׳
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is from the word for healing, though written with ה, and means to repair it, used as a borrowed sense, like "he repaired the altar of the Lord".

sources.quote: בה"א כמו באל"ף ובא בדרך השאלה כמו וירפא את מזבח ה' ההרוס
sources.says: Radak says the ה stands for an א, and it is a borrowed use, like "he repaired the altar of the Lord that was torn down".

19:14.headline: God sent Jeremiah "there" only, Malbim says, not to the Temple
19:14.body: Malbim reads "where God sent him there" as limiting: God sent Jeremiah to speak at Topheth. Repeating it in the Temple court was his own choice, which is why Pashhur could strike him in the next chapter.

sources.quote: ה' שלחו רק שינבא בהתופת ושם היה שלוח מה', אבל מה שהלך ונבא זאת שנית בחצר בית ה' זה עשה מדעתו
sources.says: Malbim says God sent him only to prophesy at Topheth, where he was God's messenger, but going to prophesy it again in the Temple court he did on his own.

sources.quote: רק ע"מ שדבר מעצמו בלא ציוי לא היה שליח ה' והיה יכול לשלוט בו
sources.says: Malbim says that because he spoke on his own without a command he was not God's messenger, so Pashhur could overpower him.

2:2.headline: Your bridal days: a word for bride and for perfect beauty
2:2.body: כלולות is a rare word for the time of a wedding. Rashi ties it to bringing the bride under the wedding canopy. Malbim says it joins two ideas, כלה, a bride, and כליל, perfect beauty.

sources.quote: כְּלִילַת חֻפָּתֵךְ, שֶׁהִכְלַלְתִּיךְ לְחֻפָּה
sources.says: Rashi says it means the crowning of your wedding canopy, when God brought Israel under it.

sources.quote: ענינו מענין כַלָה ומענין כליל היופי
sources.says: Malbim says the word comes from both 'bride' and 'perfect beauty', and that the two are one idea.

2:5.headline: They chased emptiness and became empty
2:5.body: The verse uses the same word twice: they went after ההבל, emptiness, and ויהבלו, they became empty. Malbim says whoever clings to something with no substance takes on its nature.

sources.quote: אבל הדבק בהבל שא"ל קיום גם הוא נעשה הבל
sources.says: Malbim says one who clings to emptiness, which does not last, becomes empty too.

sources.quote: נעשו גם המה הבל מבלי ממש
sources.says: Metzudat David says they themselves became empty, with nothing real to them.

2:13.headline: God as a spring: life that flows out without end
2:13.body: God calls Himself a spring of living water. Radak says a spring needs no outside supply and never stops. Maimonides reads the image as God's constant outflow of existence itself.

sources.quote: שלא יבאו לו המים ממקום אחר אלא ממקומו הם נובעין ועוד שאין להם הפסק
sources.says: Radak says a spring's water comes from itself, not from elsewhere, and never stops.

sources.quote: כלומר שפיעת החיים, דהיינו המציאות שהיא החיים בלי ספק
sources.says: Maimonides says the spring of living water means the flow of life from God, that is, existence itself.

2:13.headline: Not wells but cisterns, which only hold what is poured in
2:13.body: באר is a well fed by a spring. Here the word is voweled like בורות, cisterns. Malbim explains the difference: a cistern only stores collected water, so a cracked one is left dry.

sources.quote: שהבור הוא ממים מכונסים, והבאר הוא ממים נובעים
sources.says: Malbim says a cistern holds gathered water while a well holds flowing water, and that the vowel here points to cisterns.

sources.quote: הם חריצים עשוים בבנין לאסוף לתוכם מי המטר
sources.says: Radak says these are built pits for collecting rainwater.

2:20.headline: Written 'I will not serve', read 'I will not cross'
2:20.body: The word is written אעבוד, 'I will not serve', but read אעבור, 'I will not cross the line'. Radak gives both: Israel promised not to break God's word, and not to serve idols again.

sources.quote: והכתוב אעבוד לא אעבוד עוד עכו"ם
sources.says: Radak says the written form means 'I will no longer serve idols'.

sources.quote: וַתֹּאמְרִי לֹא אֶעֱבוֹר. עַל דְּבָרֶיךָ
sources.says: Rashi reads it as 'I will not cross your words'.

2:23.headline: A young she-camel that loves to roam
2:23.body: בכרה looks like the word for firstborn. Rashi says it is a young female camel, the kind that likes to keep moving. Malbim ties it to בכור: the choicest of its kind.

sources.quote: גְּמַלָּה נְקֵבָה בְּחוּרָה, שֶׁהִיא אוֹהֶבֶת לָנוּעַ
sources.says: Rashi says it is a young female camel that loves to wander.

sources.quote: בא על הנבחר במינו
sources.says: Malbim says the word means the choicest of its kind, like the firstborn.

2:24.headline: Not a cow but a wild donkey
2:24.body: פרה usually means a cow. Here it is spelled with ה but means פרא, the wild donkey of the desert, which runs where it wants.

sources.quote: כמו פרא באל״ף והוא חמור הבר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is like פרא with an aleph, the wild donkey.

sources.quote: בה"א כמו באל"ף פרא אדם
