sources.says: Radak says it is written with ה but means the same as פרא with aleph.

2:31.headline: See the word of God: you cannot see words
2:31.body: One hears a word; one does not see it. Maimonides says ראו here means grasp, as Hebrew uses one sense for another. Rashi brings the midrash that Jeremiah showed them the jar of manna, something they could see.

sources.quote: כמו "שמעו", כי המכוון הוא: הַשיגו את משמעות דבריו
sources.says: Maimonides says 'see' here means the same as 'hear': grasp the meaning of His words.

sources.quote: הוֹצִיא לָהֶם צִנְצֶנֶת הַמָּן
sources.says: Rashi says Jeremiah brought out the jar of manna and told them to look at it.

sources.quote: כי יש ראיה בלב
sources.says: Radak says there is seeing with the heart, meaning understanding.

2:31.headline: A land of deep darkness, with God's name added
2:31.body: מאפליה appears only here. Metzudat Zion says it comes from אופל, darkness, with יה added to make it stronger. Malbim brings the sages' reading: a land where crops ripen late.

sources.quote: וכשבא להגדיל הדבר סומכו למלת יה וכן שלהבת יה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is from darkness, and יה is added to make it greater, as in שלהבתיה.

sources.quote: וחז"ל (מדבר רבה פ"א) פי' מענין כי אפילות הנה
sources.says: Malbim says the sages read it from אפילות, late-ripening crops.

20:2.headline: A prison, or wooden stocks that lock the neck
20:2.body: Rashi and Metzudat David say המהפכת is the name of a prison. Radak reports his father's view: a frame of two boards with a hole that locks the prisoner's neck.

sources.quote: שֵׁם מְקוֹם הָאֲסוּרִים, וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: ״לְכִיפְתָּא״
sources.says: Rashi says it is the name of the place of prisoners, and Jonathan translated it "to the kifta".

sources.quote: המהפכת. הוא שם של בית הסוהר
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the name of the prison.

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי ז"ל פירש כלי שהוא עשוי שני עצים ועושין בנתים בית צואר ומכניסין שם צוארי האסורין
sources.says: Radak says his father explained it as a device of two pieces of wood with a neck hole between them, where prisoners' necks were put.

20:3.headline: Pashhur's name is turned into "terror all around"
20:3.body: Jeremiah says God's name for him is not Pashhur but מגור מסביב, "terror all around". Rashi hears פש חור, a great free man, in the old name, and Malbim says the new name means the opposite: shrinking in fear.

sources.quote: שֶׁלְּשׁוֹן פַּשְׁחוּר מַשְׁמַע אָדָם גָּדוֹל וּבֶן חוֹרִין, פָּשׁ חוּר
sources.says: Rashi says the name Pashhur means a great man and a free man, "pash hur".

sources.quote: דָּבָר אַחֵר: פָּשׁ סְחוֹר, רַבִּים סְבִיבוֹתֶיךָ לַהֲרֹג
sources.says: Rashi gives another reading: "pash sehor", many around you to kill.

sources.quote: כי פשחור הוא כמו פש סחור ופש הוא ענין רבוי כמו ופשו פרשיו (חבקוק א) וסחור הוא תרגומו של סביב
sources.says: Metzudat David says Pashhur is like "pash sehor": pash means many, and sehor is the Aramaic for "around".

sources.quote: ששם זה מורה על התפשטות והחירות, כי אם מגור מסביב שהוא ההפך שמתאסף אל עצמו מפני הפחד והמצור
sources.says: Malbim says the name points to spreading out and freedom, while "magor missaviv" is the opposite: drawing into oneself out of fear and siege.

20:3.headline: מגור: terror all around, or enemies gathering all around
20:3.body: Rashi first reads מגור as fear, and Radak agrees: Pashhur will never feel safe. Metzudat Zion and the Aramaic translation read it as gathering, troops massing around him.

sources.quote: מָגוֹר. יִרְאָה
sources.says: Rashi says מגור means fear.

sources.quote: לא תהיה בטוח כמו שאתה אומר אלא פחד יהיה לך מכל סביבותיך
sources.says: Radak says you will not be safe as you claim, but you will have fear from all around you.

sources.quote: ענין אסיפה וקבוץ כמו אוגר בקיץ
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means gathering and collecting, like "gathers in summer".

sources.quote: אֱלָהֵין יִתְכַּנְשׁוּן עֲלָךְ דְקָטְלִין בְּחַרְבָּא מִסְחוֹר סְחוֹר
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "but those who kill with the sword will gather against you all around".

20:5.headline: חסן means strength, so is it the city's wealth or its forts?
20:5.body: Radak says a treasure is called strength because it is what holds a person up in hard times. Malbim says here it means the strong things of the city, like its fortresses.

sources.quote: וקרא האוצר חוסן לפי שהאוצר חוזק האדם ותקפו לעת צרה
sources.says: Radak says a treasure is called חוסן because a treasure is a person's strength and power in a time of trouble.

sources.quote: ונתתי את כל חוסן הם הדברים החזקים שבעיר כמו המבצרים
sources.says: Malbim says "all the חוסן" are the strong things in the city, like the fortresses.

20:8.headline: Is Jeremiah shouting doom at them, or crying for help?
20:8.body: Rashi and the Aramaic translation say his message is always violence and ruin coming on the people. Metzudat David and Radak say he cries "violence!" about the abuse done to him.

sources.quote: וְאֵינִי קוֹרֵא אֲלֵיהֶם טוֹבָה כִּי אִם נְבוּאוֹת חָמָס וָשֹׁד
sources.says: Rashi says he calls nothing good to them, only prophecies of violence and ruin.

sources.quote: וְעַל חָטוֹפִין וּבָזוֹזִין אֲנָא מִתְנַבֵּי
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "and about robbers and plunderers I prophesy".

sources.quote: אני צועק על הרעה הנעשה לי ואקרא בקול החמס והשוד הבא לי בעבורה
sources.says: Metzudat David says he cries out about the harm done to him and calls aloud about the violence that comes to him because of his prophecy.

sources.quote: ואצטרך לקרא חמס על דבריהם הרעים שאומרים לי
sources.says: Radak says he has to cry "violence" over the cruel words they say to him.

20:10.headline: Two grammarians split: "we will report him" or "cut him down"
20:10.body: Rashi quotes Menahem, who reads the verb from a root meaning to cut or destroy. Dunash reads it plainly as "tell": they will invent a charge and report him to the king.

sources.quote: וּמְנַחֵם פֵּירֵשׁ הַגִּידוּ וְנַגִּידֶנּוּ כְּמוֹ ״לֹא תִתְגּוֹדְדוּ״
sources.says: Rashi says Menahem explained the words like "you shall not cut yourselves".

sources.quote: וְדוּנָשׁ פָּתַר אוֹתוֹ לְשׁוֹן הַגָּדָה מַמָּשׁ, וְכֹה פִּתְרוֹנוֹ: הַגִּידוּ עָלָיו דִּבְרֵי שֶׁקֶר וְנַגִּידֶנּוּ לַמֶּלֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi says Dunash read it as actual telling: tell lies about him and we will report him to the king.

sources.quote: פירוש הגידו דבר שקר עליו ונגידנו למלך
sources.says: Radak says it means tell a lie about him and we will report him to the king.

20:10.headline: Not "my side" but "my limp": friends waiting for him to stumble
20:10.body: Metzudat Zion and Malbim read צלע here as limping, from the word used for Jacob limping on his thigh. His so-called friends watch for the moment he slips.

sources.quote: ענין חגר ופסח ויאמר על המכשול והתקלה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means limping and lameness, and is said of a stumble or mishap.

sources.quote: לשון והוא צולע על יריכו
sources.says: Malbim says it is the word in "and he was limping on his thigh".

sources.quote: שׁוֹמְרֵי צַלְעִי. מְצַפִּים שִׁבְרִי
sources.says: Rashi says "watchers of my tzela" means those waiting for my downfall.

20:11.headline: "God is with me", or "God is my sign and banner"
20:11.body: Metzudat Zion reads אותי as "with me". Malbim reads it from אות, a sign: God is like a banner painted on Jeremiah's flag, a mighty warrior fighting for him.

sources.quote: אותי. עמי וכן ואדבר אותך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says אותי means "with me", as in "I will speak with you".

sources.quote: אותי.  מענין והיו לאות על ידך
sources.says: Malbim says אותי is from the sense of "and they shall be a sign on your hand".

sources.quote: ה' הוא האות והנס שלי, והוא מצוייר על דגלי כגבור עריץ הלוחם בעדי להצילני
sources.says: Malbim says God is my sign and banner, drawn on my flag as a mighty warrior fighting to save me.

20:11.headline: השכילו means "were wise", but here it means "succeeded"
20:11.body: Metzudat Zion explains why: a person who succeeds looks to others as if he acted wisely. Rashi and Radak also read it as success, as with David, who was משכיל in all his ways.

sources.quote: ענין הצלחה על כי המצליח נדמה בעיני הבריות שעושה מעשיו בהשכל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means success, because one who succeeds seems to people to act with wisdom.

sources.quote: לֹא הִצְלִיחוּ בַּעֲצָתָם
sources.says: Rashi says they did not succeed in their plan.

sources.quote: ענין הצלחה כמו ויהי דוד בכל דרכיו משכיל
sources.says: Radak says it means success, like "and David was successful in all his ways".

20:14.headline: Cursing the day he was born, or the day he was conceived?
20:14.body: Metzudat David and Malbim say "the day I was born" here is the day of conception, credited to the father, and the next phrase is the birth itself. Rashi, from the midrash, says his father fled King Manasseh, who was killing prophets, and he was conceived that day.

sources.quote: הוא יום ההריון המיוחס גם לאב
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the day of conception, which is credited to the father too.

sources.quote: ובמלת יולדתי בפועל מציין עת העבור שהולידו אביו, ועל עת הלידה אמר ילדתני אמי
sources.says: Malbim says the word יולדתי marks the time of conception, when his father begot him, while "my mother bore me" is the birth.

sources.quote: וְעַל יְדֵי אֹנֶס שִׁמֵּשׁ חִלְקִיָּהוּ אָבִיו מִטָּתוֹ בַּיּוֹם, שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹרֵחַ מִפְּנֵי מְנַשֶּׁה שֶׁהָיָה הוֹרֵג אֶת הַנְּבִיאִים
sources.says: Rashi says his father Hilkiah was forced to be with his wife by day, because he was fleeing Manasseh, who was killing the prophets.

20:15.headline: Who brought the birth news? Radak reports it was Pashhur
20:15.body: Radak asks how Jeremiah could curse a messenger who may have been a good man, and reports a tradition that it was Pashhur son of Immer. Malbim instead says King Manasseh killed the messenger.

sources.quote: ואמרו כי נודע לו כי פשחור בן אמר היה המבשר
sources.says: Radak reports it is said that Jeremiah knew the messenger was Pashhur son of Immer.

sources.quote: כי מנשה הרג אותו על שבשר את אבי
sources.says: Malbim says Manasseh killed him for bringing the news to my father.

20:17.headline: Who did not kill him in the womb? The verse never says
20:17.body: The verb has no subject, so Rashi fills in the angel of death. Radak says it may mean any person, or God, as Job says of the One who did not shut the womb.

sources.quote: אֲשֶׁר לֹא מוֹתְתַנִי מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת מֵרָחֶם. וַהֲרֵי זֶה מִן הַמִּקְרָאוֹת קִצְרֵי דִּבּוּר
sources.says: Rashi reads it "that the angel of death did not kill me in the womb", and says this is one of the verses that leaves words out.

sources.quote: אומר על איש למה לא המיתו קודם צאתו מרחם או אמר על האל כמו שאמר איוב כי לא סגר דלתי בטני
sources.says: Radak says it speaks of a man who did not kill him before he left the womb, or of God, as Job said "for He did not shut the doors of my womb".

22:3.headline: Do not wrong them with words, and do not rob them
22:3.body: The verse uses two verbs: תנו and תחמסו. Rashi says the first means hurting someone with words. Metzudat David says the second is taking their money.

sources.quote: אַל תּוֹנוּ. זוֹ אוֹנָאַת דְּבָרִים
sources.says: Rashi says 'do not wrong' means wronging with words.

sources.quote: אל תחמוסו. אל תעשו להם חמס וזהו עושק הממון
sources.says: Metzudat David says 'do not do violence' means taking their money.

22:3.headline: A word that looks like 'oppressed' but means 'oppressor'
22:3.body: עשוק appears only here. It looks like it means the one oppressed. Radak says it is shaped like 'near' or 'great' and means the oppressor. Metzudat David says it is the robber.

sources.quote: מיד עשוק. תואר בפלס קרוב גדול וענינו כמו עושק
sources.says: Radak says עשוק is a descriptive word in the pattern of קרוב and גדול, meaning the oppressor.

sources.quote: עשוק. הגזלן
sources.says: Metzudat David says עשוק is the robber.

22:6.headline: 'You are Gilead to me': head of the land, or the Temple?
22:6.body: Radak says Gilead was one town that gave its name to a whole region. So too Jerusalem is the head of all Israel. Rashi says Gilead stands for the Temple, since balm and healing come from it to the world.

sources.quote: כי גלעד עיר אחת בעבר הירדן וכל הארץ ההיא ארץ סיחון ועוג וכל הבשן היתה נקראת על שמה ארץ הגלעד כי היא ראש להם
sources.says: Radak says Gilead was one town across the Jordan, and the whole region was named for it, since it was their head.

sources.quote: גִּלְעָד אַתָּה. הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says Gilead here means the Temple.

sources.quote: שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ צֳרִי וּרְפוּאָה לְכָל הָעוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi says from it comes balm and healing for the whole world.

22:7.headline: 'Your choicest cedars': great men, or the palace's cedar roofs?
22:7.body: The king's house was just called Lebanon, so the prophet speaks of cutting its cedars. Metzudat David says this means killing the nobles and warriors. Radak says it means the cedar-panelled roofs of the houses.

sources.quote: ר״ל יהרגו השרים והגבורים ולפי שאמר ראש הלבנון אמר לשון הנופל בעצי היער
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means the officers and warriors will be killed, using forest language because he called them Lebanon.

sources.quote: ר"ל קירוי הבתים הספונים
sources.says: Radak says it means the panelled roofs of the houses.

22:10.headline: 'Do not weep for the dead': which king, and how much?
22:10.body: Rashi and Radak say the dead one is King Jehoiakim. Weep instead for the king going into exile. Radak also cites the Sages, who read it as 'do not weep too much', and set limits on mourning.

sources.quote: לִיהוֹיָקִים, שֶׁיָּמוּת לִפְנֵי הַשַּׁעַר כְּשֶׁיִּסְחָבוּהוּ לְהַגְלוֹתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means Jehoiakim, who will die by the gate when they drag him into exile.

sources.quote: ודרשו רז"ל אל תבכו למת יותר מדאי ואל תנודו לו יותר מכשיעור הא כיצד שלשה לבכי שבעה להספד שלשים לגהוץ ולתספורת
sources.says: Radak cites the Sages: do not weep for the dead too much; three days for weeping, seven for eulogy, thirty before pressing clothes and cutting hair.

22:11.headline: Who is 'Shallum'? Three kings are proposed
22:11.body: The verse names a king Shallum, son of Josiah. Rashi says it is Zedekiah, called Shallum in Chronicles. Radak thinks it is Jehoiachin. He notes Ibn Ezra thought it was Jehoahaz.

sources.quote: הוּא צִדְקִיָּהוּ, וְכָךְ נִקְרָא ״וְהָרְבִיעִי שַׁלּוּם״
sources.says: Rashi says Shallum is Zedekiah, called 'the fourth, Shallum' in Chronicles.

sources.quote: שלום הוא יהויכין ושני שמות היו לו
sources.says: Radak says Shallum is Jehoiachin, who had two names.

sources.quote: והחכם רבי אברהם בן עזרא פירש כי שלום הוא יהואחז כי במצרים מת
sources.says: Radak says Ibn Ezra explained Shallum as Jehoahaz, who died in Egypt.

22:14.headline: 'Roomy' upper rooms, or rooms open to the breeze?
22:14.body: מרוחים is a rare word. Radak says it can come from ריוח, 'space', so wide rooms. Or from רוח, 'wind': rooms built for the breeze in summer. Metzudat David reads it the second way.

sources.quote: מן ורוח לשאול ענין הרחבה ויתכן להיות מרוחים מענין רוח כלומר שיכנס בהם הרוח עשוים לימי הקיץ
sources.says: Radak says it may mean wide, or may come from wind, rooms that let the wind in, made for summer.

sources.quote: להיות ריוח גדול בין חדרי העליה שיכנס שם הרוח בימי הקיץ
sources.says: Metzudat David says there was space between the upper rooms so the wind would come in during summer.

22:15.headline: 'Your father ate and drank': a jab at a king who fasted
22:15.body: Why praise Josiah for eating and drinking? Metzudat David and Radak cite a view that Jehoiakim fasted, thinking it would pay for his evil. The prophet answers: your father ate, drank, and did justice.

sources.quote: יתכן שהיה יהויקים מסגף עצמו במאכל ומשתה ועשה הרע בחושבו שהסגוף יכפר על רעתו
sources.says: Metzudat David says Jehoiakim may have denied himself food and drink while doing evil, thinking the self-denial would atone.

sources.quote: ויש אומרים כי יהויקים היה מתענה תמיד והיה סבור כי התעניות היו תשלום מעשיו הרעים
sources.says: Radak says some hold that Jehoiakim fasted constantly and thought the fasts paid for his evil deeds.

22:16.headline: To know God is to judge the poor fairly
22:16.body: God says helping the poor is 'knowing Me'. Metzudat David explains: by doing this a person follows God's own ways, having mercy on the poor as God does.

sources.quote: הלא זהו הדעת אותי כי בזה מדבק במעשי לרחם על העניים כמוני
sources.says: Metzudat David says this is knowing Me, since by it one clings to My deeds, having mercy on the poor like Me.

sources.quote: הלא היא הדעת אותי שזה העדות שידע אותי
sources.says: Malbim says this is the proof that he knew Me.

22:17.headline: A word found only here: crushing the poor
22:17.body: מרוצה appears only here. Rashi reads it as crushing the poor, since 'oppress' and 'crush' are always paired in the Bible. Radak says oppression takes money, while crushing hurts the body.

sources.quote: רִצּוּץ דַּלִּים; וְעֹשֶׁק יוֹכִיחַ עָלָיו, כִּי עָשׁוּק וְרָצוּץ תָּמִיד סְמוּכִין בִּלְשׁוֹן מִקְרָא
sources.says: Rashi says it means crushing the poor, as 'oppression' beside it shows, since oppressed and crushed are always paired in Scripture.

sources.quote: והעשק בממון והמרוצה בגוף
sources.says: Radak says oppression is about money and מרוצה is about the body.

22:18.headline: Why mourn a king with 'alas, sister'?
22:18.body: No one will mourn Jehoiakim with 'alas, my brother' or 'alas, sister'. Radak asks why 'sister' fits a king. Either these are the usual cries for any dead man or woman, or 'sister' means Jehoiakim's wife.

sources.quote: ואיך יספדו על המלך אלא זכר לשון הספד שהקרובים סופדים על האיש הוי אחי ועל האשה הוי אחות או אמר הוי אחות על אשת יהויקים
sources.says: Radak asks how they would mourn a king this way, and says it uses the usual mourning words for a man and a woman, or 'sister' refers to Jehoiakim's wife.

22:20.headline: The Temple is called 'Lebanon' because it whitens sins
22:20.body: The Targum renders 'go up to Lebanon' as 'go up to the Temple'. Radak cites the Sages: the Temple is called לבנון, from לבן, 'white', because it whitened Israel's sins.

sources.quote: סַקִי לְבֵית מַקְדְּשָׁא וְצַוְּחִי
sources.says: Rashi gives the Targum: go up to the Temple and cry out.

sources.quote: ולמה נקרא בית המקדש לבנון שהיה מלבין עונותיהם של ישראל
sources.says: Radak cites the Sages: the Temple is called Lebanon because it whitened Israel's sins.

22:20.headline: Why would 'Bashan' mean the gates of the Temple Mount?
22:20.body: The Targum reads Bashan as the gates of the Temple Mount. Rashi admits he does not know why, and guesses doors of Bashan oak. Radak guesses Bashan was grazing land, and the Temple always had animals for offerings.

sources.quote: וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ לְפָרֵשׁ הָאֵיךְ נוֹפֵל לְשׁוֹן בָּשָׁן בְּשַׁעֲרֵי הַר הַבַּיִת, אִם לֹא בִּשְׁבִיל הַדְּלָתוֹת שֶׁעוֹשִׂין מֵאַלּוֹנֵי הַבָּשָׁן
sources.says: Rashi says he does not know how Bashan fits the Temple Mount gates, unless because of doors made from oaks of Bashan.

sources.quote: אולי כנה הר הבית בשם בשן לפי שהבשן היה מקום מרעה הבהמות ובבית המקדש גם כן היה תמיד בהמות לקרבן
sources.says: Radak suggests the Temple Mount was called Bashan because Bashan was pasture, and the Temple always had animals for offerings.

22:22.headline: Your shepherds will be 'shepherded' by the wind
22:22.body: תרעה sounds like 'will graze', echoing רעיך, 'your shepherds'. Radak reads it that way: the wind will graze on them and eat them up. Metzudat Zion reads it as 'break', as in 'you will break them with an iron rod'.

sources.quote: שהיו להם כפרנסים וכרועים אותם תרעה רוח תאכלם הרוח
sources.says: Radak says those who were their providers and shepherds, the wind will graze on them, that is, eat them up.

sources.quote: תרעה. ענין שבירה כמו תרועם בשבט ברזל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means breaking, as in 'break them with a rod of iron'.

22:23.headline: Jerusalem nesting high in cedars, like a bird
22:23.body: Rashi says Jerusalem made its nest in tall cedar towers. Malbim takes the bird image further. Mammals giving birth are tended, but no one helps a bird lay eggs. So no one showed mercy when the city's labor pains came.

sources.quote: שֶׁשַּׂמְתְּ קִנֵּךְ בְּמִגְדְּלוֹת בָּתֵּי אֲרָזִים
sources.says: Rashi says you made your nest in towers of cedar houses.

sources.quote: משא"כ העופות המטילים ביצים לא יחוננו אותם, עפ"ז ידמה במליצתו את ירושלים כעוף
sources.says: Malbim says birds that lay eggs are not tended, and so the prophet likens Jerusalem to a bird.

22:23.headline: 'What grace did you find', or 'where did you camp'?
22:23.body: Rashi reports an old dispute. Menahem read נחנת as from חניה, camping. Dunash read it as from חן, grace. Malbim reads it as mercy: what mercy were you shown in your labor pains?

sources.quote: וּמְנַחֵם פָּתַר נֵּחַנְתְּ לְשׁוֹן חֲנִיָּה; אֲבָל דּוּנַשׁ פָּתַר אוֹתוֹ לְשׁוֹן חֵן
sources.says: Rashi says Menahem explained נחנת as from camping, but Dunash explained it as from grace.

sources.quote: ומה נחנת ר"ל מה חנינה עשו לך בבא לך חבלים
sources.says: Malbim says it means: what mercy was shown you when the pains came?

22:24.headline: 'Coniah': the king's name cut short as a put-down
22:24.body: The king is Jehoiachin, also called Jeconiah. Here God calls him Coniahu, dropping the first part of his name. Radak says it was to belittle him.

sources.quote: וקראו כניהו לפחיתות
sources.says: Radak says he called him Coniahu to diminish him.

sources.quote: כניהו. הוא יכניה והוא יהויכין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says Coniahu is Jeconiah, who is Jehoiachin.

22:24.headline: 'I will tear you off' hides 'I will mend you'
22:24.body: אתקנך means 'I will pull you off', like a signet ring. Rashi says the extra נ invites a midrash. Where he was torn off, he was mended: he repented in Babylon. His grandson Zerubbabel was later called God's 'signet'.

sources.quote: וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה (פסיקתא דרב כהנא כד:יא): בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁנִּתַּק – נִתְקַן; שֶׁעָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה בְּבָבֶל
sources.says: Rashi cites a midrash: where he was torn off, there he was mended, because he repented in Babylon.

sources.quote: וגם רמז במלת אתקנך ענין תיקון
sources.says: Malbim says the word אתקנך also hints at repair.

22:26.headline: 'Your mother who bore you', or who raised you badly?
22:26.body: ילדתך usually means 'bore you'. Metzudat Zion says it can mean 'raised', as with children born on Joseph's knees. Metzudat David says she raised him in evil ways.

sources.quote: ילדתך. ענין גדול ואמון וכן יולדו על ברכי יוסף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means raising and rearing, as in 'born on Joseph's knees'.

sources.quote: אשר גדלה אותך ללכת בדרך הרעה
sources.says: Metzudat David says she raised him to walk in the evil way.

22:28.headline: An idol is an עצב because it brings its worshipers grief
22:28.body: This form, עצב, appears only here. Metzudat Zion says it means an idol. It is named from עצב, 'sorrow', because its worshipers cry out and get no answer. Rashi reads it as a broken, worthless image.

sources.quote: כן נקרא הצורה הנעבדת כמ״ש עצבי הגוים (תהלים קלה) וזהו לפי שמעצב לב עובדיו צועק אליו ואינו נענה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says an idol is called this because it grieves the hearts of its worshipers, who cry to it and get no answer.

sources.quote: שֶׁמָּא צוּרָה נִשְׁבָּר וְנִבְזֶה הָאִישׁ הַזֶּה
sources.says: Rashi says the question is whether this man is a broken, despised image.

22:29.headline: 'Land, land, land': why three times?
22:29.body: Rashi gives three readings. He went from his land to another land, so you, land of Israel, listen. Or: the land that is the land of lands. Or: the three lands of Israel, Judah, the far side of the Jordan, and the Galilee.

sources.quote: מֵאַרְצוֹ גָּלָה אֶל אֶרֶץ אַחֶרֶת, וְאַתְּ, אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שִׁמְעִי דְּבַר ה׳
sources.says: Rashi says: from his land he was exiled to another land, and you, land of Israel, hear God's word.

sources.quote: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שָׁלֹשׁ אֲרָצוֹת הָיוּ בָּהּ: יְהוּדָה וְעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן וְהַגָּלִיל
sources.says: Rashi also says the land of Israel had three lands in it: Judah, across the Jordan, and the Galilee.

22:30.headline: 'Childless', or 'ruined'? And a decree undone by repentance
22:30.body: The Targum reads ערירי as childless. Metzudat Zion reads it as ruined, as in 'raze it, raze it'. Radak cites the Sages: repentance tore up this decree, since his grandson Zerubbabel later ruled Judah.

sources.quote: כְּתוּבוּ יַת גַבְרָא הָדֵין דְלָא וְלַד
sources.says: The Targum says: write this man as one without a child.

sources.quote: ערירי. ענין השחתה וחורבן כמו ערו ערו עד היסוד בה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means destruction and ruin, as in 'raze it, raze it to the foundation'.

sources.quote: גדולה תשובה שמקרעת גזר דינו של אדם שנאמר כתבו את האיש הזה ערירי
sources.says: Radak cites the Sages: great is repentance, which tears up a person's sentence, as with 'write this man childless'.

23:4.headline: The same verb for neglect, punishment, and none missing
23:4.body: The root פקד runs through these verses: the shepherds did not look after the flock, so God will "look after" them with punishment. Here Rashi reads it a third way: none of the flock will be missing.

sources.quote: וְלֹא יֶחְסְרוּ, לָשׁוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it means they will not be missing, as in "not one man of us is missing."

sources.quote: ענין זכרון והשגחה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says that in verse 2 the same verb means remembering and watching over.

23:6.headline: A king named 'The LORD is our righteousness'
23:6.body: The king to come is called ה' צדקנו, "the LORD is our righteousness." Radak says the name praises God, not the king, the way Moses named an altar "the LORD is my banner," and Rashi reads it as: in his days the LORD will make us righteous.

sources.quote: ישראל יקרא המשיח בזה השם
sources.says: Radak says Israel will call the Messiah by this name.

sources.quote: וזו הקריאה על דרך הקריאה שקרא משה רבינו עליו השלום למזבח ה' נסי
sources.says: Radak says the name works like Moses naming an altar "the LORD is my banner": it names what God did, not the one who bears it.

sources.quote: ה׳ מַצְדִּיק אוֹתָנוּ בְּיָמָיו שֶׁל זֶה
sources.says: Rashi says it means the LORD makes us righteous in this king's days.

23:9.headline: A man whom wine has 'passed over'
23:9.body: עבר means to pass or cross over. Maimonides says it is also used for someone who overdoes a thing and crosses its limit, as with this drunk man, and Radak says the wine has overpowered him.

sources.quote: הוא הושאל גם למי שעשה מעשה כלשהו והפריז בו ועבר את גבולו
sources.says: Maimonides says עבר is also borrowed for one who did something to excess and went past its bounds, and cites this verse.

sources.quote: עבר עליו היין כלומר שגבר עליו ונשתכר
sources.says: Radak says the wine came over him, meaning it overpowered him and he became drunk.

23:10.headline: Their running, or their desire?
23:10.body: מרוצתם means their running: Radak says they run eagerly, but only toward evil. Rashi notes that the Targum reads it from רצון, will, so it is their desire that is evil.

sources.quote: זריזותם ומרוצתם הם לרעה כי לא ירוצו לדבר מצוה
sources.says: Radak says their eagerness and running are for evil, since they never run to do a good deed.

sources.quote: וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם לְשׁוֹן רָצוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it means a running course, and that the Targum reads it as will or desire.

sources.quote: בִּרְעוּת נַפְשֵׁיהוֹן
sources.says: The Targum renders it "in the desire of their souls."

23:12.headline: Slippery, dark, and pushed: three ways to fall at once
23:12.body: Their road will be slippery, in the dark, and they will be pushed. Rashi says each of the first two alone makes a man stumble, so together they mean stumbling on stumbling, and Radak counts all three to show how fast they will fall.

sources.quote: כִּשָּׁלוֹן עַל כִּשָּׁלוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it is stumbling on stumbling: slippery ground in daylight trips you, and darkness without slipperiness trips you too.

sources.quote: ולרוב מהירות הנפילה זכר בה שלש סבות חלקות הדרך והאפלה והדחיה
sources.says: Radak says the verse names three causes, the slippery road, the darkness and the push, to show how quickly they will fall.

23:17.headline: Walking after what the heart sees and wants
23:17.body: The phrase is usually read as stubbornness of heart. Metzudat Zion reads שררות from a root meaning to see: following whatever the heart sees and craves.

sources.quote: ענין ראיה ר״ל מה שהלב רואה וחומד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means seeing: what the heart sees and desires.

sources.quote: בְּהִרְהוּר לִבֵּיהּ
sources.says: The Targum renders it "in the musing of his heart."

23:19.headline: A storm that settles, shakes, or whirls
23:19.body: Rashi says the storm "settles" and comes to rest on the heads of the wicked. Metzudat Zion hears trembling in the word, and Malbim a whirlwind that turns in circles like a dance.

sources.quote: מִשְׁתַּכֵּן, מְחַזֵּר לִשְׁכּוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it means settling down, looking for a place to rest.

sources.quote: מלשון חיל וחלחלה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from the words for trembling and shuddering.

sources.quote: סער ההולך במחול וסבוב שהוא מזיק מאד
sources.says: Malbim suggests it is a storm that moves in a circle, like a dance, and does great harm.

23:20.headline: 'You will understand,' a hint that the dead will rise
23:20.body: The verse says you will understand it at the end of days, not they will. Radak sees a hint that the same people will live again then, when the dead are revived.

sources.quote: ובאמרו תתבוננו ולא אמר יתבוננו רמז לתחיית המתים בימות המשיח
sources.says: Radak says that by saying "you will understand" rather than "they will," the verse hints at the revival of the dead in the days of the Messiah.

23:23.headline: A God of nearby, or a God of lately?
23:23.body: מקרב can mean near in place or recent in time. Rashi reads near: do you think I see only what is close to Me? Radak reads recent: am I a new god, like the idols that "came lately"?

sources.quote: שֶׁאֵינִי רוֹאֶה אֶלָּא בְּסָמוּךְ לִי
sources.says: Rashi reads it as: do they think I see only what is near Me and cannot judge those far below?

sources.quote: כמו אלהים אחרים שנאמר עליהם חדשים מקרוב באו
sources.says: Radak reads it as recent, like the other gods of whom it is said "new ones that came lately."

23:24.headline: God fills heaven and earth, but not as a body fills space
23:24.body: God says He fills heaven and earth. Radak says this is a figure of speech: God has no body to take up space, so it means His watch over the world reaches every place.

sources.quote: וזה דרך משל כי הוא יתברך איננו גוף שיהיה ממלא מקום אלא רוצה לומר כי השגחתו בכל מקום
sources.says: Radak says this is figurative, since God is not a body that fills space; it means His providence is everywhere.

sources.quote: כך באותו אור בעצמו הוא צופה בנו, ובשלו הוא יתעלה עמנו תמיד, צופה ומשגיח
sources.says: Maimonides cites this verse to say that by the same light through which we know God, He watches us and is always with us.

23:28.headline: No grain without straw, and no dream without nonsense
23:28.body: Straw and grain stand for dream and prophecy: Rashi reads "what has a lie to do with truth?" Radak brings the sages' lesson that just as there is no grain without straw, there is no dream without some empty talk in it.

sources.quote: מַה עִנְיַן שֶׁקֶר אֵצֶל אֱמֶת
sources.says: Rashi says it means: what does falsehood have to do with truth?

sources.quote: כשם שאי אפשר לבר בלא תבן כך אי אפשר לחלום בלא דברים בטלים
sources.says: Radak cites Rabbi Yochanan: as there cannot be grain without straw, there cannot be a dream without idle things.

23:29.headline: Real prophecy hits like a hammer, not like a dream
23:29.body: God's word is like fire and like a hammer that smashes rock. Rashi and Metzudat David say true prophecy comes with overwhelming force, unlike a dream, and Malbim says it shatters the prophet's body the way a hammer breaks stone.

sources.quote: כִּי דְּבַר נְבוּאָה כְּשֶׁבָּאָה בְּפִי הַנָּבִיא בִּגְבוּרָה הִיא בָאָה בּוֹ כְּאֵשׁ בּוֹעֶרֶת
sources.says: Rashi says prophecy enters the prophet with power, like a burning fire, so no one should mistake a dream for it.

sources.quote: כן הוא חלום הנבואיי ולא כן חלום הדמיוני כי הרגשתם קלה מאד
sources.says: Metzudat David says a prophetic dream is felt with great force, while an ordinary dream is felt only faintly.

sources.quote: שהוא כפטיש יפוצץ סלע לחתיכות כן תפוצץ את הגוף
sources.says: Malbim says as a hammer smashes rock to pieces, prophecy shatters the prophet's body.

23:33.headline: A 'burden' of the LORD: prophecy and heavy load
23:33.body: משא means a prophecy, and also a heavy load. The people mockingly asked for the LORD's משא, meaning His words weighed on them, and God answers that they are the burden, and He will throw it off.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן שְׂחוֹק, לְפִי שֶׁנְּבוּאָתוֹ לָהֶם לְמַשָּׂא
sources.says: Rashi says they said it in mockery, because his prophecy was a burden to them.

sources.quote: אַתֶּם לְמַשָּׂא לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says the answer is: you are a burden to God, and He will cast you off.

sources.quote: כי כשהיו אומרים משא ה' היה דעתם וכונתם ענין כבדות ומשא
sources.says: Radak says that when they said "burden of the LORD," they meant heaviness and load.

23:36.headline: Turning a prophet's words into their opposite
23:36.body: God says the people "turn upside down" the words of the living God. Maimonides uses this verse to show how listeners can hear the very opposite of what a prophet means, and Radak says they turned a word for prophecy into a word for burden.

sources.quote: ומחלקם הם מבינים מה שמנוגד לו או סותר אותו
sources.says: Maimonides says that some prophetic words the masses do not understand at all, and some they take in the opposite sense, citing this verse.

sources.quote: בלבבכם תהפכו אותם מנבואה לכבדות
sources.says: Radak says in their hearts they turned God's word from prophecy into heaviness.

24:1.headline: Two 'dudaim' of figs: a rare word for pots or baskets
24:1.body: Rashi says דּוּדָאֵי means pots. Radak says the א is extra, so it is the same as דּוּד in the next verse, a basket, as Targum Jonathan has it. Rashi also reads the dudaim of the Song of Songs as these two baskets of good and bad figs.

sources.quote: דּוּדָאֵי. קְדֵרוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the word means pots.

sources.quote: ואל"ף דודאי תאנים נוספת
sources.says: Radak says the letter א in דודאי is extra.

sources.quote: תְּרֵין סַלֵי תֵינִין
sources.says: Targum Jonathan translates: two baskets of figs.

sources.quote: דּוּדָאֵי הַתְּאֵנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת וְהָרָעוֹת
sources.says: Rashi reads the dudaim of the Song of Songs as the baskets of good and bad figs in this verse.

24:2.headline: The first-ripe figs stand for the first group sent into exile
24:2.body: Rashi says early figs are dear to the person who finds them. Malbim says a fig left on the tree after it ripens is spoiled by the sun, so the first ones picked, the exiles of King Jehoiachin, are the good ones.

sources.quote: שֶׁהֵם חֲבִיבוֹת עַל מוֹצְאֵיהֶם בְּרֵאשִׁיתָם
sources.says: Rashi says the first figs are dear to those who find them.

sources.quote: התאנה אם אין לוקטין אותה תיכף כשנתבכרה היא מותלעת מהשמש
sources.says: Malbim says a fig not picked as soon as it ripens is spoiled by the sun.

sources.quote: המשיל את גלות יהויכין שנלקטו תחלה מארץ ישראל לתאני הבכורות שנלקטו ראשונה
sources.says: Malbim says the prophet compares Jehoiachin's exiles, taken first from the land, to the first figs picked.

24:9.headline: A byword: people will repeat their story over and over
24:9.body: לִשְׁנִינָה comes from the verb in 'you shall repeat them to your children'. Rashi and the Metzudat David say people everywhere will keep retelling what happened to them.

sources.quote: ענין ספור ואמירה כמו ושננתם לבניך
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says it means telling and saying, as in 'you shall repeat them to your children'.

sources.quote: שֶׁיִּשְׁנְנוּ וִידַבְּרוּ הַכֹּל בְּפֻרְעָנוּתָם
sources.says: Rashi says everyone will repeat and talk about their punishment.

sources.quote: יתמידו לספר מהצרות הבאות עליהם
sources.says: The Metzudat David says people will keep telling of the troubles that came on them.

25:1.headline: 'On Jeremiah' means 'to Jeremiah'
25:1.body: Radak, Metzudat David and Malbim say על here means אל, 'to'. In the next verse, Malbim notes that Jeremiah spoke to Jerusalem's people directly but only about the rest of Judah, so על there means 'about'.

sources.quote: הדבר, על ירמיהו. כמו אל
sources.says: Radak says על ירמיהו is like אל, 'to'.

sources.quote: על ירמיהו. אל ירמיהו
sources.says: Metzudat David says על ירמיהו means אל ירמיהו.

sources.quote: ואל כל. בירושלים ישב ודבר אליהם בנוכח ולא כן ליהודה דבר עליהם לא אליהם
sources.says: Malbim says that in Jerusalem he sat and spoke to them face to face, but for Judah he spoke about them, not to them.

25:3.headline: 'I rose early and spoke' means 'I spoke again and again'
25:3.body: Rashi says אשכים ודבר is a present tense: I was always rising early to speak. Metzudat Zion says it means eager haste, and Radak says the aleph stands for the ה of השכם, since the letters א ה ו י swap.

sources.quote: אַשְׁכֵּים וְדַבֵּר. לְשׁוֹן הוֹוֶה: הָיִיתִי מַשְׁכִּים וּמְדַבֵּר תָּמִיד
sources.says: Rashi says it is a present tense: I was always rising early and speaking.

sources.quote: אשכים. מלשון השכמה והוא ענין זרוז
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says אשכים comes from rising early, which means eagerness.

sources.quote: האל״ף במקום ה״א השכם כי אותיות אהו״י מתחלפות
sources.says: Radak says the aleph is in place of the ה of השכם, because the letters אהו״י swap.

25:7.headline: Written 'they angered me', read 'to anger me'
25:7.body: The text is written הכעסוני, 'because they angered me', but read הכעיסני, 'to anger me'. Radak says the reading means they worship idols in order to anger God, not for any benefit to themselves.

sources.quote: כתוב רצה לומר בעבור שהכעיסוני וקרי הכעיסני למען הכעיס אותי עושים העכו"ם לא להנאה שיש להם בה
sources.says: Radak says the written form means because they angered me, and the read form means to anger me, which idol-worshippers do not for any benefit to themselves.

25:12.headline: How do the 'full seventy years' add up?
25:12.body: Radak counts Nebuchadnezzar's 45 years, Evil-Merodach's 23, and two of Belshazzar's three, because Belshazzar was killed in his third year before it was complete. Metzudat Zion says מלאות means completion.

sources.quote: הרי מ"ה וכ"ג הרי ס"ח ושתים לבלשצר הרי ע' לפיכך אמר כמלאת כי שלמים היו להם ע' שנה
sources.says: Radak adds forty-five and twenty-three to make sixty-eight, and two for Belshazzar to make seventy, which is why it says 'when it is filled'.

sources.quote: כמלאות. ענין השלמה כמו ובמלאות ימי טהרה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says כמלאות means completion, like 'when the days of purification are completed'.

25:16.headline: 'Shake violently' may mean 'go mad'
25:16.body: Metzudat Zion, Radak and Malbim say והתגעשו means violent shaking, like 'the earth shook and quaked'. Rashi, following Targum Jonathan, reads it as going mad.

sources.quote: וְהִתְגֹּעֲשׁוּ. ״וְיִשְׁתַּגְּעוּן״ (תרגום יונתן)
sources.says: Rashi gives Targum Jonathan's 'and they will go mad'.

sources.quote: והתגועשו. ענין תנועה חזקה כמו ותגעש ותרעש הארץ
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means strong motion, like 'and the earth shook and quaked'.

sources.quote: וענינו ענין ותגעש ותרעש הארץ
sources.says: Radak says its meaning is like 'and the earth shook and quaked'.

sources.quote: והתגעשו. רעש הגוף
sources.says: Malbim says והתגעשו is the shaking of the body.

25:16.headline: Here והתהללו means 'act mad', not 'praise themselves'
25:16.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion say it comes from הוללות, madness and foolishness, as in 'the chariots rage'. Malbim says it is the mind's confusion, while the shaking is the body's.

sources.quote: וְהִתְהוֹלָלוּ. לְשׁוֹן הוֹלֵלוּת
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word of madness, and they will be foolish.

sources.quote: והתהוללו. מלשון הוללות ושטות כמו והתהוללו הרכב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from madness and folly, like 'the chariots rage'.

sources.quote: והתהוללו. בלבול השכל
sources.says: Malbim says והתהוללו is the confusing of the mind.

25:18.headline: 'As this day' shows Jeremiah wrote this after the fall
25:18.body: Rashi and Metzudat David say כיום הזה means as they are today, so Jeremiah wrote his book after the destruction.

sources.quote: כַּאֲשֶׁר הֵם הַיּוֹם; לְאַחַר הַחֻרְבָּן כָּתַב יִרְמְיָה סִפְרוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means as they are today, and that Jeremiah wrote his book after the destruction.

sources.quote: כי ירמיה כתב ספרו אחר החורבן לזה אמר כיום הזה שהמה חרבים
sources.says: Metzudat David says Jeremiah wrote his book after the destruction, so he said 'as this day', when they are in ruins.

25:18.headline: Why 'its kings', when only one king ruled?
25:18.body: Metzudat David says the plural counts the king's sons, who were also called kings. Radak says it means three kings, Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin and Zedekiah.

sources.quote: עם כי לא היה אלא מלך אחד אמר מלכיה כי גם בני המלך נקראו בשם מלכים
sources.says: Metzudat David says that though there was only one king, it says 'its kings' because the king's sons were also called kings.

sources.quote: ואת מלכיה. יהויקים ויהויכין וצדקיהו
sources.says: Radak says 'its kings' means Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin and Zedekiah.

25:23.headline: 'Cut at the corner': dwellers at the edge, or the circumcised?
25:23.body: Rashi, Radak and Targum Jonathan say קצוצי פאה means those who live at the farthest edge, from קצה and פאה. Malbim says it means the rest of Ishmael's and Keturah's sons, who cut off the flesh of the foreskin.

sources.quote: הַמּוּקְצִים בִּקְצֵה אוֹתָהּ הָרוּחַ
sources.says: Rashi says they are those set at the edge of that direction.

sources.quote: השוכנים בקצה העולם בפאתו כי הפאה הוא קץ הדבר
sources.says: Radak says they are those who dwell at the end of the world, in its corner, since פאה is the end of a thing.

sources.quote: כָּל מַקְפֵי פָאתָא
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it 'all who encircle the corner'.

sources.quote: יתר בני ישמעאל ובני קטורה שקצצו ערלת בשרם
sources.says: Malbim says it means the rest of the sons of Ishmael and Keturah, who cut the foreskin of their flesh.

25:26.headline: Sheshach is Babylon, written in a letter-swap code
25:26.body: Rashi, Metzudat David and Radak say ששך is Babylon written in the code that swaps the first Hebrew letter with the last and the second with the second to last, known as א״ת ב״ש. Targum Jonathan simply writes 'king of Babylon'.

sources.quote: שֵׁשַׁךְ. הוּא בָּבֶל בְּא״ת ב״ש
sources.says: Rashi says ששך is Babylon, in the code א״ת ב״ש.

sources.quote: ומלך ששך. הוא בבל בא״ת ב״ש וכן נקרא בסוף הספר
sources.says: Metzudat David says the king of ששך is Babylon in the code א״ת ב״ש, and it is called so at the end of the book.

sources.quote: וששך היא בבל באלפא ביתא דא״ת ב״ש
sources.says: Radak says ששך is Babylon in the alphabet of א״ת ב״ש.

sources.quote: וּמַלְכָּא דְבָבֶל יִשְׁתֵּי בַּתְרֵיהוֹן
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it 'and the king of Babylon will drink after them'.

25:30.headline: 'Heidad' is the shout of workers treading grapes
25:30.body: Rashi, Metzudat Zion and Radak say הידד is the shout workers give to urge each other on, as grape-treaders do. So God's cry against the earth is like the winepress shout.

sources.quote: לָשׁוֹן הוּא שֶׁצּוֹעֲקִין עוֹשֵׂי מְלָאכָה כְּבֵדָה בְּקוֹל רָם, לְזָרֵז זֶה אֶת זֶה לְהִתְחַזֵּק, וְדוֹרְכֵי גִּתּוֹת רְגִילִין בָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word that workers at heavy labor shout loudly to urge each other on, and grape-treaders are used to it.

sources.quote: הידד. המלה ההיא מיוחדת לקריאת דורכי היין לזרז עצמם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says that word is special to the call of wine-treaders urging themselves on.

sources.quote: יצעק כמו הדורכים בגת שמרימין קול לחזק עצמם
sources.says: Radak says he will shout like those who tread in the winepress, who raise their voice to strengthen themselves.

25:30.headline: 'Will answer' may mean 'will shout'
25:30.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion say ענה here means raising a loud voice, a shout. Malbim reads it as answering: all the predators answer the lion's roar, as all the treaders answer the first.

sources.quote: יַעֲנֶה. כָּל לְשׁוֹן עֲנִיָּה צְעָקַת קוֹל רָם הִיא
sources.says: Rashi says every use of ענייה is a cry in a loud voice.

sources.quote: יענה. ענין הרמת קול וכן וענו הלוים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says יענה means raising the voice, as in 'and the Levites shall speak up'.

sources.quote: הידד כדורכים יענה, כמו שלקול הראשון של הדורך עונים כולם הידד
sources.says: Malbim says it is as at the first treader's cry, when everyone answers 'heidad'.

25:31.headline: 'Is judged' means 'argues His case'
25:31.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion say נשפט here means arguing a dispute, not being judged. Radak says it is as if God enters a court case with the nations to punish them for their evil.

sources.quote: נִשְׁפָּט. מִתְוַכֵּחַ בַּדִּין
sources.says: Rashi says נשפט means arguing in judgment.

sources.quote: נשפט. ענין ויכוח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נשפט means argument.

sources.quote: נשפט. כאילו נכנס במשפט עמהם שיענישם על רעתם
sources.says: Radak says נשפט means as if He entered a lawsuit with them to punish them for their evil.

25:36.headline: 'Their pasture' may be a place, or the flock itself
25:36.body: Metzudat David says מרעיתם is the place where the shepherds fed the flock, a picture of Jerusalem. Radak says it is the flock of their pasture, the nations whose kings are their shepherds.

sources.quote: מרעיתם. מקום שהרועים רעו את הצאן והוא למשל על ירושלים
sources.says: Metzudat David says מרעיתם is the place where the shepherds fed the flock, a picture of Jerusalem.

sources.quote: מרעיתם. צאן מרעיתם והם הגוים שהם מלכיהם ורועיהם
sources.says: Radak says מרעיתם means the flock of their pasture, the nations whose kings are their shepherds.

sources.quote: מרעיתם. מל׳ מרעה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says מרעיתם is from the word for pasture.

29:2.headline: The 'shutters' taken to Babylon were the gatekeepers
29:2.body: מסגר comes from the word for shutting. The Targum and Metzudat David read it as the men who shut the city gates, exiled along with the craftsmen.

sources.quote: הם האומנים ושומרי השערים אשר סגרו אותם בעתם כן ת״י
sources.says: Metzudat David says these are the craftsmen and the gatekeepers who shut the gates at the right time, as the Targum has it.

sources.quote: וְאוּמְנַיָא וְתַרְעַיָא מִירוּשְׁלֵם
sources.says: The Targum renders the pair as 'the craftsmen and the gatekeepers'.

29:8.headline: The same verb Eve used for the snake's trick
29:8.body: God warns that the false prophets must not ישיאו the exiles, lead them astray. Rashi and Metzudat Zion point to Eve's words in Eden, 'the snake השיאני, tricked me.'

sources.quote: יַשִּׁיאוּ. לְשׁוֹן הֲסָתָה, כְּמוֹ ״הַנָּחָשׁ הִשִּׁיאַנִי״
sources.says: Rashi says it means enticing, as in 'the snake tricked me' (Genesis 3:13).

sources.quote: ענין פתוי והסתה כמו הנחש השיאני
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means seducing and enticing, as with the snake in Genesis 3.

29:8.headline: Whose dreams are these, and who makes them happen?
29:8.body: The verse speaks of 'your dreams that you מחלמים', a form meaning 'make dream'. Radak says the people make their prophets dream, because the prophets would not dream if no one listened. Malbim says the people bring on these dreams by what they think about all day.

sources.quote: מחלמים. משפטו מחלימים כי הוא מבנין הפעיל
sources.says: Radak says the word is a causative form, properly מחלימים, 'you make dream'.

sources.quote: שאתם גורמים שיהיו הם חולמים שאם לא הייתם אתם שומעים אל חלומותיהם לא היו חולמים
sources.says: Radak says you cause them to dream, since they would not dream if you did not listen to their dreams.

sources.quote: ר"ל אתם מסבבים החלומות ע"י רעיונות היום
sources.says: Malbim says you bring about the dreams through your daytime thoughts.

29:14.headline: Two returns: to your old standing, then to your land
29:14.body: The verse says ושבתי את שבותכם and later והשבתי אתכם, two forms of 'return'. Malbim says the first means restoring the people's rank and the second means bringing them back to the place. Metzudat David reads the first as giving back their former rule.

sources.quote: הוא תמיד השבת המדרגה
sources.says: Malbim says the simple form שב always means restoring a rank.

sources.quote: והשיב בהפעיל הוא השבה למקום
sources.says: Malbim says the causative form השיב means bringing back to a place.

sources.quote: ושבתי הוא השבת המדרגה שתשובו למעלתכם
sources.says: Malbim says ושבתי means you will return to your former standing.

sources.quote: את הדבר הראוי להשיב לכם והוא הממשלה הראשונה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means giving back what should be returned to you, your former rule.

29:22.headline: The false prophet's name is cut short to shame him
29:22.body: In verse 21 he is called אחאב. Here his name is spelled אחב, without the alef. Radak says the name was made smaller as an insult.

sources.quote: וכאחב. הקטין שמו לגנאי
sources.says: Radak says the name was made smaller to shame him.

sources.quote: וכאחב. הוא אחאב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says this is the same Ahab named in verse 21.

29:24.headline: Shemaiah 'the Nehelamite': from a town, or a dreamer
29:24.body: Rashi and the Targum say הנחלמי names his home town. Radak says he got the name because he dreamed dreams (חלומות) for the exiles, promising they would soon go home. It echoes the false dreams in verse 8.

sources.quote: הַנֶּחֱלָמִי. שֵׁם מָקוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says it is the name of a place.

sources.quote: נקרא כן לפי שהיה חולם להם חלומות שישובו מהרה לירושלם
sources.says: Radak says he was called this because he dreamed dreams for them that they would soon return to Jerusalem.

sources.quote: וְלִשְׁמַעְיָה דְמִן חֲלַם
sources.says: The Targum calls him 'Shemaiah who is from Chelam'.

29:26.headline: 'Madman' was a common insult for a prophet
29:26.body: Shemaiah wants every משגע, every madman who prophesies, locked up, and he means Jeremiah. Radak says people called a true prophet 'madman' to mock him, as Jehu's officers did in 2 Kings 9:11.

sources.quote: ולנביא היו קוראים לגנאי משגע וכן מדוע בא המשגע הזה
sources.says: Radak says people called a prophet 'madman' as an insult, as in 'why did this madman come to you'.

sources.quote: על כל איש משוגע ומתנבא דברי שגעון מלבו
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means anyone who prophesies mad words of his own making.

3:2.headline: A crude word is written, but a gentler one is read aloud
3:2.body: The written word שגלת is a blunt word for sleeping with someone. Radak says the reading tradition replaces it with שכבת, 'you lay', to keep the language clean.

sources.quote: שגלת. כתיב שכבת קרי כמו ישגלנה ישכבנה לשון נקיה
sources.says: Radak says שגלת is what is written and שכבת is what is read, the same way the Torah's ישגלנה is read ישכבנה, as clean language.

sources.quote: שגלת. ענין משכב המשגל וכן ואיש אחר ישגלנה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means sexual relations, as in Deuteronomy 28:30.

3:2.headline: Why the desert nomad is called ערבי
3:2.body: Israel waits by the roads for her lovers like a nomad in the desert. Rashi says the name ערבי comes from ערבה, the open desert where he lives. Malbim suggests ערב, evening: someone who sits in the desert at dusk where no one sees him.

sources.quote: וְעַל שֵׁם כָּךְ הוּא קָרוּי עֲרָבִי, שֶׁשּׁוֹכֵן בָּעֲרָבָה
sources.says: Rashi says he lives in tents out in the desert, and is called ערבי because he dwells in the ערבה.

sources.quote: כערבי יל"פ מענין ערב ולילה, היושב בערב במדבר שאין איש רואהו
sources.says: Malbim says it can be read from ערב, evening: one who sits in the desert at evening where no one sees him.

sources.quote: כי כן דרך הערביים השכנים במדבר יושבים להם על הדרכים מיחלי השיירות
sources.says: Radak says desert Arabs sit by the roads waiting for caravans to trade with.

3:5.headline: 'And you could': you won out, or you did all you could
3:5.body: The verse ends with one word, ותוכל, 'and you were able'. Rashi reads it as winning: you won the fight to rebel. Radak, following the Targum, reads it as doing as much evil as you were able.

sources.quote: וַתּוּכָל. וְנִצַּחְתְּ לִמְרוֹד
sources.says: Rashi says it means you prevailed in rebelling.

sources.quote: תרגם יונתן ואסגית כלומר הרבית לעשות רעות בכל יכלתך
sources.says: Radak says the Targum renders it 'you did much', meaning you did as much evil as you could.

sources.quote: כמו כי שרית עם אלהים ותוכל
sources.says: Malbim compares it to Jacob's 'you strove with God and prevailed', meaning she won out in holding on to her evil.

3:7.headline: Two sisters, two names: the one who strayed and the traitor
3:7.body: The prophet calls northern Israel משבה, 'the one who turned away', and Judah בגודה, 'the traitor'. Rashi says Judah gets the harsher name because she saw her sister exiled and still did not learn. Malbim says Israel strayed in the open, while Judah cheated in secret.

sources.quote: בֹּגֵדָה קָשָׁה מִמְּשׁוּבָה
sources.says: Rashi says 'traitor' is a harsher word than 'one who turned away'.

sources.quote: יְהוּדָה, שֶׁרָאוּ שֶׁגָּלוּ אֵלּוּ וְלֹא לָקְחוּ מוּסָר, קְרוּיִין בֹּגֵדָה
sources.says: Rashi says Judah is called traitor because they saw the north exiled and did not take the lesson.

sources.quote: ואת שבט יהודה קרא בשם בוגדה שדומה כזונה הבוגדת בבעלה בצנעה
sources.says: Malbim says Judah is called traitor because she is like a wife who cheats on her husband in secret.

3:12.headline: 'I will not let my face fall': here 'face' means anger
3:12.body: God says לא אפיל פני בכם, literally 'I will not cast my face on you'. Rashi and the Targum read פני as 'my anger'. Metzudat Zion says anger is called face because it shows on the face. Malbim says there is a face of favor and a face of anger.

sources.quote: פָּנַי. ״רוּגְזִי״, כֵּן תַּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן
sources.says: Rashi says פני means 'my anger', as the Targum translates.

sources.quote: פני. ענין חמה וכעס
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means wrath and anger, because anger is seen on a person's face.

sources.quote: יש פנים של רצון, שהוא ההשגחה לטובה
sources.says: Malbim says there is a face of favor, which is God's care for good, and a face of anger, which is His attention to punish.

3:13.headline: 'Your ways' here means 'your legs'
3:13.body: The verse says Israel scattered her דרכים to strangers. Metzudat Zion says דרכים here means legs, the things you tread with. Rashi reads the whole phrase as an image of a harlot.

sources.quote: דרכיך. רגליך ע״ש שדורכים ופוסעים בו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says דרכיך means your legs, named for treading and stepping.

sources.quote: וַתְּפַזְּרִי אֶת דְּרָכַיִךְ. לְשׁוֹן זְנוּת
sources.says: Rashi says the phrase is the language of harlotry, the spreading of legs.

3:14.headline: 'Return, you children who turned away'
3:14.body: שובו, 'return', and שובבים, 'wayward', sound alike. Radak ties שובבים to משבה, the name the prophet gave northern Israel, meaning rebels. Rashi says they turned aside because they had too much ease and plenty.

sources.quote: שובו בנים שובבים.  מורדים כמו משובה שפירשנו
sources.says: Radak says שובבים means rebels, the same word as משובה explained earlier.

sources.quote: שֶׁשּׁוֹבַבְתֶּם דַּרְכְּכֶם מֵרוֹב כֹּל
sources.says: Rashi says they turned their way aside because they had plenty of everything.

3:15.headline: Shepherds 'after my heart' means shepherds after my will
3:15.body: God promises leaders כלבי, 'like my heart'. Maimonides lists this verse to show that לב, heart, can mean will. So the leaders will act as God wants.

sources.quote: הוא שמו של הרצון: "וְנָתַתִּי לָכֶם רֹעִים כְּלִבִּי"
sources.says: Maimonides says one meaning of לב is will, and cites 'I will give you shepherds after my heart'.

sources.quote: שירעו אותם כלבי וחפצי
sources.says: Radak says it means they will lead the people according to God's heart and wish.

3:22.headline: God offers to 'heal' their turning away
3:22.body: God says ארפה, 'I will heal', about Israel's sins. Radak says healing is used here for forgiveness. A sin is a wound of the soul, and forgiveness with return is its cure.

sources.quote: ואמר ענין רפואה על הסליחה דרך השאלה וכן רפאה נפשי כי חטאתי לך
sources.says: Radak says healing is used for forgiveness as a figure, as in 'heal my soul, for I have sinned against You'.

sources.quote: כן מכת הנפש והוא העון רפואתה הסליחה עם התשובה
sources.says: Radak says sin is a wound of the soul, and its healing is forgiveness together with repentance.

3:24.headline: 'The Shame' is a nickname for the idol Baal
3:24.body: The people say 'the Shame' ate up their fathers' work. Radak says the Shame is the god Baal, renamed for the disgrace he brings, as Jerubbaal is also called Jerubbesheth.

sources.quote: הבעל שהיו עובדים נקרא בשת כמו וינזרו לבשת שהוא כמו לבעל וכן נקרא ירובשת ירובעל
sources.says: Radak says the Baal they served is called Shame, as in Hosea, and so Jerubbaal is also called Jerubbesheth.

sources.quote: וְהַבֹּשֶׁת. עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁעָסַקְנוּ בָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says the Shame is the idol worship they practiced.

34:5.headline: "You will die in peace": blinded and jailed, yet in peace?
34:5.body: Zedekiah's eyes were put out. Radak says "in peace" still fits: he did not die by the sword, he died in bed and was honored as a king. Rashi and Metzudat David cite the sages: Nebuchadnezzar died first, Zedekiah was let out of prison, and he died the next day and was buried with honor.

sources.quote: אע"פ שנקרו עיניו כיון שלא ימות בחרב וימות על מטתו ויעשו לו כבוד כמו שעושים למלכים זהו בשלום
sources.says: Radak says that although his eyes were put out, he would not die by the sword but in his bed, honored as kings are, and that is "in peace".

sources.quote: שֶׁכָּל יְמֵי נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר לֹא יָצְאוּ אֲסִירָיו מֵאֲסִירֵיהֶם, וּכְשֶׁמֵּת נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר יָצָא צִדְקִיָּהוּ מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִים, וּלְמָחֳרָת מֵת וְקָבְרוּהוּ בְּכָבוֹד
sources.says: Rashi says Nebuchadnezzar never freed his prisoners while he lived; when he died, Zedekiah came out of prison, died the next day, and was buried with honor.

sources.quote: ארז״ל לאחר שמת נ״נ הוציאו לצדקיה מן המאסר ומת על מטתו
sources.says: Metzudat David cites the sages: after Nebuchadnezzar died, Zedekiah was taken out of prison and died in his bed.

34:5.headline: "Burnings" for dead kings: their beds and belongings, not their bodies
34:5.body: The verse does not mean burning the king himself. Rashi and Metzudat David say it was the custom to burn a dead king's bed and the things he used. Radak says they burned spices on the bed, as was done for King Asa.

sources.quote: כָּךְ הָיָה דַּרְכָּם, לִשְׂרֹף עַל הַמְּלָכִים מִטָּתָן וּכְלֵי תַשְׁמִישָׁן
sources.says: Rashi says it was their custom to burn the kings' beds and the things they used.

sources.quote: כמו שהיו שורפים על מטתם בשמים וזנים מרוקחים כמו שנאמר באסא
sources.says: Radak says they used to burn spices and blended perfumes on their beds, as is said of Asa.

sources.quote: כי כן היה הדרך לשרוף על המלכים
sources.says: Metzudat David says this was the custom, to burn things for kings.

34:8.headline: Liberty "for them": for the slaves, or for everyone?
34:8.body: Radak says "them" means the slaves, who are named only in the next verse. Malbim reads it as the people themselves: the pact meant no one in Jerusalem would again fear being sold into slavery when poor.

sources.quote: לקרא להם דרור פירוש להם לעבדים ולשפחות כמו שאמר לשלח איש את עבדו וגו' ובא הכנוי טרם הידיעה
sources.says: Radak says "to them" means to the male and female slaves, as the next verse says; the word "them" comes before the people it refers to are named.

sources.quote: שדבר באזני העם שע"י ברית הזה יקראו לעצמם דרור, שעד עתה לא היה אחד מהם בטוח בעצמו פן יעני וימכר לעבד
sources.says: Malbim says the king told the people that through this pact they would proclaim liberty for themselves, since until then none of them was safe from becoming poor and being sold as a slave.

34:11.headline: Freed, then forced back: they seized their slaves again
34:11.body: Metzudat Zion says כבש means seizing by force. Malbim gives the background: during the siege the king feared the slaves would desert to Nebuchadnezzar, so they were freed. Once the siege lifted, their masters took them back.

sources.quote: ויכבשום. ענין התפיסה בחזקה כמו ויש מבנותינו נכבשות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means seizing by force, as in Nehemiah, "some of our daughters are forced".

sources.quote: ובעת המצור התירא המלך שימרדו אז לצאת אל נבוכדנצר כדי שיפטרו מעבדות ולכן כרתו ברית לשלחם
sources.says: Malbim says that during the siege the king feared the slaves would rebel and go over to Nebuchadnezzar to escape slavery, so they made a pact to free them.

sources.quote: ואחר שנסתלק המצור שבו והחזיקו בם לעבדים ושפחות
sources.says: Malbim says that after the siege lifted, they went back and held them as slaves.

sources.quote: אח״ז נתחרטו והחזירו את העבדים וכו׳, ותפשו בהם בחזקה
sources.says: Metzudat David says that afterward they regretted it, took the slaves back, and held them by force.

34:14.headline: "At the end of seven years" means after six
34:14.body: The next words say the slave serves six years and then goes free. So Metzudat David says מקץ here means the start of the seventh year: the beginning of a span can also be called its "end". Malbim also says the Torah required freeing him after six years.

sources.quote: מקץ. ר״ל מתחילה כי הראש יקרא קצה כמו הסוף
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means at the beginning, since the start of something is called its "end" just as its finish is.

sources.quote: לימי עבדותו וכאשר יפרש אחריו ועבדך שש שנים ואחר כך תשלחו חפשי
sources.says: Metzudat David says the seven years count his service, as the verse goes on to explain: he serves six years and then you set him free.

sources.quote: ממצות התורה הוזהרו לשלחו אחר שש שנים
sources.says: Malbim says the Torah commanded them to free him after six years.

34:17.headline: God answers in kind: "I proclaim your liberty" to the sword
34:17.body: They took back the liberty they had proclaimed for their slaves, so God proclaims "liberty" for them. Rashi and Metzudat David explain: God will no longer be their master to protect them, so they are left free for the sword, plague and famine. Malbim adds that one who serves God is free from chance, and one who leaves His service falls under it.

sources.quote: מֵאִתִּי, שֶׁאֵינִי אָדוֹן לָכֶם לְהַצִּיל, וְתִהְיוּ הֶפְקֵר אֶל הַחֶרֶב וְאֶל הָרָעָב
sources.says: Rashi says it means free from God: He is no longer their master to save them, and they will be left ownerless to the sword and famine.

sources.quote: ר״ל אתן אתכם חפשים ממני להיות מופקרים אל החרב וכו׳ ולא אהיה עוד אדון עליכם
sources.says: Metzudat David says God will set them free of Him, abandoned to the sword, and will no longer be their master.

sources.quote: כי מי שהוא עבד ה' הוא חפשי מן המקרים ואין דבר אחר שולט עליו, וכשיוצא חפשי מרשות ה' הוא תחת רשות המקרים
sources.says: Malbim says one who is God's servant is free from chance, and nothing else rules him; one who goes free of God's rule falls under the rule of chance.

34:18.headline: A calf cut in two: "so may the pact-breaker be cut"
34:18.body: Radak and Metzudat David say this was how a covenant was made, as in Abraham's covenant between the pieces: cut an animal in two and walk between the halves. Rashi explains what it meant: so may whoever breaks it be cut apart. He reads this pact darkly: when they took their slaves back, they swore together to rebel against God.

sources.quote: כן היא דרך כריתת הברית וכן ברית אברהם אבינו בין הבתרים
sources.says: Radak says this is the way a covenant is made, as in Abraham's covenant between the pieces.

sources.quote: שכרתו העגל לשני חלקים ועברו בין החלקים כי כן היה דרך כורתי ברית
sources.says: Metzudat David says they cut the calf into two parts and passed between them, for that was how people made a covenant.

sources.quote: וְהִיא הָיְתָה בְּרִית חֲזָקָה וּגְמוּרָה, לֵאמֹר: כָּכָה יִבָּתֵר וְיֵחָלֵק הָעוֹבֵר עָלֶיהָ
sources.says: Rashi says it was a strong and complete covenant, meaning: so may whoever breaks it be cut and divided.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁחָזְרוּ וְכָבְשׁוּם, כָּרְתוּ כֻּלָּם בְּרִית לִמְרוֹד בַּמָּקוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says that when they went back and seized the slaves, they all made a covenant to rebel against God.

34:18.headline: They "crossed" between the halves, and "crossed" the covenant
34:18.body: The verse uses the verb עבר twice. The men who "passed over" God's covenant, breaking it, are the same men who "passed" between the calf's halves to seal their pact. Metzudat Zion explains the first as "those who cancel". Targum Jonathan has "who transgressed My covenant".

sources.quote: העוברים. המבטלים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says העברים here means those who cancel.

sources.quote: דַעֲבָרוּ עַל קְיָמִי
sources.says: Targum Jonathan renders it "who transgressed My covenant".

sources.quote: וְכָרְתוּ הָעֵגֶל לִשְׁנַיִם וְעָבְרוּ בֵּין בְּתָרָיו
sources.says: Rashi says they cut the calf in two and passed between its pieces.

36:2.headline: Was the burned scroll the book of Lamentations? Ibn Ezra says no
36:2.body: Radak and the Metzudat David cite the sages: this scroll was the book of Lamentations. Ibn Ezra disagrees, because the king says the scroll spoke of the king of Babylon, and Lamentations never mentions Babylon or its king.

sources.quote: ורז"ל דרשו זו מגלת איכה
sources.says: Radak says the sages taught that this was the scroll of Lamentations.

sources.quote: ארז״ל שזאת היתה מגלת איכה
sources.says: The Metzudat David says the sages taught that this was the scroll of Lamentations.

sources.quote: ואיננה המגלה הנשרפת על יד יהויקים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Lamentations is not the scroll that Jehoiakim burned.

sources.quote: ואין במגילת ספר איכה זכר בבל ולא מלכה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the book of Lamentations makes no mention of Babylon or its king.

36:6.headline: A day of fasting, or a day of gathering?
36:6.body: The Metzudat Zion and Radak read צוֹם as a fast day. Radak reports that his father read it as an assembly, from צוֹמֶת, a meeting point, a day when people gathered to take counsel about their trouble.

sources.quote: צום. תענית
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says צום means a fast.

sources.quote: ואדני אבי ז"ל פירש ביום קבוץ מן צומת הגידין בדברי רבותינו ז"ל
sources.says: Radak says his father explained it as a day of gathering, from the rabbinic phrase for the place where the sinews meet.

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי ז"ל פירש צום קבוץ וכן ביום צום שבירמיהו
sources.says: Radak says his father explained צום as a gathering, here and in this verse of Jeremiah.

36:22.headline: The king's fire: a brazier, or logs that burn like brothers
36:22.body: Rashi says the plain sense is a brazier, but the sages heard אָח, brother, in it: logs that catch fire from one another like brothers. Malbim links it to אָחוּ, reeds that are dried and burned to start a fire.

sources.quote: פֵּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ (שבת כ.): עֵצִים; עַל שֵׁם שֶׁנִּדְלָקִים בְּאַחְוָה
sources.says: Rashi says the sages explained it as wood, named for catching fire in brotherhood.

sources.quote: וּלְפִי פְשׁוּטוֹ מַשְׁמַע שֶׁהוּא כְּלִי שֶׁמְּבַעֲרִין עָלָיו אוּר
sources.says: Rashi says the plain sense is a vessel on which a fire is lit.

sources.quote: הלשון ותרעינה באחו, מיבשים האחו ומבעיר בם את האש
sources.says: Malbim ties the word to אחו, reeds, which are dried and used to light the fire.

36:23.headline: 'Three or four doors': columns of the scroll, or verses?
36:23.body: Radak says the 'doors' are the columns of the scroll, which open and close like doors. Rashi gives the sages' reading, verses of Lamentations: the king shrugged off four, but when he heard 'her foes have become the head' he cut the scroll.

sources.quote: פירוש דפין כלומר דפי המגלה ונקראים דלתות לפי שנפתחים ונסגרים כדלתות
sources.says: Radak says the doors are the columns of the scroll, called doors because they open and close like doors.

sources.quote: וחז"ל פי' פסוקים, מפני שיש פתח והפסק בין פסוק לפסוק
sources.says: Malbim says the sages explained them as verses, because there is an opening and a break between one verse and the next.

sources.quote: אָמַר: מֵעַכְשָׁיו אֵינִי מֶלֶךְ; מִיָּד וַיִּקְרָעֶהָ בְּתַעַר הַסֹּפֵר
sources.says: Rashi says that when the king heard 'her foes have become the head' he said 'from now I am not king' and at once cut the scroll.

36:32.headline: 'Many words like them': a chapter where every letter comes three times
36:32.body: Rashi says the burned scroll held three alphabet poems of Lamentations. The rewritten scroll added chapter 3, where each letter opens three verses, so what was added was 'like them', three for three.

sources.quote: מִתְּחִלָּה הָיוּ שָׁלֹשׁ אַלְפָא בֵּיתִין
sources.says: Rashi says that at first there were three alphabet poems.

sources.quote: שֶׁכָּל אוֹת מְשֻׁלֶּשֶׁת בָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says Jeremiah added 'I am the man', in which every letter is tripled.

sources.quote: כי מתחלה אמר שלשה אלפ״א בית״א
sources.says: The Metzudat David says that at first Jeremiah said three alphabet poems.

37:1.headline: 'A king reigned': the one before him hardly counted
37:1.body: The verse says וימלך מלך, 'a king reigned', instead of just 'Zedekiah reigned'. Radak says the extra word is there because Jehoiachin ruled only three months and was not counted as a king.

sources.quote: לפי שמלכות יהויכין לא עמדה אלא ג' חדשים אמר וימלך מלך
sources.says: Radak says the text says 'a king reigned' because Jehoiachin's three-month rule did not count as kingship.

37:13.headline: The guard's grandfather was the false prophet Jeremiah opposed
37:13.body: The verse names the guard's grandfather, Hananiah. Rashi says he is Hananiah son of Azzur, the false prophet of chapter 28, and the sages tell that he ordered his family to trip up Jeremiah.

sources.quote: בֶּן בְּנוֹ הָיָה זֶה, וּלְכָךְ יִחֲסוֹ הַכָּתוּב
sources.says: Rashi says the guard was Hananiah's grandson, and that is why the text gives his family line.

sources.quote: צוה את בנו שאם יוכל להכשיל את ירמיהו יעשה
sources.says: Radak brings the teaching that Hananiah told his son to bring Jeremiah down if he could, and the order passed down to this grandson.

37:13.headline: 'You are falling to the Babylonians' means 'You are defecting'
37:13.body: נפל usually means to fall. Here it means to go over and join the enemy, as in 'let us fall to the camp of Aram' in 2 Kings 7:4.

sources.quote: רוצה לומר מתחבר ונשמע אליהם
sources.says: Radak says it means joining them and obeying them, as the Aramaic translation has it.

sources.quote: ענין הטיה זה התחברות כמו ונפלה אל מחנה ארם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means leaning toward and joining, as in 'let us fall to the camp of Aram'.

37:13.headline: Two ways to say 'seized', one for a runaway
37:13.body: Verse 13 says ויתפש את ירמיהו and verse 14 says ויתפש בירמיהו. Malbim says the first means catching someone who is running away, and the second means taking hold of him.

sources.quote: תפש שאחריו את משתתף עם לכידה שתופש את הבורח
sources.says: Malbim says תפש followed by את means capturing someone who flees, and followed by ב means grabbing hold.

37:19.headline: The written word asks 'where is it?', the promise itself
37:19.body: The text is read ואיה, 'and where are', but written ואיו, 'and where is it'. Radak says the written form asks where the thing your prophets promised has gone.

sources.quote: ואיו כתיב רוצה לומר איו הדבר שהבטחתם בו מפי נביאכם
sources.says: Radak says the written איו means 'where is the thing you were promised by your prophets'.

39:2.headline: The city 'split open', the walls or the starving people
39:2.body: הבקעה says the city was broken open. Metzudat David says the walls gave way almost by themselves, since the people were too weak from hunger to resist. Malbim reads it of the people: hunger made them break out to surrender to Babylon.

sources.quote: בקעו חומתה כאלו נעשית מעצמה כי אנשי ירושלים היו חלושים ברעב
sources.says: Metzudat David says the army broke the wall as if it happened by itself, because the people were weak with hunger.

sources.quote: נבקעו העם לצאת אל מלך בבל
sources.says: Malbim says hunger made the people break out to go over to the king of Babylon.

39:5.headline: Nebuchadnezzar 'spoke judgments' with Zedekiah: he argued his case
39:5.body: The verse says the king spoke משפטים, judgments, with Zedekiah. Metzudat Zion says here it means arguing. Rashi says Nebuchadnezzar demanded: why did you break your oath?

sources.quote: משפטים. ענין ויכוח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word here means an argument.

sources.quote: לָמָּה עָבַרְתָּ עַל הַשְּׁבוּעָה
sources.says: Rashi says the king asked why Zedekiah broke his oath.

sources.quote: על שמרד בו והפר בריתו ועבר על שבועת
sources.says: Radak says it was about his rebellion, his broken treaty and his broken oath.

39:6.headline: Judah's nobles, or the court that freed Zedekiah from his oath
39:6.body: Nebuchadnezzar killed all the חרי, the nobles, of Judah. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as officers and rulers. Rashi says they were the Sanhedrin, punished for releasing Zedekiah from his oath.

sources.quote: אֵלּוּ הַסַּנְהֶדְרִין, עַל שֶׁהִתִּירוּ לוֹ אֶת שְׁבוּעָתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says these were the Sanhedrin, because they released Zedekiah from his oath.

sources.quote: קציני יהודה ושריו
sources.says: Radak says they were Judah's officers and princes.

sources.quote: חורי. ענין שררה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means rulers.

39:8.headline: 'The house of the people': their homes, or the synagogue
39:8.body: The Babylonians burned בית העם, the house of the people. Radak reads it as the people's houses in general. Rashi, and a midrash in Radak, say it means the synagogue.

sources.quote: כמו בתי העם דרך כלל, ובדרש ואת בית העם זה בית הכנסת
sources.says: Radak says it means the people's houses in general, and the midrash says it is the synagogue.

sources.quote: וְאֶת בֵּית הָעָם. בָּתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the house of the people means the synagogues.

39:10.headline: Fields to dig, or wine vats: a word found only here
39:10.body: The poor were given vineyards and יגבים. Rashi says fields to work, since the word means digging. Radak agrees: fields, and field workers are called יוגבים. Metzudat Zion reads it as יקבים, wine vats, since ג and ק can swap.

sources.quote: שָׂדוֹת לְעָבְדָם. כָּל יְגִיבָה לְשׁוֹן חֲפִירָה
sources.says: Rashi says they are fields to work, since the word means digging.

sources.quote: וכן נקראו עובדי השדות יוגבים
sources.says: Radak says they are fields, and the men who work fields are called יוגבים.

sources.quote: כמו ויקבים כי גיכ״ק מתחלף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is like יקבים, wine vats, because ג and ק interchange.

4:1.headline: The second תשוב means "rest" in Radak, not "return"
4:1.body: Rashi takes both as return, the second back to your first glory. Radak says the second תשוב means rest, like "in return and rest you shall be saved".

sources.quote: אֵלַי תָּשׁוּב לִכְבוֹדְךָ וּגְדֻלָּתְךָ הָרִאשׁוֹנָה
sources.says: Rashi says the second תשוב is a return to your first honor and greatness.

sources.quote: תשוב השני ענין מנוחה כמו בשובה ונחת תושעון
sources.says: Radak says the second תשוב means rest, like "in returning and rest you shall be saved".

4:2.headline: בו in "the nations will bless themselves by him": God or Israel?
4:2.body: Radak first reads "him" as God: the nations will bless themselves by Him and not by idols. He allows that it may mean Israel, and Rashi and Jonathan read it that way.

sources.quote: ויתכן לפרש כנוי בו שב לישראל כלומר אם תעשה כל זה יתברכו הגוים בך
sources.says: Radak says the word בו may refer to Israel, so the nations will bless themselves by you.

sources.quote: אִם תַּעֲשׂוּ כֵּן, אָז יִתְבָּרְכוּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַגּוֹיִם
sources.says: Rashi says that if you do so, the nations will bless themselves by Israel.

sources.quote: וְיִתְבָּרְכוּן עַמְמַיָא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Jonathan translates it as "the nations will be blessed through Israel".

4:2.headline: יתהללו: they will praise, or they will boast of belonging to Israel
4:2.body: Rashi gives two readings: they will tell of your praise, or whoever can cling to Israel will take pride in it. Metzudat David reads it as each one boasting "I am as blessed as Israel".

sources.quote: יַגִּידוּ שִׁבְחֲכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says יתהללו means they will tell your praise.

sources.quote: מִי שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִדָּבֵק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, יִתְפָּאֵר בַּדָּבָר
sources.says: Rashi gives a second reading: whoever can cling to Israel will take pride in it.

sources.quote: המהלל עצמו יאמר הנה אני מוצלח כישראל
sources.says: Metzudat David says the one boasting will say "I am as fortunate as Israel".

4:4.headline: The "foreskin of the heart" is a covering that blocks feeling
4:4.body: Metzudat Zion says ערלה here means a blockage. Malbim says it is a cover wrapped around the heart so that it cannot feel or wake up.

sources.quote: ערלות. ענין אוטם וכן ערלי לב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ערלות means a blockage, like "uncircumcised of heart".

sources.quote: ערלת הלב המכסה והמעטיף את הלב מהרגיש
sources.says: Malbim says the foreskin of the heart is what covers and wraps the heart so it cannot feel.

sources.quote: זאת היא מילת הלב
sources.says: Radak says this is the circumcision of the heart.

4:5.headline: הגידו is telling quietly; השמיעו is telling in public
4:5.body: Malbim's word list says מגיד is to tell in private, and משמיע is to announce in public. Here the verse tells Judah, then announces in Jerusalem.

sources.quote: המגיד הוא בצינעה, והמשמיע הוא בפרהסיא
sources.says: Malbim says מגיד is to tell in private and משמיע is to announce in public.

4:6.headline: העיזו means gather, but Malbim says gather to a strong place
4:6.body: Rashi ties it to "send in (העז) your livestock" in Exodus 9:19, so it means gather. Malbim says it differs from the other gathering words, since it is gathering to a place of strength.

sources.quote: הֵאָסְפוּ, כְּמוֹ ״שְׁלַח הָעֵז
sources.says: Rashi says העיזו means gather, like "send in your livestock" in Exodus 9:19.

sources.quote: הבדלו מן אסף כנס ודומיהן, שנאסף למקום עוז וחזק
sources.says: Malbim says העיזו is set apart from the other gathering words, since it means gathered to a place of strength.

4:7.headline: תצינה: laid waste, or sprouting? Radak's father reads it as sprouting
4:7.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion tie it to ציה, a dry waste, so the cities are laid waste. Radak's father ties it to "the pomegranates have budded (הנצו)", so ruined cities sprout grass and weeds.

sources.quote: תִּצֶּינָה. לְשׁוֹן ״צִיָּה
sources.says: Rashi says תצינה comes from ציה, a dry waste.

sources.quote: תצינה. מלשון ציה ושממון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says תצינה is from ציה, dry and desolate.

sources.quote: ואאז"ל פי' תצמחנה מענין הנצו הרמונים ויהיה לפי זה הפתרון שנים שרשים וענין אחד והערים החרבות יצמיחו דשאים ועשבים
sources.says: Radak says his father read it as "they will sprout", from "the pomegranates have budded", so the ruined cities grow grass and weeds.

4:9.headline: ונשמו: be astonished, or be left empty and idle
4:9.body: Metzudat Zion says it means astonishment, like "they were astonished at his day". Radak says the priests will be left desolate, since their service has stopped, and Jonathan translates it as "will be laid waste".

sources.quote: ענין תמהון כמו על יומו נשמו
