sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ונשמו means astonishment, like "they were astonished at his day" in Job 18:20.

sources.quote: ואז יהיו נשמים כי בטלה עבודתם
sources.says: Radak says the priests will be left desolate, since their service has ended.

sources.quote: וְיִצְדוּן כַּהֲנַיָא
sources.says: Jonathan translates it as "the priests will be laid waste".

4:10.headline: Jeremiah says God "deceived" the people, using Eve's word
4:10.body: The verb is the one Eve used: "the serpent deceived me". Radak softens it: by holding back from the false prophets, it is as if God is the one deceiving them.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן ״הַנָּחָשׁ הִשִּׁיאַנִי
sources.says: Rashi says the verb is like "the serpent deceived me" in Genesis 3:13.

sources.quote: ענין הסתה והפתוי כמו הנחש השיאני
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says השא means inciting and enticing, like "the serpent deceived me".

sources.quote: כאילו אתה משיא אותם
sources.says: Radak says that since God holds back from the false prophets, it is as if He were deceiving the people.

4:16.headline: נצרים: besiegers, or Nebuchadnezzar's army, named for his name
4:16.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion say besiegers. Radak says it means Nebuchadnezzar's army, called after his name (נבוכדנצר), and notes that Jonathan reads it like "pickers".

sources.quote: נוֹתְנֵי מָצוֹר עֲלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says נוצרים are those who lay siege.

sources.quote: ופירוש נוצרים חיל נבוכדנצר ונקראו על שמו
sources.says: Radak says נוצרים is Nebuchadnezzar's army, called after his name.

sources.quote: וי"ת נוצרים כמו בוצרים בבי"ת שתרגם משרית עממיא חטופין כקטופין
sources.says: Radak says Jonathan translates נוצרים like בוצרים, "seizers like pickers".

sources.quote: יש הבדל בין נוצר לשומר
sources.says: Malbim says there is a difference between a נוצר and a שומר, and נוצרים applies to a city under siege.

4:19.headline: המיה, "stirring", is said only of the heart
4:19.body: Maimonides says the word for stirring is said only of the heart among all the organs. Malbim adds that the gut reacts by nature, to fear and grief, while the heart stirs over things a person can change.

sources.quote: ולשון המיה נאמר רק בלב מכל שאר האברים
sources.says: Maimonides says the language of stirring is said only of the heart, among all the organs, and cites "my heart stirs within me".

sources.quote: יש הבדל בין התחלחלות המעיים להמיית הלב, כי המעיים לא יתפעלו רק מן הטבע מן הפחד והיגון אשר אין בחירת האדם יכול עליו, והלב יתפעל מן הרצון ויהמה על דבר שאדם יכול עליו לשנותו לקרבו או לרחקו
sources.says: Malbim says the gut trembles by nature, from fear and grief, while the heart stirs over what a person can change.

4:19.headline: "My soul heard", not my ear: the prophet hears in vision
4:19.body: Radak says it says נפשי and not "my ears", because the enemy had not yet come. His soul heard the shofar in prophecy. Rashi says the news came from behind the curtain, as in the Talmud.

sources.quote: אמר נפשי ולא אמר אזני כי עדיין לא שמעו אזניו כי עדיין לא בא האויב אבל נפשו שמעה בנבואה
sources.says: Radak says it says נפשי and not "my ears" because the enemy had not come yet, and his soul heard it in prophecy.

sources.quote: מֵאֲחוֹרֵי הַפַּרְגּוֹד (חגיגה טו.) בָּאַתְנִי בְּשׂוֹרַת קוֹל מִתְּרוּעַת מִלְחָמָה
sources.says: Rashi says the news of the sound of battle came to him from behind the curtain, citing Hagigah 15a.

4:20.headline: נקרא is "happens", although spelled with an alef
4:20.body: The word usually means "is called". Metzudat Zion and Radak read it as "befalls", from מקרה, even though it is spelled with an alef.

sources.quote: נקרא. מל׳ מקרה ועם הוא באל״ף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נקרא is from מקרה, a happening, though it is spelled with an alef.

sources.quote: נקרא. ענין מקרה אע"פ שהוא באל"ף
sources.says: Radak says נקרא means a happening, even though it is written with an alef.

4:22.headline: Maimonides: חכמה has four senses, and here it is cunning
4:22.body: In the Guide, חכמה can mean knowing truths, a craft, fine character, or cunning. This verse, "wise to do evil", is his example of the last.

sources.quote: המונח "חכמה" מציין בעברית ארבע משמעויות
sources.says: Maimonides says the word חכמה has four meanings in Hebrew.

sources.quote: והוא מציין תחכום וערמה: "הָבָה נִתְחַכְּמָה לוֹ" (שמות א,י). לפי משמעות זו נאמר: "וַיִּקַּח מִשָּׁם אִשָּׁה חֲכָמָה" (שמואל־ב יד,ב), כלומר בעלת תחכום וערמה. ובמשמעות זו גם: "חֲכָמִים הֵמָּה לְהָרַע
sources.says: Maimonides says the fourth meaning is cunning and craftiness, and gives "they are wise to do evil" as an example.

4:23.headline: Maimonides quotes "formless and void" as the fall of Jerusalem
4:23.body: These are the words from the story of creation. Radak says the land is called that because it is desolate and empty of people, as at the beginning, and Maimonides quotes the verses as Jeremiah's picture of Jerusalem's fall.

sources.quote: ירמיה אמר בתיאור חורבן ירושלם בעֲוֹנוֹת אבותינו: "רָאִיתִי אֶת הָאָרֶץ וְהִנֵּה תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ [וְאֶל הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֵין אוֹרָם. רָאִיתִי הֶהָרִים וְהִנֵּה רֹעֲשִׁים וְכָל הַגְּבָעוֹת הִתְקַלְקָלוּ. רָאִיתִי וְהִנֵּה אֵין הָאָדָם וְכָל עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם נָדָדוּ. רָאִיתִי וְהִנֵּה הַכַּרְמֶל הַמִּדְבָּר, וְכָל עָרָיו נִתְּצוּ מִפְּנֵי ה' מִפְּנֵי חֲרוֹן אַפּוֹ]" (ירמיה ד,כג-כו
sources.says: Maimonides quotes "I saw the earth, and it was formless and void" as Jeremiah's description of the destruction of Jerusalem.

sources.quote: כתרגומו צדיא וחרובא כיון שהיא שממה ואין יושבין עליה הרי היא כתהו ובהו כמו בתחילת בריאתה
sources.says: Radak says the land is like תהו ובהו because it is desolate and has no one living on it, as at the beginning of creation.

4:23.headline: ואל השמים: "and the heavens", or "toward the heavens"?
4:23.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion say אל stands for את, so "I saw the heavens". Malbim says ראה takes את, so אל means he could not see the heavens themselves in the darkness, only look up toward them.

sources.quote: כמו ואת השמים וכן אספרה אל חק
sources.says: Radak says אל here is like את, as in "I will tell of the decree".

sources.quote: כמו ואת השמים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ואל השמים is like ואת השמים.

sources.quote: פעל ראה נקשר תמיד עם מלת את, ופה ר"ל שלא ראה השמים עצמם מפני החשך רק ראה אליהם אל הרום
sources.says: Malbim says ראה always goes with את, so here it means he did not see the heavens themselves because of the darkness, but looked up toward the height.

4:24.headline: התקלקלו: ruined, or shaken loose and made light
4:24.body: Metzudat Zion reads it as ruin. Rashi says the hills were torn from their places and flung, like "he shook the arrows". Radak's father says it comes from קלות, lightness: they shook because of how light they were.

sources.quote: ענין השחתה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says התקלקלו means ruin.

sources.quote: נִתְּקוּ וְנִזְרְקוּ מִמְּקוֹמָן; וְעִם ״קַלְקַל בַּחִצִּים״ (יחזקאל כא:כו) חִבְּרוֹ מְנַחֵם
sources.says: Rashi says they were torn from their places and thrown, and Menachem linked it to "he shook the arrows".

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי ז"ל פי' ענין קלות כלומר רעשו מרוב קלותם כי כבדותם יעמידם
sources.says: Radak says his father read it as lightness: they shook from their lightness, since their heaviness would hold them still.

4:24.headline: Rashi: the mountains are the patriarchs, the hills the matriarchs
4:24.body: A midrash that Rashi quotes reads "the mountains" as the fathers and "the hills" as the mothers. Their merit has run out.

sources.quote: רָאִיתִי הֶהָרִים אֵלּוּ הָאָבוֹת, וְכָל הַגְּבָעוֹת אֵלּוּ אִמָּהוֹת (ראש השנה יא.), כְּלוֹמַר זְכוּתָן תַּמָּה
sources.says: Rashi quotes a midrash that the mountains are the fathers and the hills the mothers, meaning their merit has run out.

4:29.headline: פרש: horsemen as a group, or one horseman (Malbim)
4:29.body: Radak says the singular stands for many, like "I have an ox and a donkey". Malbim says he reads it plainly as one horseman, and "the whole city" as Jerusalem.

sources.quote: לשון יחיד על רבים דרך כלל כמו ויהי לי שור וחמור
sources.says: Radak says the singular stands for many in general, like "I have an ox and a donkey".

sources.quote: לדעת המפרשים הוא שם המין ר"ל פרשים
sources.says: Malbim says the commentators take פרש as the name of the kind, meaning horsemen.

sources.quote: ולפירושי הוא כפשוטו פרש אחד, וכן כל העיר ירושלים
sources.says: Malbim says in his own reading it is plainly one horseman, and the whole city is Jerusalem.

4:29.headline: כפים are rocks, as the Aramaic word for rock, כיפא, shows
4:29.body: Rashi notes that the Targum translates "rock" as כיפא, and Metzudat Zion ties כפים to the same word. Malbim says it names high, bent rocks, related to כפף, to bend.

sources.quote: סֶלַע״ (ירמיה כג:כט) מְתֻרְגָּם ״בְּכִיפַיָּא
sources.says: Rashi says the Targum translates "rock" as כיפא.

sources.quote: תרגום של סלע היא כיפא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the Aramaic for "rock" is כיפא, and cites "holes of the dust and the rocks" in Job 30:6.

sources.quote: סלעים גבוהים וכפופים וחברו חורי עפר וכיפים (איוב ל׳:ו׳) ומשתתף עם כפף
sources.says: Malbim says כפים are high, bent rocks, related to כפף.

4:30.headline: תקרעי: "tear" is used for painting the eyes
4:30.body: The word means to tear, but here it is about eye paint. Rashi says the paint makes the opening of the eye look wider, as if torn open.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן קְרִיעָה, שֶׁהַפּוּךְ נִרְאֶה כְּמַרְחִיב קֶרַע הָעַיִן
sources.says: Rashi says the paint makes the eye's opening look torn wider.

sources.quote: מרוב ההתמדה לכחול העינים נראה כאלו קורעת פתיחת בית העין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says from constantly painting the eyes it looks as if she tears open the socket.

sources.quote: תכחלין ואמר בלשון קריעה כי היא קורעת עיניה מרוב התמדתה לכחול אותם
sources.says: Radak says Jonathan translates it as "paint", and that she is said to tear her eyes because of how much she keeps painting them.

44:17.headline: 'Queen of heaven' or 'work of heaven'? Two readings of one word
44:17.body: Radak reads מְלֶכֶת as מְלֶאכֶת with the א missing: the 'work of heaven', meaning the stars God made. Others, like the Metzudat David, take it from מֶלֶךְ, king: the sun, which rules the other stars.

sources.quote: רוצה לומר למעשה השמים והם הכוכבים מלאכת האל יתברך והוא חסר אל"ף
sources.says: Radak says it means the work of heaven, the stars that God made, with the letter א missing.

sources.quote: ויש מפרשים למלכת משרש מלך
sources.says: Radak says others take the word from the root for king.

sources.quote: לכוכב גדול שבשמים הוא השמש וכאלו מולך על כולם
sources.says: The Metzudat David says it is the great star in the sky, the sun, as if it reigns over all the others.

sources.quote: לְכוֹכְבַת שְׁמַיָא
sources.says: Targum Jonathan translates: the star of heaven.

44:17.headline: 'We were good': well fed, well off, or good before God?
44:17.body: Radak, writing on Genesis, says טוֹבִים here means well fed, the way a calf is called good when it is fat. The Metzudat David says it means rich, and Malbim says they meant good in God's eyes, since they did not think their incense denied God.

sources.quote: וְהָיָה גַּם כֵּן טוֹב, רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר שָׁמֵן
sources.says: Radak says good here means fat, and cites this verse as another example.

sources.quote: ר״ל עשירים ומלאים טוב
sources.says: The Metzudat David says it means rich and full of good things.

sources.quote: ובכ"ז ונהיה טובים ר"ל טובים לאלהים, כי לא היה בזה הכחשה לאל ממעל
sources.says: Malbim says they meant good toward God, since in their view this did not deny God above.

44:19.headline: 'To sadden her' means to please her, or to make her image
44:19.body: The Metzudat Zion and Radak say 'to sadden her' is a polite reversal that really means to make her glad. Malbim instead takes the word from עֲצַבִּים, idols.

sources.quote: מלשון עצבון והוא דרך כנוי על השמחה
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says the word is from sadness, used in a reversed way for joy.

sources.quote: על דרך הכנוי רוצה לומר לשמחה
sources.says: Radak says it is a reversed expression that means to gladden her.

sources.quote: להעציבה מענין עצבים
sources.says: Malbim says the word comes from the sense of idols.

44:23.headline: The evil 'happened' to you: the prophet borrows the word for chance
44:23.body: Malbim says קָרָאת comes from מִקְרֶה, an event with no cause or purpose behind it. He says the people believed the disaster was mere chance, because God had not punished them at once.

sources.quote: קראת. מלשון מקרה
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says the word comes from chance happening.

sources.quote: מענין מקרה, וגדר המקרה שבא בלא סבה ובלא כונת מכוון
sources.says: Malbim says it is from chance, which means something that comes without a cause and without anyone intending it.

sources.quote: תחשבו היום שהרעה באה לכם במקרה ולא בהשגחה
sources.says: Malbim says they think the evil came to them by chance and not by God watching over them.

46:2.headline: Pharaoh Necho: 'the lame one,' or just his name?
46:2.body: The Targum calls him "Pharaoh the lame," reading נכו like נכה רגלים, lame in the feet. Ibn Ezra holds that נכה is simply his personal name, and sets aside a midrash about Solomon's throne.

sources.quote: פַרְעֹה חֲגִירָא
sources.says: The Targum renders the name as "Pharaoh the lame."

sources.quote: תירגם יונתן חגירא וכן בן נכה רגלים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion notes the Targum's "the lame" and compares "a son lame in the feet."

sources.quote: כי נכה שם העצם, ואל יקשה עליך דרש כסא שלמה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Pharaoh is a title and נכה is the king's own name, and the midrash about Solomon's throne should not trouble you.

46:3.headline: Two kinds of shield
46:3.body: The verse names both a מגן and a צנה. Rashi says the מגן was leather, oiled before battle, and the צנה was wood, while Malbim says one stopped arrows and the other stopped swords and spears.

sources.quote: שֶׁל עוֹר הוּא, וְהוּא שָׁלוּק; וּכְשֶׁיּוֹצֵא לַמִּלְחָמָה מוֹשְׁחוֹ בְּשֶׁמֶן
sources.says: Rashi says the מגן is made of boiled leather, and a soldier oils it when he goes to war.

sources.quote: שֶׁל עֵץ, דְּמוּת תְּרִיסִין שֶׁלָּנוּ
sources.says: Rashi says the צנה is made of wood, like the shields of his own day.

sources.quote: מגן מפני קשת, וצנה מפני חרב וחנית ומקיף מג' רוחות
sources.says: Malbim says the מגן guards against arrows, and the צנה against sword and spear, covering three sides.

46:5.headline: Terror all around, or enemies gathering all around?
46:5.body: מגור מסביב usually means terror on every side. Radak notes that the Targum reads מגור as gathering: enemies closing in on every side.

sources.quote: ענין פחד כמו ויגר מואב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means fear, as in "Moab was afraid."

sources.quote: ויונתן תרגם מגור ענין אסיפה
sources.says: Radak says the Targum translated מגור as gathering.

sources.quote: דְמִתְכַּנְשִׁין עֲלֵיכוֹן מִסְחוֹר סְחוֹר
sources.says: The Targum speaks of those who gather against them from all around.

46:9.headline: Not boasting, but racing about like madmen
46:9.body: The verb looks like הלל, to praise or boast, but the commentators read it from הוללות, madness. The chariots race back and forth so wildly they look insane.

sources.quote: והוללות הרכב הוא מרוצת הסוסים רצוא ושוב ודהירתם שידמה הוללות ושגעון
sources.says: Radak says the chariots' madness is the horses running back and forth and galloping, which looks like madness.

sources.quote: כי ברוב המרוצה נראים כמשתגעים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from the word for madness, since in their great speed they look mad.

sources.quote: וְהִתְהוֹלְלוּ. לְשׁוֹן סִכְלוּת
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word for folly.

46:10.headline: Revenge for King Josiah
46:10.body: The verse calls the battle a day of God's revenge. Radak says it is revenge for Josiah, king of Judah, whom Pharaoh Necho killed at Megiddo.

sources.quote: נקמת יאשיהו המלך שהמיתו פרעה נכה במגדו
sources.says: Radak says it is revenge for King Josiah, whom Pharaoh Necho killed at Megiddo.

sources.quote: לקח השם יתבר' נקמת יאשיהו המלך ממנו
sources.says: Radak says that while Necho was at Carchemish, God took revenge on him for King Josiah.

46:11.headline: Why Egypt is called a virgin
46:11.body: Egypt is called בתולת בת מצרים, the virgin daughter of Egypt. Metzudat David says it is because no nation had yet conquered her.

sources.quote: קראה בתולה על שלא נכבשה עדיין משום אומה
sources.says: Metzudat David says she is called a virgin because no nation had yet conquered her.

46:11.headline: No cure, or no strength left in the bones?
46:11.body: תעלה here means healing, and Radak says the medicine stands for Egypt's allies. Malbim reads it as the marrow and natural moisture of the body: Egypt has no strength left for any medicine to work on.

sources.quote: ענין רפואה כמו רפואות תעלה אין לך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means healing.

sources.quote: והרפואה היא משל על עזרת העוזרים כמו כוש פוט ולוד
sources.says: Radak says the healing is a figure for help from allies like Cush, Put and Lud.

sources.quote: המוח שבעצמות ולחות הטבעי
sources.says: Malbim says תעלה is the marrow in the bones and the body's natural moisture.

46:16.headline: The sword of the dove, or the cruel sword?
46:16.body: חרב היונה looks like "the sword of the dove." Malbim says Assyria and Babylon flew a dove on their banners, while Rashi and Radak read it as the oppressing sword, and the Targum as a sword that makes men reel like wine.

sources.quote: ידוע שמלכי אשור ובבל היה להם צורת יונה על דגלם
sources.says: Malbim says the kings of Assyria and Babylon had a dove on their banners and credited their victories to it.

sources.quote: הַיּוֹנָה לְשׁוֹן יַיִן. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: לְשׁוֹן אוֹנָאָה
sources.says: Rashi brings the Targum, which reads it as wine, a sword like intoxicating wine, and another reading, oppression.

sources.quote: היונה. האונסת כי אין מי שיעמוד כנגדה
sources.says: Radak says it means the sword that overpowers, since no one can stand against it.

46:17.headline: A mocking name for Pharaoh: 'Noise'
46:17.body: The soldiers give Pharaoh a new name: "Noise, who let the appointed time pass." Rashi says he boasted loudly of his armies, set a day for battle, and then never came out.

sources.quote: בַּמִּלְחָמָה הִכְרִיזוּ מָשָׁל שֶׁל חֶרְפָּה
sources.says: Rashi says in the war they proclaimed a name of disgrace for him.

sources.quote: שֶׁיִּעֵד הַיּוֹם מִלְחָמָה קָבוּעַ לָצֵאת וּלְהִלָּחֵם וְלֹא יָצָא
sources.says: Rashi says he set a fixed day to go out and fight, and did not go out.

sources.quote: ומלך עומד במקום שנים מלך מצרים ומלך שאון
sources.says: Radak says the word king does double duty: king of Egypt, and king of noise.

46:18.headline: As sure as Mount Tabor, or trapped like game on Tabor?
46:18.body: Rashi reads it as an oath: as surely as Mount Tabor stands among the mountains, this will happen. Radak's father reads a picture instead: Tabor was where hunters spread nets, and Carmel's timber was shipped by sea, so Egypt will be trapped and carried off.

sources.quote: כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר דְּבַר אֱמֶת הוּא שֶׁתָּבוֹר קָבוּעַ בֶּהָרִים
sources.says: Rashi says as true as it is that Tabor is fixed among the mountains and Carmel by the sea, so truly this will come on Egypt.

sources.quote: כמו שהר תבור הוא מועד לצוד שם ולפרוש שם רשתות
sources.says: Radak cites his father: as Mount Tabor is a place to hunt and spread nets, so they will be caught.

sources.quote: כמו עצי הכרמל שמביאים בים כן יביאו אותם בשביה
sources.says: Radak says as Carmel's wood is brought by sea, so they will be brought into captivity.

46:20.headline: Egypt the heifer, and the bull it worshipped
46:20.body: Egypt is called a heifer. Malbim says Egypt worshipped a bull at Memphis, and Radak says the heifer in Abraham's covenant hinted at the exile in Egypt, since Egypt is called a heifer here.

sources.quote: מצרים היו מכבדים ומעריצים את השור שיחסו לו אלהות, והוא עמד בנוף
sources.says: Malbim says the Egyptians revered a bull as a god, kept at Memphis, and the Chaldeans killed it when Memphis fell.

sources.quote: רָמַז בּוֹ לְגָלוּת רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁהוּא גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁנִּקְרָא עֶגְלָה
sources.says: Radak says the heifer in Abraham's covenant hinted at the first exile, in Egypt, which is called a heifer in this verse.

46:20.headline: 'Very beautiful,' with a hint at the bull's mouth
46:20.body: יפה־פיה is one word with letters doubled, meaning very beautiful. Malbim adds a hint: פיה also sounds like "her mouth," and the bull Egypt worshipped had a special mark on its mouth.

sources.quote: פתרונו כמלה אחת ור״ל יפה ביותר ולזה נכפל העי״ן והלמ״ד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is one word meaning very beautiful, with letters doubled to show it.

sources.quote: בהשור שבחרו לאלהות היה להם סימן מיוחד בפיו, לכן אמר שפיו יפה
sources.says: Malbim says the bull they chose as a god had a special mark on its mouth, so the verse says its mouth is beautiful.

46:20.headline: A cut from the north, or a sign from the north?
46:20.body: קרץ appears only here. Rashi reads it as cutting, a slaughter coming from the north, while Malbim adds it can mean a wink or sign, since the Egyptians read omens in how their sacred bull moved.

sources.quote: קֶרֶץ לְשׁוֹן חִתּוּךְ
sources.says: Rashi says קרץ is a word for cutting, and the Targum has "killing nations."

sources.quote: ויל"פ מענין רמז כמו קורץ בעיניו, כי המצרים היו מנחשים ע"י תהלוכות השור
sources.says: Malbim says it may mean a hint, like winking, since the Egyptians divined by the bull's movements.

46:21.headline: Her hired soldiers, or her great men?
46:21.body: שכריה looks like "her hired men," and Radak reads it as mercenaries. Rashi and the Targum read it as "her great ones," her officers.

sources.quote: גייסות ששכרו לעזרם
sources.says: Radak says these are troops they hired to help them.

sources.quote: שְׂכִירֶיהָ. שָׂרֶיהָ
sources.says: Rashi says it means her officers, as in "the great razor" in Isaiah.

sources.quote: אַף רַבְרְבָהָא בְגַוָהּ
sources.says: The Targum renders it "also her great ones within her."

46:22.headline: A voice that walks like a snake
46:22.body: Egypt's voice "walks" like a snake. Maimonides says walking is borrowed here for something spreading that has no body at all, and Rashi brings a teaching that when God cut off the snake's legs, its voice went out to the end of the world.

sources.quote: לאחר מכן הושאל להתפשטות דבר כלשהו והופעתו, גם אם אין הוא גשמי כלל
sources.says: Maimonides says walking was borrowed for the spreading of something even when it has no body at all, and cites this verse.

sources.quote: וְקִטֵּעַ אֶת רַגְלָיו וְהָלַךְ קוֹלוֹ בְּסוֹף הָעוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi says we learn from here that when God cut off the snake's legs, its voice traveled to the end of the world.

sources.quote: ציור הנחש הוא שהיו לו רגלים ונקצצו ע"י חטאו
sources.says: Malbim says the snake once had legs that were cut off for its sin, a picture of Egypt cut off from going beyond its land.

46:28.headline: 'Not leave you unpunished,' or 'not wipe you out'?
46:28.body: ונקה לא אנקך can be read "I will not leave you unpunished." Rashi and Metzudat David read it as wiping out: God will punish Israel, but will not clear the world of them.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן טִיאוּט וְהַשְׁמֵד
sources.says: Rashi says ונקה is a word for sweeping away and destroying, as the Targum renders it.

sources.quote: ולא אנקה אותך מן העולם שישאר העולם נקי ממך
sources.says: Metzudat David says God will not clear you out of the world so that the world is empty of you.

48:2.headline: Madmen will be 'cut off', a play on its own name
48:2.body: The town מדמן is told תדמי, you will be cut off or silenced. The verb echoes the town's name. Radak and Metzudat David both call it a play on words.

sources.quote: גם העיר מדמן תהיה נכרתה וגם הוא לשון נופל על לשון
sources.says: Metzudat David says the town Madmen will be cut off, and that this too is a play on words.

sources.quote: ענין כריתה כמו נדמתה אשקלון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says תדמי means being cut off, as in 'Ashkelon is cut off'.

sources.quote: לשון נופל על הלשון הוא צחות הלשון וכן מדמן תדמי
sources.says: Radak counts 'Madmen will be silenced' as a play on words.

48:4.headline: Moab's 'little ones': children, rulers, or the town of Zoar
48:4.body: צעיריה means 'her small ones'. Metzudat David reads it as children taken captive. The Aramaic Targum reads it as rulers, and Radak suggests the great are called small as an insult. Malbim reads it as the people of the town Zoar.

sources.quote: הבנים הקטנים שהלכו בשבי
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means the small children who went into captivity.

sources.quote: ותרגם יונתן שלטניהון ואפשר שכנה הכתוב הגדולים בלשון צעירים על דרך גנאי
sources.says: Radak says the Targum renders it 'their rulers', and that the verse may call the great ones 'little' to shame them.

sources.quote: אנשי עיר צוער
sources.says: Malbim says it means the people of the town of Zoar.

48:7.headline: Moab trusted its 'works', meaning its flocks and herds
48:7.body: מעשה usually means a deed or work. Metzudat Zion and Radak say here it means livestock, because a herdsman's whole work is his animals.

sources.quote: כן יקרא מקנה הבקר והצאן כי העוסק במקנה כל מעשהו בהם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says cattle and sheep are called this, since a herdsman spends all his work on them.

sources.quote: במקניך ובקניניך וכן ואיש במעון ומעשיהו בכרמל
sources.says: Radak says it means your livestock and property, as with Nabal, whose 'work' was in Carmel.

48:9.headline: 'Go out' here is read as 'fly away' on feathers
48:9.body: נצא תצא looks like 'you will surely go out'. Rashi and Radak read it from נצה, feathers or flight, so Moab will fly off into exile.

sources.quote: וְיִהְיֶה נֵצֵא מִגְּזֵרַת נִצָּהּ, כֵּן חָבְרוּ מְנַחֵם
sources.says: Rashi says Menachem placed נצא with נצה, flight, so Moab will go into exile in haste.

sources.quote: זהו שאמר כי נצא תצא ענינו כי עוף תעוף
sources.says: Radak says it means 'you will surely fly away'.

sources.quote: מלשון נוצה וכנף ור״ל תעוף בנוצת כנפים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from the word for feather, meaning to fly on feathered wings.

48:11.headline: Moab is wine left on its dregs, never poured out
48:11.body: שמרים are the dregs at the bottom of a wine jar. Radak says wine left on its dregs keeps its taste, as Moab, never exiled, kept its ease. Malbim says a people moved from land to land changes its ways, like wine poured between jars.

sources.quote: ודימה אותו ליין שעומד על שמריו והוא היין הטוב כי בהרקת היין מכלי אל כלי ילך ריחו וטעמו
sources.says: Radak says Moab is likened to good wine resting on its dregs, since pouring wine from jar to jar loses its smell and taste.

sources.quote: והנמשל שהעם שיגלו אותו ממקום למקום, ישנה מנהגיו ונימוסיו אל מנהגי ונמוסי המדינה שבא לשם
sources.says: Malbim says the lesson is that a people exiled from place to place takes on the customs of each land it comes to.

48:12.headline: God sends 'tippers': men who empty, move, or make wine burst
48:12.body: צעים is a rare word. Rashi reads it as men who empty out. Metzudat Zion reads it as men who drive Moab from place to place. Malbim reads it as wine boiling up until it bursts its jar, a picture of revolt inside Moab.

sources.quote: צוֹעִים. מְרִיקִים, וְכֵן ״מִהַר צֹעֶה לְהִפָּתֵחַ״
sources.says: Rashi says it means those who empty out, and compares a verse in Isaiah.

sources.quote: ענין טלטול והנעה ממקום למקום
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means moving and shaking from place to place.

sources.quote: ורתיחת היין נקרא צועה וזועה, שהוא סועה וסוער בפנימיותו
sources.says: Malbim says the boiling of wine is called צועה, since it storms inside the jar.

48:15.headline: Her towns 'went up': vanished, or the destroyer went up
48:15.body: עלה usually means went up. Metzudat Zion and Radak read it here as 'was taken away', the towns' crowds are gone. Radak's father read it as the destroyer going up against her towns. Malbim reads it as going up to the slaughter.

sources.quote: ענין סלוק והפסק כמו אל תעלני בחצי ימי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means removal and ending, as in 'do not take me up in the middle of my days'.

sources.quote: ופי' עלה נפסק רוצה לומר המון עריה נפסק
sources.says: Radak says it means the crowds of her towns came to an end.

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי ז"ל פירש ולעריה עלה השודד
sources.says: Radak reports that his father read it as the destroyer going up against her towns.

sources.quote: העם אשר בעיר, ופי' עלה לטבח
sources.says: Malbim says it means the people of the town went up to the slaughter.

48:25.headline: Why a kingdom is called a 'horn'
48:25.body: Moab's horn is cut off. Radak explains that a kingdom is called a horn because the horn sits highest on an animal, as a king stands above the people.

sources.quote: ולפי שהקרן היא גבוה על כל אברי הבהמה נקראת המלכות קרן שהיא גבוהה במעלה על כל העם
sources.says: Radak says the kingdom is called a horn because the horn is the highest part of an animal, as the kingdom is highest over the people.

sources.quote: ענין ממשלה כמו וירם קרן משיחו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says horn means rule, as in 'He will raise the horn of His anointed'.

48:26.headline: Drunk Moab 'slaps' in its vomit, or doubts what it is
48:26.body: ספק can mean to clap or strike, and it can also mean doubt. Metzudat Zion and Radak read it as the drunk thrashing in his vomit. Malbim reads it as doubt: the drunk cannot tell vomit from wine and drinks it again.

sources.quote: ענין הכאה וחבטה כמו ויספוק את כפיו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means striking, as when Balak struck his hands together.

sources.quote: כמו שהשכור מתגולל ומתהפך מצד אל צד בהקיאו היין ששתה וספק בגופו לארץ
sources.says: Radak says it is like a drunk rolling from side to side as he vomits, striking his body on the ground.

sources.quote: ואח"ז מסתפק על הקיא אם הוא קיאו או אם הוא יין, וחוזר ושותה את קיאו
sources.says: Malbim says the drunk then doubts whether it is vomit or wine, and drinks his vomit again.

48:27.headline: Moab shook its head in mockery, or will wander in exile
48:27.body: תתנודד means to move to and fro. Rashi gives two readings. Moab shook its head mocking Israel's ruin. Or, because Moab mocked, Moab itself will wander into exile, as the Targum reads.

sources.quote: הָיִיתָ מֵנִיד בְּרֹאשְׁךָ וּמִתְלוֹצֵץ עַל חֻרְבָּנוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says Moab would shake its head and mock Israel's ruin.

sources.quote: אַתָּה תִּתְנוֹדָד – לָצֵאת בַּגּוֹלָה
sources.says: Rashi gives a second reading: you will wander off into exile, as the Targum translates.

48:29.headline: Six words for pride, and Malbim says they differ
48:29.body: The verse piles up words for pride. Malbim says they are not the same: גאוה is pride a person imagines in his heart, while גאון is real greatness that lifts him above others.

sources.quote: הגאון והגאוה אינם נרדפים, שהגאוה מדומה שיתגאה בלבבו, והגאון הוא אמתי שיש לו מעלה שע"י יגאה מאחיו
sources.says: Malbim says גאון and גאוה are not the same: one is imagined pride in the heart, the other a real quality that raises him above his brothers.

sources.quote: כפל הדבר רבת פעמים לפי מרבית הגאוה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the idea is repeated many times to match how great the pride was.

48:30.headline: Moab's 'baddim': its warriors, or its empty boasts
48:30.body: בדיו is a rare word. Rashi reads it as Moab's warriors. Metzudat Zion reads it as lies made up in the heart, and Malbim as Moab's schemes.

sources.quote: בַּדָּיו. גִּבּוֹרָיו
sources.says: Rashi says it means his warriors.

sources.quote: דבר כזב הבדוי מן הלב וכן אשר בדא מלבו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means lies made up in the heart, as in 'which he devised of his own heart'.

sources.quote: ובדיו.  מחשבותיו
sources.says: Malbim says it means his thoughts and plans.

48:33.headline: A shout that is no shout: joy turned into a war cry
48:33.body: הידד was the happy shout of men treading grapes. The verse says there will be a הידד that is not a הידד. Rashi and Malbim explain: people will still shout, but it will be the cry of flight and war, not of harvest.

sources.quote: שֶׁהֵידָד יִצְעֲקוּ לֹא יְהִי הֵידָד הָרִאשׁוֹן, כִּי אִם הֵידָד שֶׁל מְנוּסַת חֶרֶב
sources.says: Rashi says the shout they raise will not be the first, happy one, but the shout of fleeing the sword.

sources.quote: דרך דורכי הענבים לצעוק הידד לזרז זא״ז
sources.says: Metzudat David says grape treaders used to shout הידד to urge each other on.

sources.quote: ר"ל לא יצעקו הידד של שמחה רק הידד של שבר ויללה
sources.says: Malbim says they will not shout for joy, only a shout of ruin and wailing.

48:34.headline: Moab, the prize three-year-old calf, or its ring of officers
48:34.body: עגלת שלשיה reads as 'a third heifer'. Radak says a three-year-old calf is the best, and Metzudat David says Moab was a fine land like the choicest calf. Malbim reads it as a ring of warriors and officers, from מעגל, circle, and שלישים, officers.

sources.quote: ופירוש שלישיה גדולה או בת שלש שנים כי היא הטובה
sources.says: Radak says שלשיה means great, or three years old, which is the best age.

sources.quote: מדינה חשובה כעגל השלישי לבטן המעולה ביותר
sources.says: Metzudat David says Moab was a fine land, like the third calf of a mother, which is the choicest.

sources.quote: עגלת שלשיה שהם מעגל הגבורים והשלישים של מואב
sources.says: Malbim says it means the circle of Moab's warriors and officers.

48:43.headline: Pachad, pachat, pach: terror, pit, and trap that sound alike
48:43.body: Three near-identical words: פחד terror, פחת pit, פח trap. Rashi and Malbim show how each leads to the next, as in a hunt: fear drives the animal into the pit, and climbing out it is caught in the trap.

sources.quote: שֶׁהַפַּחַד גּוֹרֵם לוֹ לָנוּס, וְהַפַּחַת מוּכָן לִיפּוֹל בּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the terror makes him run, and the pit is ready for him to fall into.

sources.quote: וכדי שתפול אל הפחת מפחידים אותה בכלבים שע"י הפחד תפול בהפחת וע"י הפחת תלכד בפח
sources.says: Malbim says hunters scare the animal with dogs so it falls into the pit, and from the pit it is caught in the trap.

48:44.headline: Written 'the one who made others flee', read 'the one who flees'
48:44.body: The written text has הניס, one who made others flee, and it is read aloud as הנס, one who flees. Radak says both apply: some fled, and some sent their children and cattle away.

sources.quote: כתיב ביו"ד כלומר מי שהניס בניו ומקנהו כמו הניס את עבדיו ואת מקנהו והקרי הוא הנס אומר על עצמו
sources.says: Radak says the written form means one who sent his children and cattle fleeing, and the read form means one who flees himself.

49:1.headline: 'Their king' took Gad's land, or their god Milcom did
49:1.body: מלכם can be read 'their king' or as Milcom, the god of Ammon. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as the god. Radak reads it as Ammon's king, who may have built his royal city in Gad's land.

sources.quote: עֲבוֹדַת כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁל בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן מַלְכָּם שְׁמָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says Milcom is the name of the idol of the people of Ammon.

sources.quote: מלכם. כך שם הגלולים של בני עמון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says this is the name of Ammon's idol, as in I Kings 11.

sources.quote: ואפשר בנה בארץ גד מלך בני עמון עיר המלוכה לפיכך אמר מלכם
sources.says: Radak says perhaps the king of Ammon built his royal city in Gad's land, which is why it says 'their king'.

49:7.headline: Teman: a grandson of Esau, or simply 'the south'
49:7.body: תימן is a place in Edom, and the word also means south. Radak says it is named for Teman, son of Eliphaz son of Esau. Rashi and the Targum read it as the south, since Edom lies south of Israel.

sources.quote: ותימן הוא מבני אליפז בן עשו אבל ת"י בדרומא
sources.says: Radak says Teman is one of the sons of Eliphaz son of Esau, but the Targum renders it 'in the south'.

sources.quote: אֱדוֹם בִּדְרוֹמָהּ שֶׁל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא
sources.says: Rashi says Edom is in the south of the land of Israel.

49:13.headline: Why a town of Moab is punished along with Edom
49:13.body: Rashi says Bozrah was a Moabite town. It is punished here with Edom because an early king of Edom, Jobab son of Zerah, came from Bozrah. Radak instead calls Bozrah Edom's royal city.

sources.quote: בָּצְרָה מֵעָרֵי מוֹאָב, אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי הָעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״יוֹבָב בֶּן זֶרַח מִבָּצְרָה״
sources.says: Rashi says Bozrah was a Moabite town, but since 'Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah' ruled Edom, it is struck along with Edom.

sources.quote: בצרה. היא עיר מלוכה באדום
sources.says: Radak says Bozrah is a royal city in Edom.

49:26.headline: Destroyed means 'silenced': a ruined city makes no sound
49:26.body: The soldiers ידמו, are cut off. Rashi says the word comes from דממה, silence, because no sound is heard in a ruined city.

sources.quote: וְאֵינוֹ זָז מִלְּשׁוֹן דְּמָמָה, שֶׁכָּל עִיר חֲרֵבָה אֵין קוֹל נִשְׁמָע בָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says the word does not leave the sense of silence, since in every ruined city no sound is heard.

sources.quote: ידמו. ענין כריתה כמו ער מואב נדמה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means being cut off, as in Isaiah 15:1.

5:1.headline: Find one 'man': not any person, but a person of worth
5:1.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion say איש here means a man great in good deeds, not just anyone. Radak also asks how none could be found, and cites his father: the pious were hiding at home, afraid to show themselves in the streets.

sources.quote: איש. ר״ל גדול ובעל מעשים טובים וכן הלא איש אתה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says איש means a great man with good deeds, as in 'are you not a man?'

sources.quote: אם תמצאו איש. ר"ל איש טוב וגדול במעשים
sources.says: Radak says it means a good man, great in deeds.

sources.quote: כי החסידים שהיו בירושלם היו מתחבאים בבתיהם ולא היו יכולים להתראות ברחובות ובחוצות מפני הרשעים
sources.says: Radak cites his father: the pious in Jerusalem hid in their houses and could not be seen in the streets because of the wicked.

5:1.headline: Justice toward people, faithfulness toward God
5:1.body: The verse looks for someone who does משפט and seeks אמונה. Malbim says that wherever these two words appear together, the first is about how people treat each other and the second is about a person's bond with God.

sources.quote: משפט בין אדם לחברו ואמונה בין אדם למקום
sources.says: Malbim says משפט is between a person and another person, and אמונה is between a person and God.

5:3.headline: God's eyes look for faithfulness, or for what lasts?
5:3.body: Rashi reads אמונה as faithfulness: God looks to do good to the faithful, so why have these people betrayed him? Metzudat Zion and Radak read it as what endures, like a peg in a firm place: God watches over what lasts, not over empty things.

sources.quote: הֵם בַּעֲלֵי אֱמוּנָה לְהֵיטִיב, וְלָמָּה בָּגְדוּ אֵלֶּה בָּךְ
sources.says: Rashi speaks of those who are faithful, to do them good, and asks why these have betrayed God.

sources.quote: לאמונה. ענין דבר המתקיים וכן יתד במקום נאמן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means something that lasts, as in 'a peg in a firm place'.

sources.quote: השגחתך בעולם הלא לאמונה כלומר לדבר קיים לא לדבר בטל
sources.says: Radak says God's watching over the world is for what lasts, not for what is empty.

5:4.headline: Poor in money, or poor in knowledge?
5:4.body: Rashi and Metzudat David say דלים here means poor in wisdom. Radak explains that the common people work as vinedressers and farmers, so they lack the learning of the great, and that is why the prophet turns next to the great ones.

sources.quote: אַךְ דַּלִּים הֵם מֵחָכְמָה
sources.says: Rashi says they are poor in wisdom.

sources.quote: אין תבונה בהם ואך דלים המה מחכמה
sources.says: Metzudat David says they have no understanding and are poor in wisdom.

sources.quote: כי ברוב דלת העם אין להם דעת ובינה כמו הגדולים לפי שהם כורמים ויוגבים
sources.says: Radak says most of the common people lack the knowledge of the great, because they are vinedressers and farmers.

5:6.headline: A wolf of the desert, or a wolf of the evening?
5:6.body: Rashi reads ערבות as the desert, so this is a desert wolf. Malbim gives that reading or 'evening', since wolves raid towns at night, and Radak pictures the wolf coming out at dusk.

sources.quote: זְאֵב עֲרָבוֹת. לְשׁוֹן ״עֲרָבָה וְשׁוּחָה״ (ירמיה ב:ו): זְאֵב הַמִּדְבָּר
sources.says: Rashi says it is from ערבה, desert: a wolf of the wilderness.

sources.quote: מענין ערבה ומדבר, או מענין ערב שהזאבים יפולו בעיר בלילה
sources.says: Malbim says it is either from 'desert' or from 'evening', since wolves fall on the town at night.

sources.quote: ולזאב שיוצא לעת ערב ובא סמוך לישוב
sources.says: Radak compares the enemy to a wolf that comes out at evening near where people live.

5:6.headline: The leopard hurries, keeps watch, or lies in wait
5:6.body: Rashi reads שקד as hurrying. He reports that Menachem read it as keeping watch, as in Proverbs 8:34, and that the Targum reads it as lying in wait.

sources.quote: שׁוֹקֵד. מְמַהֵר, וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ עִם לְשׁוֹן שְׁמִירָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means hurrying, and that Menachem grouped it with words for guarding.

sources.quote: וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם לְשׁוֹן אֲרִיבָה
sources.says: Rashi says the Targum renders it as lying in wait.

sources.quote: שוקד. ענין מהירות כמו כי שוקד אני
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means speed, as in God's 'I am hastening' in Jeremiah 1.

5:7.headline: 'How could I forgive?' or 'Where is the merit?'
5:7.body: Rashi reads אי as a question of disbelief: should I forgive you for this? He reports that Menachem read it as 'no', while Metzudat Zion and Malbim read 'where', as in 'where is Abel your brother', meaning: where is the merit?

sources.quote: בִּתְמִיהָּ: שֶׁמָּא לָזֹאת אֶסְלַח לָךְ?! וּמְנַחֵם פֵּרֵשׁ אֵי כְּמוֹ אַיִן
sources.says: Rashi reads it as an astonished question, and says Menachem explained אי as 'there is not'.

sources.quote: אי. ענינו כמו אנה וכן אי הבל אחיך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means 'where', as in 'where is Abel your brother'.

sources.quote: כמו אי הבל אחיך, איה הזכות
sources.says: Malbim says it means 'where is the merit?'

5:8.headline: Well-fed horses, or 'armed' ones?
5:8.body: Metzudat Zion and Radak read מיזנים from מזון, food: horses fed so well that they are full of lust by morning. Malbim reads it from זיון, 'armed', meaning sexually aroused, and also mentions the food reading.

sources.quote: מיוזנים. מלשון מזון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from 'food'.

sources.quote: והוא כמו הפוך מזונים מן מזון
sources.says: Radak says it is like מזונים, from 'food', with the letters changed.

sources.quote: מיוזנים משכים, מענין זיון
sources.says: Malbim reads it from 'arming'.

sources.quote: י"מ מענין מזון
sources.says: He notes that some read it from 'food'.

5:8.headline: Rising early, or a cruder word?
5:8.body: Rashi and Radak read משכים as 'early in the morning', like dew that goes early. Malbim reports another reading that ties it to אשך, the testicles, so the horses are full of lust.

sources.quote: מַשְׁכִּים – לְאוֹר בֹּקֶר בְּהַשְׁכָּמָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means at first light, early in the morning.

sources.quote: וכן כטל משכים הולך כלומר בהשכמה בבקר
sources.says: Radak compares 'like dew that goes early': early in the morning.

sources.quote: וי"מ משכים כמו מאשכים מן מרוח אשך
sources.says: Malbim reports that some read משכים as if from אשך, the testicles.

5:9.headline: God's 'soul' means God himself, or his will
5:9.body: Radak says God's 'soul' is simply God himself, as when God swears 'by his soul', meaning 'by myself'. The Targum reads it as 'my will'.

sources.quote: ונפשו הוא והוא נפשו וכן נשבע ה' בנפשו כמו בי נשבעתי
sources.says: Radak says God's soul is God himself, so 'God swore by his soul' means 'by myself I swore'.

sources.quote: ויונתן פי' בנפשי כלומר ברצוני
sources.says: Radak says the Targum explains 'my soul' as 'my will'.

5:10.headline: Climb her walls, or go up her vineyard rows?
5:10.body: This word appears only here. Menachem and Radak read it as walls, but Rashi says the branches named next belong to a vineyard, so he reads it as the rows of the vineyard, as do Metzudat Zion and Malbim.

sources.quote: וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ לְשׁוֹן חוֹמָה עִם ״אֲדַלֵּג שׁוּר״
sources.says: Rashi reports that Menachem grouped it with 'wall', as in 'I leap over a wall'.

sources.quote: וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר שָׁרוֹתֶיהָ לְשׁוֹן שׁוּרוֹת הַכֶּרֶם
sources.says: Rashi says he reads it as the rows of the vineyard.

sources.quote: עלו בשרותיה. בחומותיה תרגום חומה שורא
sources.says: Radak says it means her walls, since the Aramaic for wall is שורא.

sources.quote: בשרותיה. בשורות הכרם
sources.says: Malbim says it means the rows of the vineyard.

5:10.headline: Cut off her branches, or her battlements?
5:10.body: Metzudat Zion and Malbim read נטישות as long vine branches, as in Isaiah 18:5. Radak keeps the picture of a city and reads them as the teeth along the top of the wall, while the Targum reads them as her palaces.

sources.quote: הם הענפים הגדולים המתפשטים למרחוק כמו ואת הנטישות הסיר התז
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are the large branches that spread far, as in Isaiah 18:5.

sources.quote: ונטישות הם ענפי הגפן המתפשטים ברוחב בין שורות הכרם
sources.says: Malbim says they are vine branches spreading out between the vineyard rows.

sources.quote: הסירו נטישותיה. הם שיני החומה ויונתן תירגם כמו ארמנותיה
sources.says: Radak says they are the teeth of the wall, and the Targum renders them like 'her palaces'.

5:15.headline: 'Hear' here means 'understand'
5:15.body: Metzudat Zion and Radak say תשמע means understand, as when Joseph's brothers did not know he understood them. Malbim adds that one phrase means a foreign language and the other a strange accent you cannot follow.

sources.quote: תשמע. ענין הבנה כמו כי שומע יוסף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means understanding, as in 'Joseph understood' (Genesis 42:23).

sources.quote: ולא תשמע. ולא תבין
sources.says: Radak says it means 'and you will not understand'.

sources.quote: לא תדע לשונו הוא לשון אחרת, ולא תשמע מה ידבר, הוא לעגי שפה, שהמבטא שלו משונה
sources.says: Malbim says 'you will not know its language' is a foreign tongue, and 'you will not understand what it says' is a strange accent.

5:17.headline: To make poor, or to smash down?
5:17.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion take ירשש from רש, a poor man: the enemy will impoverish your cities. Radak says the word also means smashing cities, as when Edom says 'we are beaten down, but we will rebuild'.

sources.quote: יְרוֹשֵׁשׁ. יְמַסְכֵּן
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'he will make poor'.

sources.quote: ירושש. מל׳ רש ועני
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from 'poor and needy'.

sources.quote: וענין הרישות נופל ג"כ בהריסת הערים כמו כי תאמר אדום רששנו ונשוב ונבנה חרבות
sources.says: Radak says the word is also used for tearing down cities, as in Malachi 1:4.

5:19.headline: 'In return for what?' The answer is measure for measure
5:19.body: Malbim says תחת marks a payment that matches the deed, as in 'an eye for an eye'. Radak spells out the match: you served foreign gods in your own land, so you will serve foreigners in a land not yours.

sources.quote: מלת תחת הנרדף עם מלת יען מורה שהיו התשלומין מדה כנגד מדה, עין תחת עין
sources.says: Malbim says the word תחת shows that the payment was measure for measure, as in 'an eye for an eye'.

sources.quote: מדה כנגד מדה אתם עבדתם אלהי נכר בארצכם תעבדו עם נכר בארץ לא לכם
sources.says: Radak says it is measure for measure: you served foreign gods in your land, you will serve a foreign people in a land not yours.

5:22.headline: Two kinds of fear: awe, and trembling at punishment
5:22.body: Malbim says 'fear me' is about awe at God's greatness, while 'tremble before me' is fear of punishment. Radak ties תחילו to the shaking of a woman in labor.

sources.quote: שירא את מורה על יראת הרוממות
sources.says: Malbim says 'fear me' points to awe at God's greatness.

sources.quote: והחילה מפניו, מורה יראת העונש
sources.says: He says trembling before him points to fear of punishment.

sources.quote: תחילו. מן חיל כיולדה
sources.says: Radak says the word comes from the trembling of a woman giving birth.

5:24.headline: Written 'and early rain': rain all year, plus the two crop rains
5:24.body: The written text has 'and' before the early rain. Radak explains that God gives rain all year for gardens and drinking, and also the early and late rains for the crops, each in its time.

sources.quote: אבל למה שכתב ויורה בוי"ו השמוש הנותן גשם בשאר עתי השנה לצורך הגנות ולשתות
sources.says: Radak says that because it is written 'and early rain', the verse means God gives rain the rest of the year for gardens and drinking.

sources.quote: יורה. הוא המטר היורד על הזרעים המרוה הזרעים והאדמה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says יורה is the rain that falls on the seeds and soaks the seeds and the ground.

sources.quote: ומלקוש. הוא המטר המאוחר היורד על הקשין ועל המלילות
sources.says: He says מלקוש is the late rain that falls on the stalks and the ripening ears.

5:24.headline: The seven weeks of harvest, kept free of rain
5:24.body: Rashi reads שבעת as the seven weeks of harvest, which begin with the omer offering and end with the two loaves. Radak says God guards those weeks so no rain falls and spoils the harvest.

sources.quote: שִׁבְעָה שָׁבוּעוֹת, שֶׁחָקַק לָנוּ בָּהֶן שְׁתֵּי חֻקּוֹת קָצִיר: חֹק הָעֹמֶר וְחֹק שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם
sources.says: Rashi says these are seven weeks in which God set two harvest laws: the omer and the two loaves.

sources.quote: ישמור לנו שלא ירד מטר בימי הקציר שלא יפסיד הקציר
sources.says: Radak says God keeps them for us so no rain falls in the harvest days and ruins the harvest.

5:28.headline: Sleek and fat, or busy with schemes?
5:28.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion link עשתו to 'a block of ivory' in Song of Songs: they grew thick and their skin shiny. Malbim offers another reading, from עשתונות, thoughts: they planned evil and then did it.

sources.quote: עָשְׁתוּ. לְשׁוֹן ״עֶשֶׁת שֵׁן״ (שיר השירים ה:יד), גּוּף עָב
sources.says: Rashi says it is from 'a block of ivory': a thick body.

sources.quote: עשתו. ענין צחות ובהירות כמו מעיו עשת שן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means sleekness and shine, as in 'a block of ivory'.

sources.quote: ויל"פ מלשון עשתות שאנן
sources.says: Malbim says it can also be read from the word for thoughts, as in Job 12:5.

5:31.headline: Priests who rule, or priests who scoop up bribes like honey
5:31.body: Metzudat Zion reads ירדו as 'rule', as in 'rule among your enemies'. Radak's first reading takes it from scooping honey with the hand: the priests scoop up bribes because they taste sweet.

sources.quote: ירדו. ענין ממשלה כמו רדה בקרב אויביך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means ruling, as in Psalm 110:2.

sources.quote: ענין לקיחה מן רדה הדבש כלומר יקחו השחד לעות המשפט יקחו אותם על ידיהם כרודה הדבש בידו שהוא טוב וערב
sources.says: Radak says it means taking, from scooping honey: they take bribes to twist justice, as one scoops honey by hand because it is sweet.

sources.quote: וי"מ אותו ענין ממשלה
sources.says: He notes that some read it as ruling.

50:2.headline: בל and מרודך are Babylon's idols, and each fits its verb
50:2.body: Rashi says בל and מרודך are the names of Babylon's idols. Malbim says בל was the idol of honor, so the verse says it was shamed (הוביש). מרודך was the idol of strength, so the verse says it was dismayed (חת).

sources.quote: שְׁמוֹת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁל בָּבֶל
sources.says: Rashi says בל and מרודך are names of Babylon's idols.

sources.quote: אליל בל היה אליל הכבוד ועשו לו עצבים אמר הוביש, אליל מרודך היה אליל הגבורה ועשו לו גלולים אמר חת שהוא הפך אומץ לב
sources.says: Malbim says בל was the idol of honor, so the verse says הוביש, and מרודך was the idol of might, so it says חת, the opposite of courage.

50:4.headline: Weeping as they return: tears of joy, or of repentance?
50:4.body: Radak says there is a kind of weeping that comes from joy, so the people weep gladly as they come back to their land. Metzudat David says they go with repentance and pleading. Malbim compares them to someone who lost his father and is searching for him.

sources.quote: משמחתם בשובם לארצם כי יש בכי של שמחה
sources.says: Radak says the weeping comes from their joy at returning to their land, since there is weeping of joy.

sources.quote: הלוך ובכו ילכו. בתשובה ובתחנונים ילכו
sources.says: Metzudat David says they will go in repentance and in pleading.

sources.quote: הלוך ובכו ילכו כמי שנאבד לו אביו המוליכו בדרך
sources.says: Malbim says they go weeping like a person who has lost the father who led him on the road.

50:5.headline: Do they ask the way to Zion, or ask Zion itself?
50:5.body: Radak reads it plainly: the returning exiles ask one another the road to Zion. Malbim also allows a poetic reading: they ask the city itself, and Zion answers them, "Come, join the LORD."

sources.quote: בשובם מגלות בבל ישאלו זה לזה דרך ציון
sources.says: Radak says that on returning from Babylon they will ask one another the way to Zion.

sources.quote: וכאילו שואלים את העיר שתגיד להם את דרכם, והיא משיבה בואו ונלוו אל ה'
sources.says: Malbim says it can be a figure of speech: they ask the city to tell them their way, and it answers, come and join the LORD.

50:5.headline: ונלוו: join the LORD yourselves, or others will join you?
50:5.body: Metzudat David reads it as the exiles urging one another to attach themselves to God. Radak says the Targum takes it to mean that converts will join Israel as they leave Babylon.

sources.quote: אמרו אלו לאלו באו והתחברו אל ה׳ בברית המתקיים עד עולם
sources.says: Metzudat David says they will say to one another, come and join yourselves to the LORD in a lasting covenant.

sources.quote: דעתו בזה שילוו עמהם גרים בעלותם מבבל
sources.says: Radak says the Targum's meaning here is that converts will join them as they go up from Babylon.

50:8.headline: The leaders walk in front like he-goats before the flock
50:8.body: Metzudat Zion says עתודים are male goats. Radak says the exiles should leave without fear, like the goats that lead the flock. Malbim says the goats stand for their leaders: Ezra, Nehemiah and the heads of the exile.

sources.quote: כעתודים. הם הזכרים מן העזים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says עתודים are the male goats.

sources.quote: תהיו בצאתכם כמו העתודים שהולכים לפני הצאן כן תהיו אתם בלא פחד ובלא יראה
sources.says: Radak says that when they leave they should be like the goats that go before the flock, without fear or dread.

sources.quote: והם המנהיגים שהלכו לפניהם שהם עזרא ונחמיה וראשי הגולה
sources.says: Malbim says the goats are the leaders who went before them: Ezra, Nehemiah and the heads of the exile.

50:11.headline: דשה: a heifer treading grain, or grazing on grass?
50:11.body: Rashi says the heifer threshes in the grain and eats all the time. Radak says one reading is a heifer always grazing on grass, fat and healthy. He notes that some books spell it with a ה and read it from דיש, threshing.

sources.quote: הַדָּשָׁה בַּתְּבוּאָה וְאוֹכֶלֶת תָּמִיד
sources.says: Rashi says it is the heifer that threshes in the grain and eats all the time.

sources.quote: כעגלה שהיא תמיד רועה בדשא שהיא שמנה ובריאת בשר
sources.says: Radak says it is a heifer that is always grazing on grass, fat and healthy in flesh.

sources.quote: ובמקצת ספרים הוא כתוב בה"א ופי' מענין דיש
sources.says: Radak says that in some books it is written with a ה, and that it then comes from דיש, threshing.

50:14.headline: ידו: throw stones, shoot arrows, or throw by hand?
50:14.body: The verb means to throw. Rashi says what is thrown is stones. Metzudat David says arrows. Malbim says not shot from a bow at all, but thrown by hand.

sources.quote: זִרְקוּ לָהּ אֲבָנִים, כְּמוֹ ״וַיַּדּוּ אֶבֶן בִּי״
sources.says: Rashi says they should throw stones at her, as in וידו אבן בי.

sources.quote: ידו אליה. השליכו חצים אליה
sources.says: Metzudat David says throw arrows at her.

sources.quote: אל תשליכו את החצים ע"י הקשת רק השליכו אותם בידכם
sources.says: Malbim says do not shoot the arrows with the bow, but throw them with your hands.

50:15.headline: נתנה ידה: begging for help, or giving up?
50:15.body: Rashi says it is like a person with no strength who stretches out a hand to anyone, begging for mercy and help. Radak says it means she handed herself over to the enemy, because she could not stand against them.

sources.quote: כְּאָדָם שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כֹּחַ וּמוֹשִׁיט יָד לְכָל מִי שֶׁרוֹאֶה, לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים וְעֶזְרָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is like a person without strength who holds out a hand to everyone he sees, asking for mercy and help.

sources.quote: כלומר מסרה עצמה אל האויבים כי לא תוכל לעמוד בפניהם
sources.says: Radak says it means she gave herself over to the enemies, because she could not stand against them.

50:21.headline: פקוד: a place name, or a word meaning reckoning?
50:21.body: Rashi says Pekod is the name of a country, as in Ezekiel. Radak says it may also name Babylon because the time had come to reckon with its sin, but he notes that the Targum treats it as a city's name.

sources.quote: שֵׁם מְדִינָה, וְכֵן ״פְּקוֹד וְשׁוֹעַ וְקוֹעַ״ (יחזקאל כג:כג)
sources.says: Rashi says Pekod is the name of a country, as in פקוד ושוע וקוע in Ezekiel.

sources.quote: קראה גם כן פקוד שבא העת לפקוד עונם ויונתן לא תירגם כן פקוד לדעתו שהוא שם מערי בבל
sources.says: Radak says she was also called פקוד because the time had come to reckon their sin, but the Targum did not translate it so, since it holds it is the name of one of Babylon's cities.

50:21.headline: חרב here: ruin, or "strike with the sword"?
50:21.body: Metzudat Zion reads it from חורבן, ruin. Radak reads it as an order built on חרב, the sword: strike them with the sword.

sources.quote: חרוב. מלשון חורבן והחרם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is from the language of ruin and the ban.

sources.quote: חרוב צווי מעניין חרב כלומר חרוב בחרב
sources.says: Radak says it is a command from חרב, meaning strike with the sword.

50:26.headline: מאבסיה: gates, or storehouses named for a feeding trough?
50:26.body: This is a rare word. Rashi says the Targum renders it as gates, but he finds nothing like it, and Menachem ties it to אבוס, a feeding trough. Metzudat Zion says it is a grain store, from the same word.

sources.quote: תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״אִבּוּלָהָא״ – שַׁעֲרֵיהָּ; וְאֵין לוֹ דִּמְיוֹן. וּמְנַחֵם חִבְּרוֹ לְשׁוֹן אֵבוּס
sources.says: Rashi says the Targum renders it as her gates, but there is nothing like it, and Menachem connects it to the word for a feeding trough.

sources.quote: ענינו אוצר התבואה והוא מענין אבוס בעליו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a store of grain, and comes from אבוס בעליו.

50:26.headline: סלוה: tread on it, or heap it up?
50:26.body: Rashi says it means thresh it, tread it down. Radak says his father read it as piling up in heaps, because he took the root to mean lifting.

sources.quote: סָלּוּהָ. דּוּשׁוּ אוֹתָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says סלוה means thresh it.

sources.quote: ואדוני אבי ז"ל פי' כי עשו תלים תלים כמו ערמים משללה כי לדעתו כל לשון מסלה עניין הרמה
sources.says: Radak says his father explained that they made heaps like piles, since in his view every use of מסלה means raising up.

50:28.headline: Malbim: a פליט has already been under the sword
50:28.body: The verse lists those who fled (נסים) and those who escaped (פלטים). Malbim says a פליט is one who had already been under the sword and got away.

sources.quote: הפליט כבר היה תחת החרב
sources.says: Malbim says the פליט had already been under the sword.

sources.quote: ופלטים. נמלטים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ופלטים means those who got away.

50:29.headline: השמיעו here means gather the people, not just make heard
50:29.body: Metzudat Zion and Radak say it means to gather, because a crowd is gathered by sounding a call. Rashi points to וישמע שאול את העם.

sources.quote: ענין אסיפה וקבוץ כמו וישמע שאול את העם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means gathering, as in וישמע שאול את העם.

sources.quote: אספו לפי שאסיפת העם על יד השמעת קול נאמרה בלשון שמיעה
sources.says: Radak says it means gather them, because gathering the people by a sounded call is said with the word for hearing.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן ״וַיַּשְׁמַע שָׁאוּל אֶת הָעָם״ (שמואל א טו:ד)
sources.says: Rashi says it is the language of וישמע שאול את העם in Samuel.

50:30.headline: לכן: an oath, or simply "therefore"?
50:30.body: Rashi says לכן is here a word of oath. Metzudat David reads it in the usual way: since she acted proudly against the LORD, therefore her young men will fall.

sources.quote: לָכֵן. לְשׁוֹן שְׁבוּעָה
sources.says: Rashi says לכן is the language of an oath.

sources.quote: הואיל וזדה אל ה׳ לכן יפלו
sources.says: Metzudat David says since she acted proudly against the LORD, therefore they will fall.

50:38.headline: יתהללו: go mad, or boast?
50:38.body: Rashi first says they will act insanely. His second view matches the Targum's משתבחין, meaning boasting. Radak finds it odd that the Targum says praise, since the word means folly.

sources.quote: יִשְׁתַּטּוּ. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: פורוונטרונט בְּלַעַ״ז, וְכֵן תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: ״מִשְׁתַּבְּחִין״
sources.says: Rashi says it means they will act madly, then gives another view with an Old French word, matching the Targum's משתבחין.

sources.quote: ומן התימה שתרגם יונתן ובטעותהא משתבחין תרגם יתהוללו ענין תהלה והוא לפי הנמצא עניין הוללות וסכלות
sources.says: Radak says it is surprising that the Targum translated it as praise, since the word is found to mean folly.

50:39.headline: איים: the Targum says cats; Malbim ties it to the idols' terrors
50:39.body: This is a rare word for a wild animal. Radak says the Targum renders it as חתולין. Malbim says the beasts sent will look like the terrifying shapes, the אימים, that Babylon used for its idols.

sources.quote: איים. תירגם יונתן חתולין
sources.says: Radak says the Targum renders איים as חתולין.

sources.quote: אשלח לשם חיות נוראות כדמות חיות האימים שהיו להם לפסילים
sources.says: Malbim says I will send fearsome animals there, like the shapes of the terrifying animals they had as idols.

50:44.headline: גאון הירדן: the lions' place, or the Jordan in flood?
50:44.body: Rashi learns that גאון הירדן is where lions live. Metzudat Zion says it is the high, rich plain beside the Jordan, where the lions were. Radak says it means the Jordan swelling with water over its banks.

sources.quote: לָמַדְנוּ, שֶׁגְּאוֹן הַיַּרְדֵּן מְקוֹם אֲרָיוֹת הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says we learn that the גאון of the Jordan is a place of lions.

sources.quote: ענין גבהות ורוממות ור״ל ככר המעולה הסמוך לירדן ושם היה מקום האריות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means height and loftiness: the choice plain next to the Jordan, where the lions lived.

sources.quote: כלומר יעלה ויתגבר כמו שמתגברים המים כשהירדן בגאונו מלא על כל גדותיו
sources.says: Radak says he will rise and grow strong, as the waters do when the Jordan in its swelling is full over all its banks.

50:45.headline: אם לא here is an oath: "surely they will"
50:45.body: Metzudat David says אם לא is a form of oath. It means he swears the young of the flock will drag them away, and that he will make their dwelling desolate.

sources.quote: אם לא. הוא ענין שבועה ור״ל העצה היא בשבועה
sources.says: Metzudat David says אם לא is an oath, meaning the plan is sworn.

sources.quote: אם לא ישים. בשבועה אשר יעשה את כל נוה ונוה שממה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is by oath that he will make every dwelling desolate.

51:1.headline: A coded name: 'the heart of My foes' spells Chaldea
51:1.body: Swap each letter of לב קמי for its mirror in the alphabet (א for ת, ב for ש, and so on) and you get כשדים, the Chaldeans. Rashi and Radak point out the code. Radak adds that the words also mean what they say, 'the heart of My enemies'.

sources.quote: לֵב קָמָי. כַּשְׂדִּים בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא דְּא״ת ב״ש
sources.says: Rashi says לב קמי is כשדים in the Atbash letter swap.

sources.quote: ויהיה לב קמי כמשמעו לב אויבי
sources.says: Radak brings the Atbash reading and also reads it plainly as 'the heart of My enemies'.

51:2.headline: Strangers who will scatter her
51:2.body: זרים, strangers, sits next to וזרוה, 'they will scatter her'. Radak says the sound play is deliberate, for elegance. Malbim reads וזרוה from זר, a ring: they will surround her on every side.

sources.quote: וזרוה מן מזרה ישראל והוא לשון נופל על הלשון לצחות
sources.says: Radak says וזרוה comes from 'He who scattered Israel', a play of word on word for elegance.

sources.quote: וזרוה, יסובבו אותה סביב כזר
sources.says: Malbim says it means they will surround her like a ring.

51:2.headline: 'I will send' armies that chose to come on their own
51:2.body: Maimonides says the prophets often name God as the cause of things people do by their own choice. He gives this verse as an example: the Persians and Medes beat the Chaldeans, yet God says 'I will send'.

sources.quote: ועל ניצחונם של פרס ומדי על הכשדים נאמר
sources.says: Maimonides lists this verse, about the Persian and Median victory over the Chaldeans, among things caused by human choice that are spoken of as God's act.

51:5.headline: Israel is not a widow; her husband is alive
51:5.body: אלמן appears only here. Radak reads it from 'widow': a widow's husband is gone for good, but Israel's husband, God, lives and will come back to her.

sources.quote: אינו כמו האלמנה שמת בעלה שהיא עזובה ממנו לעולם לא כן ישראל כי בעלה חי וקים
sources.says: Radak says Israel is not like a widow left forever, because her husband lives.

sources.quote: לֹא שְׁכָחוֹ מִלִּנְקוֹם נִקְמָתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says God did not forget to avenge Israel.

51:7.headline: A gold cup, or wine as clear as gold?
51:7.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion say 'gold' describes what is in the cup: pure, clear wine, the wrath God pours out. Malbim reads it as the cup itself, made of strong metal like Babylon.

sources.quote: קרא היין הזך זהב לזכות הזהב
sources.says: Radak says the clear wine is called gold because gold is pure.

sources.quote: זהב. ר״ל נקי וצלול כזהב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means clean and clear like gold.

sources.quote: היו דומים ככוס זהב שהוא מתכות חזק
sources.says: Malbim says Babylon was like a gold cup, a strong metal.

51:11.headline: Polish the arrows, or fit them with feathers?
51:11.body: Rashi and Radak read הברו from ברר, to make clean and bright. Radak's father read it from אבר, a wing feather: fletch the arrows so they fly straight. Malbim takes it the same way.

sources.quote: הָבֵרוּ. לְשׁוֹן נִקָּיוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it means cleaning.

sources.quote: הברו משפטו האברו מן אבר כיונה ארך האבר שענינו נוצה
sources.says: Radak reports his father's view that it comes from אבר, a feather, meaning to put feathers on the arrows.

51:11.headline: Fill the quivers, or gather the shields?
51:11.body: Rashi says שלטים are quivers that hold arrows, so 'fill the quivers'. Radak says they are shields, and מלאו here means 'gather'.

sources.quote: אַשְׁפּוֹת שֶׁהַחִצִּים נְתוּנִים בָּהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says they are quivers that the arrows are kept in.

sources.quote: מלאו השלטים. אספו המגינים
sources.says: Radak says it means 'gather the shields'.

51:14.headline: God swore 'by His soul', a human way of speaking
51:14.body: Radak says God has no soul separate from Himself, as a person does. 'By His soul' just means 'by Himself'; the Torah speaks in human language.

sources.quote: כי אינו דבר אחד ונפשו דבר אחר כמו האדם אלא שדברה תורה כלשון בני אדם
sources.says: Radak says God and His soul are not two things as with a person; the Torah speaks in human terms.

51:16.headline: Clouds called 'the lifted ones'
51:16.body: נשיאים usually means princes. Metzudat Zion says here it means clouds, named for the way they lift themselves up.

sources.quote: נשיאים. עננים ע״ש שמנשאים עצמם למעלה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says נשיאים are clouds, called so because they raise themselves up.

51:20.headline: Babylon as God's sledgehammer
51:20.body: מפץ appears only here. Radak and Metzudat Zion say it is a tool for smashing stones and walls: God used Babylon to break the nations. Malbim says the hammer here is Israel.

sources.quote: מפץ שם הכלי שמנפצים בו האבנים
sources.says: Radak says מפץ is the name of the tool used to smash stones.

sources.quote: מפץ. שם כלי עשוי לרצץ ולשבור בו החומות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a tool made to crush and break walls.

sources.quote: מפץ יאמר לישראל אתה מפץ של כלי מלחמה
sources.says: Malbim says God is speaking to Israel: you are My hammer.

51:25.headline: Why flat Babylon is called a mountain
51:25.body: Babylon sits on a plain. Radak says 'mountain' means a fortified city, as strong as one built on a mountain. The Aramaic translation also renders it 'city'.

sources.quote: קרא בבל הר ואם היא בקעה רוצה לומר הר עיר בצורה
sources.says: Radak says Babylon is called a mountain though it is a valley, meaning a fortified city.

51:27.headline: Horses like bristling locusts
51:27.body: סמר appears only here. Rashi links it to 'the hair of my flesh stood up' in Job: the horses come like locusts with bristles on end. Metzudat Zion reads it as hard like a nail.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ ״תְּסַמֵּר שַׂעֲרַת בְּשָׂרִי״
sources.says: Rashi says it means bristling, like 'the hair of my flesh stood up'.

sources.quote: סמר. ענין התקשות כמסמר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means hardening like a nail.

51:30.headline: Their strength slipped away, like the sinew that slipped
51:30.body: Rashi links נשתה to גיד הנשה, the sinew that slipped out of place when Jacob wrestled: Babylon's strength jumped away. Radak reads it as 'ran dry', like water drying up from the sea.

sources.quote: נָשְׁתָה. קָפְצָה; כְּמוֹ ״גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה״
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'jumped away', like the sinew that moved from its place.

sources.quote: נשתה גבורתם. פסקה וכן ונשתו מים מהים
sources.says: Radak says it means their strength stopped, as in 'the waters dry up from the sea'.

51:32.headline: Burning the reed beds, or the forts?
51:32.body: Radak says אגמים are the reeds that grow along rivers, burned so the attackers could get in. He also cites Rabbi Yonah, who read it as fortresses, from the Arabic word for them.

sources.quote: ורבי יונה כתב כי אגמים הם המבצרים ודמה אותו ללשון הערב
sources.says: Radak says the word means the reeds by the rivers, and reports Rabbi Yonah's view that it means fortresses, from Arabic.

sources.quote: האגמים. הוא הגומא הגדל ע״פ המים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the reed that grows by the water.

51:34.headline: Not 'drove me away' but 'rinsed me out'
51:34.body: הדיחני can mean 'he drove me out'. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as rinsing a dish: Nebuchadnezzar left Jerusalem like a washed bowl with nothing left in it.

sources.quote: כמו שידיח אדם את הכלי שלא נשאר בו דבר
sources.says: Radak says it is like a man rinsing a vessel until nothing is left in it.

sources.quote: הדיחני. מלשון הדחה ושטיפת כלי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means rinsing and washing a vessel.

51:35.headline: My food, or my flesh?
51:35.body: Rashi reads שארי as 'my food', the food Babylon ate up. Radak reads it as 'my flesh', meaning the people who were killed, while חמסי is the goods that were looted.

sources.quote: צַעֲקַת חֲמָסִי וּמְזוֹנוֹתַי
sources.says: Rashi says it is the cry over the wrong done to me and over my food.

sources.quote: שארי בשרי ואמר חמסי על הממון אשר בזזו ושארי על החללים
sources.says: Radak says שארי is my flesh: חמסי is the looted money and שארי the slain.

51:38.headline: Lions that 'bray'
51:38.body: נערו appears only here. Rashi, Radak and Metzudat Zion all note that the sages used this word for a donkey's bray. Here it is the roar of young lions.

sources.quote: נערו. כעניין שאגו ורז"ל נהגו בזה הלשון על חמור באמרם חמור נוער
sources.says: Radak says it means roaring, and the rabbis used the word of a donkey, 'the donkey brays'.

sources.quote: נָעֲרוּ. לְשׁוֹן חֲמוֹר נוֹעֵר
sources.says: Rashi says it is the word used for a donkey braying.

51:41.headline: Sheshach is Babel in code
51:41.body: Swap each letter of ששך for its mirror in the alphabet (ש for ב, ך for ל) and you get בבל, Babel. Rashi, Radak and Metzudat Zion all read it this way.

sources.quote: שֵׁשַׁךְ. בָּבֶל בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא דְּא״ת ב״ש
sources.says: Rashi says Sheshach is Babel in the Atbash letter swap.

sources.quote: ששך. הוא בבל בא״ת ב״ש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says Sheshach is Babel by Atbash.

51:44.headline: Nations will no longer 'stream' to Bel
51:44.body: ינהרו comes from the same root as נהר, river. Rashi says the nations flowed to Babylon's god like rivers to the sea. Radak says the verb means running toward what you want, and that is why a river is called נהר.

sources.quote: ענין מרוצה אל החפץ וכן ונהרו אליו כל הגוים ולפיכך נקרא הנהר בזה הלשון
sources.says: Radak says it means running toward something wanted, and a river is named from it as the place where water runs.

sources.quote: וְלֹא יִנְהֲרוּ. וְלֹא יֵאָסְפוּ
sources.says: Rashi says it means they will not gather, like rivers that all go to the sea.

51:47.headline: Babylon will be ashamed, or dried up?
51:47.body: תבוש usually means 'be ashamed', and Radak reads it so: the people will be shamed when their idols break. Metzudat Zion reads it from יבש, dry: the land will wither.

sources.quote: כלומר כל אנשי ארצה יהיה להם בושת
sources.says: Radak says all the people of the land will be ashamed.

sources.quote: תבוש. מלשון יבשות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it comes from dryness.

51:59.headline: Officer of gifts, or the king's companion at rest?
51:59.body: Rashi follows the Aramaic, which reads מנוחה like מנחה, a gift: Seraiah brought in the people who came with tribute. Radak reads it from rest: he kept the king company in his leisure.

sources.quote: עַל יָדוֹ הָיוּ רוֹאִים אֶת פְּנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמְּבִיאִים לוֹ תְּשׁוּרָה
sources.says: Rashi says those who brought the king gifts saw him through Seraiah.

sources.quote: שהיה ריע המלך והיה עם המלך בעת מנוחתו
sources.says: Radak says he was the king's friend and was with him in his time of rest.

52:11.headline: The prison is called a 'house of deposits'
52:11.body: בית הפקדת comes from פקדון, something left in storage. A prisoner is put away and kept, like a deposit.

sources.quote: הפקודות. מלשון פקדון וגניזה והוא בית הסוהר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from deposit and storing away, and it means a prison.

sources.quote: בֵּית הַפְּקֻדּוֹת. בְּבֵית הָאֲסִירִין
sources.says: Rashi says it is the house of prisoners.

52:13.headline: Which 'great house' burned?
52:13.body: The sages read it as a house where something is made great: prayer in a synagogue, or Torah in a study hall. Metzudat David reads it as every great man's house in Jerusalem.

sources.quote: בָּתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת שֶׁמְּגַדְּלִין בָּהֶם תְּפִלָּה, וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: בָּתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת שֶׁמְּגַדְּלִין בָּהֶם אֶת הַתּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi gives two views from the Talmud: synagogues where prayer is made great, or study halls where Torah is made great.

sources.quote: לומר שהם כל בית אדם גדול אשר בירושלים
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means the house of every important person in Jerusalem.

52:20.headline: Oxen 'under the stands'? Rashi admits he is puzzled
52:20.body: The twelve bronze oxen stood under the great basin, not under the stands. Rashi says he does not know how to read this and suggests תחת here means 'beside'. Radak ties 'under' to the basin instead.

sources.quote: לֹא יָדַעְתִּי הֵיאַךְ, שֶׁהֲרֵי תַּחַת הַיָּם הָיוּ
sources.says: Rashi says he does not know how, since the oxen were under the basin.

sources.quote: וְדוֹמֶה לִי שֶׁאֵין זֶה אֶלָּא כְּמוֹ אֵצֶל הַמְּכֹנוֹת
sources.says: Rashi suggests the word here means 'next to' the stands.

sources.quote: אלא אשר תחת אינו דבק עם המכונות אלא ר"ל אשר תחת הים שזכר
sources.says: Radak says 'under' does not go with the stands but with the basin mentioned earlier.

52:23.headline: Ninety-six pomegranates faced 'the wind', meaning the open side
52:23.body: רוחה here means a side, not wind. Each row had a hundred pomegranates, but four were hidden against the wall, so ninety-six could be seen.

sources.quote: כְּלוֹמַר: תִּשְׁעִים וְשִׁשָּׁה מֵהֶם נִרְאִים לְרוּחוֹת הָעַמּוּד
sources.says: Rashi says ninety-six of them could be seen on the sides of the pillar.

sources.quote: וְהַכּוֹתֶל מְכַסֶּה אַרְבַּע רִמּוֹנִים מִכָּל טוּר
sources.says: Rashi says the wall covered four pomegranates in each row.

sources.quote: ורוח פי' עבר ופיאה
sources.says: Radak says רוח means side or edge.

52:28.headline: One word settles two numbers in the book of Kings
52:28.body: Kings gives this exile as ten thousand in one verse and seven thousand in another. Rashi says 'Judeans' here solves it: three thousand from Judah plus seven thousand from other tribes make ten thousand.

sources.quote: בָּא זֶה וּפֵירֵשׁ: יְהוּדִים שְׁלֹשֶׁת אֲלָפִים וּמִשְּׁאָר שְׁבָטִים שִׁבְעַת אֲלָפִים, הֲרֵי עֲשֶׂרֶת אֲלָפִים
sources.says: Rashi says this verse explains: three thousand Judeans and seven thousand from other tribes, ten thousand in all.

52:31.headline: Lifting the captive king's head: raised up, or counted in?
52:31.body: נשא את ראש can mean the new king raised Jehoiachin to honor. Rashi also gives a second reading: he counted him among the other kings, as in 'take a head count'.

sources.quote: נָשָׂא. נְשָׂאוֹ וְגִדְּלוֹ. לִישְׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא: מְנָאוֹ עִם שְׁאָר הַמְּלָכִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means he raised him up, or by another reading, counted him with the other kings.

sources.quote: נשא. הגביה והרים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means he lifted him up.

6:1.headline: העזו: commentators read it as 'flee to safety' or 'gather'
6:1.body: The verb העזו is rare, and the sages do not read it as plain 'be strong'. Radak says it means 'make flee', like שלח העז מקנך, 'bring your livestock to safety'. Metzudat Zion says it means gathering.

sources.quote: העיזו. הניסו כמו שלח העז מקנך
sources.says: Radak says העיזו means הניסו, 'make flee', like the phrase שלח העז מקנך in Exodus.

sources.quote: ויונתן תרגם העיזו גלו
sources.says: Radak adds that Targum Jonathan translates the word as 'go into exile'.

sources.quote: ענין אסיפה כמו העוזו אל תעמודו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word is about gathering, as in the earlier verse העוזו אל תעמדו.

6:1.headline: Tekoa and 'blow' sound alike, so the call is a pun
6:1.body: ובתקוע תקעו means 'in Tekoa, blow the horn'. Tekoa is a town, and its name sounds like the verb for blowing. Radak says the prophet speaks with a clever turn, like ועקרון תעקר, 'Ekron will be uprooted'.

sources.quote: ואמר דרך צחות ובתקוע תקעו לשון נופל על לשון כמו ועקרון תעקר
sources.says: Radak says the prophet speaks wittily: one word falls on the other, as in ועקרון תעקר.

6:1.headline: בית הכרם: a place name, or a watchtower in a vineyard?
6:1.body: The signal is raised at בית הכרם. Rashi says that is the name of a place. Radak says it is the tall tower built in a vineyard to guard the vines, where a signal can be seen from far away.

sources.quote: בֵּית הַכֶּרֶם. שֵׁם מָקוֹם הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says בית הכרם is the name of a place.

sources.quote: מגדל שבונים בכרם אחד גבוה לשמור כל הכרמים אשר סביבותיו ואותו נקרא בית הכרם
sources.says: Radak says it is the high tower built in one vineyard to watch all the vineyards around it, and that tower is called בית הכרם.

6:1.headline: משאת is a signal, but is it a banner or a flame?
6:1.body: שאו משאת means 'raise a signal'. Rashi calls it a banner to gather and fight. Metzudat Zion calls it a flame of fire, and Radak pictures a beacon that far-off people can see.

sources.quote: שְׂאוּ מַשְׂאֵת. נֵס, לְהִקָּבֵץ וּלְהִלָּחֵם עַל נַפְשְׁכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says משאת is a banner, raised so people gather and fight for their lives.

sources.quote: משאת. ענינו להבת אש וכן וישאם דוד
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means a flame of fire.
