sources.quote: שישאו בו משאת שיראו הרחוקים הלהבה וינוסו
sources.says: Radak says they raise the signal so people far away see the flame and flee.

6:2.headline: דמיתי: 'I have compared' or 'I have destroyed'?
6:2.body: The verb can come from 'to resemble' or from 'to cut off'. Rashi says it means I have laid waste. Radak says it means I have likened Zion to a pampered woman, and he records his father's reading, 'cut off'.

sources.quote: הֶחֱרַבְתִּי תִּרְגְּמוֹ יוֹנָתָן; לְשׁוֹן ״וְנָדַמּוּ נְאוֹת הַשָּׁלוֹם״
sources.says: Rashi says דמיתי means 'I have laid waste', as Jonathan translated it, like 'the peaceful pastures are silenced'.

sources.quote: כלומר דמיתי בת ציון לאשה הנוה והמעונגה
sources.says: Radak says it means 'I have likened the daughter of Zion to a woman who is at home and pampered'.

sources.quote: פירש דמיתי כרתי כמו נדמו עמי
sources.says: Radak says his father read דמיתי as 'I have cut off', like נדמו עמי.

6:4.headline: Rashi links 'the day has turned' to the Temple burning at dusk
6:4.body: The enemy cries 'woe to us, the day has turned', meaning evening is coming. Rashi says it was as the day turned toward evening that they set fire to the Temple, and he cites the Talmud, Taanit 29a.

sources.quote: כַּאֲשֶׁר פָּנָה לְעֵת עֶרֶב הִצִּיתוּ הָאוּר בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says that when the day turned toward evening they set fire to the Temple, citing Taanit 29a.

6:6.headline: עצה here means 'trees', not 'advice'
6:6.body: The word looks like עצה, 'advice', but you cannot 'cut' advice. Rashi says it comes from עץ, a tree, and means a great many trees, the way דגה means a great many fish. The enemy is told to cut timber for the siege.

sources.quote: וְעֵצָה הָאָמוּר כָּאן – לְשׁוֹן הַרְבֵּה עֵצִים, כְּמוֹ ״דָּגָה״
sources.says: Rashi says עצה here means many trees, as דגה means many fish.

sources.quote: אמר כרתו עצים לעשות מהם דיק ולשפוך סוללה על ירושלם
sources.says: Radak says it means 'cut trees' to build a siege wall and pour a ramp against Jerusalem.

6:7.headline: As a well keeps its water flowing, she keeps her evil flowing
6:7.body: כהקיר is a rare verb that Rashi ties to מקור, a spring. A well keeps bubbling up fresh water, and so Jerusalem keeps producing fresh evil, never stopping.

sources.quote: כְּהָקִיר. לְשׁוֹן מָקוֹר
sources.says: Rashi says כהקיר is from מקור, a spring.

sources.quote: כמו שהבאר מימיה נובעין תמיד בלי הפסק כן הקרה רעתה
sources.says: Radak says that as a well's waters flow without stopping, so her evil keeps flowing.

6:8.headline: תקע can mean 'fasten', and here it means 'tear away'
6:8.body: God warns that His soul may tear away from Jerusalem. Rashi says the related word הוקע is about joining, yet this root also has a sense of removing the join, and many words work both ways. Malbim says it means taking something off where it was stuck.

sources.quote: וְיֵשׁ לְשׁוֹן הֲסָרַת הַחִבּוּר, וְהַרְבֵּה תֵּיבוֹת מְשַׁמְּשׁוֹת כֵּן
sources.says: Rashi says there is also a sense of removing the join, and many words are used this way.

sources.quote: שרשו יקע, ובא על הסרת הדבר ממקום דבוקו
sources.says: Malbim says the root is יקע and it means removing a thing from the place where it was attached.

6:9.headline: סלסלות: baskets, or 'searching through'? Two old readings
6:9.body: סלסלות is a word that appears once. Rashi says Dunash reads it like סלסלה ותרוממך, and Metzudat Zion says that sense is feeling and searching. Menachem ties it to סל, a basket.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ ״סַלְסְלֶהָ וּתְרוֹמְמֶךָּ״ (משלי ד:ח) – כָּךְ פֵּרְשׁוֹ דּוּנַשׁ. וּמְנַחֵם פֵּרֵשׁ לְשׁוֹן ״סַל״
sources.says: Rashi says Dunash explained it like סלסלה ותרוממך, and Menachem explained it from סל, a basket.

sources.quote: ענין משמוש וחפוש כמו סלסלה ותרוממך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means feeling around and searching, like סלסלה ותרוממך.

6:10.headline: ואעידה: a word for 'witness' that here means 'warn'
6:10.body: The root is the one for a witness, but here Rashi says it means a formal warning. Radak explains: a man who warns someone does it before witnesses, so the other cannot deny it later.

sources.quote: וְאָעִידָה. לְשׁוֹן הַתְרָאָה
sources.says: Rashi says ואעידה is a word for giving a warning.

sources.quote: כי המזהיר באחד מזהיר בו בפני עדים כדי שלא יכחיש בו אחר כן
sources.says: Radak says whoever warns another does so in front of witnesses, so the other cannot deny it afterwards.

6:11.headline: סוד here is a gathering of friends, not a secret
6:11.body: סוד usually means a secret. Here Metzudat Zion says it is a group that meets to share secrets and plans. Radak agrees: a company joined by one plan. So סוד בחורים is a band of young men.

sources.quote: קבוצה הנאספת להמתיק סוד ועצה וכן בסוד משחקים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says סוד is a group that gathers to share secrets and plans, as in 'the company of those who laugh'.

sources.quote: סיעה שמתחברים יחד בסוד אחד ובעצה אחת
sources.says: Radak says it means a party joined together in one secret and one plan.

6:15.headline: Two words for shame: one felt inside, one put on by others
6:15.body: The verse uses both בוש and הכלים. Malbim says בושה comes from yourself, while כלימה is shame that other people put on you. Radak says these people do not even feel it when others shame them.

sources.quote: הבושה בא מעצמו, והכלימה היא מאחרים
sources.says: Malbim says בושה comes from oneself, and כלימה comes from others.

sources.quote: לא הרגישו בכלימה שיכלימם אדם על רוע מעשיהם
sources.says: Radak says they did not feel the shame when someone shamed them for their evil deeds.

6:19.headline: 'Fruit of their thoughts': what they earn, or what they did?
6:19.body: Rashi reads פרי as שכר, 'payment', what their thoughts earn them. Radak says it means the deeds that grew out of their thoughts, so God punishes the act and not the thought alone.

sources.quote: פְּרִי מַחְשְׁבוֹתָם. שְׂכַר מַחְשְׁבוֹתָם
sources.says: Rashi says פרי מחשבותם means the payment for their thoughts.

sources.quote: אינו אומר שיענישם על המחשבה לבד אלא על מעשיהם שהם פרי מחשבותם
sources.says: Radak says God does not punish them for the thought alone, but for their deeds, which are the fruit of their thoughts.

6:23.headline: 'Ready like a man for war': the riders, or the horses?
6:23.body: Radak reads ערוך as the soldiers: each is armed like a man set for a duel. Malbim says it points back to the horses, trained for battle as if they understood it like men.

sources.quote: כל אחד מהם יהיה ערוך בכלי זיין כמו איש אחד הנועד להלחם עם חברו
sources.says: Radak says each of them will be armed like one man set to fight another.

sources.quote: מוסב על הסוסים, כאילו הסוסים יבינו תכסיסי מלחמה כאנשים
sources.says: Malbim says ערוך refers to the horses, as if the horses understood war tactics like men.

6:25.headline: Written to the community as one, read to each person
6:25.body: In the written text the verbs end in י, a form for one person, addressing the people as a single body. The reading tradition says them with ו, to each person. Radak says the meaning is the same.

sources.quote: מדבר כנגד הכנסה תלכו תצאו קרי מדבר כנגד הפרטים והענין אחד
sources.says: Radak says the written form speaks to the community, the read form speaks to the individuals, and the meaning is one.

6:25.headline: מגור מסביב: 'fear all around', or 'a gathering all around'?
6:25.body: Rashi gives two readings. One is fear. The other is gathering, as in מגורי אל חרב, so the enemy surrounds the city. Radak notes that Targum Jonathan reads it as those gathered around. Malbim says the root גור covers both fear and gathering.

sources.quote: מָגוֹר. יִרְאָה. לָשׁוֹן אַחֵר: לְשׁוֹן אֲסִיפָה
sources.says: Rashi says מגור means fear, and another reading is that it means gathering.

sources.quote: ויונתן תרגם מגור מסביב מקטלא למתכנשין מסחור סחור
sources.says: Radak says Jonathan translates it as killing by those gathered all around.

sources.quote: בא על הפחד ועל האסיפה
sources.says: Malbim says the root is used both for fear and for gathering.

6:26.headline: Rashi hears God saying 'upon us': upon Me and upon you
6:26.body: The verse says the destroyer comes 'upon us'. Rashi says, so to speak, that God is speaking here, and 'us' means both Him and the people.

sources.quote: כִּבְיָכוֹל, עָלַי וְעָלֶיךָ
sources.says: Rashi says, 'so to speak', that it means 'upon Me and upon you'.

6:27.headline: בחון: an assayer who tests, or a strong tower?
6:27.body: The word can mean testing, and it can mean a fortress. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as a tower of strength, so Jeremiah is made a fortress among the people. Malbim says the word carries both senses.

sources.quote: בָּחוֹן. לְשׁוֹן חוֹזֶק, כְּמוֹ ״עֹפֶל וָבַחַן״
sources.says: Rashi says בחון means strength, as in עופל ובחן in Isaiah.

sources.quote: ענין מגדל חזק וכן עופל ובחן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a strong tower, as in עופל ובחן.

sources.quote: שם בחון בא על בחינה ונסיון, ועל מבצר או חוזק
sources.says: Malbim says בחון is used both for testing and trial, and for a fortress or strength.

6:27.headline: 'Fortress' (בחון) leads to 'you will test' (ובחנת)
6:27.body: God calls Jeremiah a בחון, a fortress, and then says ובחנת, 'you will test their ways'. Radak says this is a play on words: because He named him בחון, He says ובחנת.

sources.quote: ואמר ובחנת לשון נופל על לשון לפי שקראו בחון אמר ובחנת את דרכם
sources.says: Radak says ובחנת is a word falling on another, because He called him בחון, He says ובחנת את דרכם.

6:28.headline: סרי סוררים: 'turned aside', or 'princes' of the stubborn?
6:28.body: Rashi reads סרי as 'turned away from the road'. Radak says the ס stands in for ש, so it is שרי סוררים, 'princes of the rebels', whose servants are rebels too.

sources.quote: סָרֵי סוֹרְרִים. סָרִים מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi says סרי סוררים means those who have turned aside from the way.

sources.quote: השרים הם שרי סוררים כלומר שעבדיהם סוררים
sources.says: Radak says the princes are שרי סוררים, meaning that their servants are rebellious.

6:29.headline: The burnt bellows is the prophet's own throat, says Radak
6:29.body: The verse pictures a silversmith whose bellows burns out while the silver stays impure. Rashi calls it a parable. Radak says the bellows is the prophet's mouth and throat, worn out by speaking to people who will not change.

sources.quote: מָשָׁל הוּא: כְּשֶׁצּוֹרְפִים כֶּסֶף נוֹפְחִין בַּמַּפּוּחַ
sources.says: Rashi says it is a parable: when they refine silver they blow with the bellows.

sources.quote: והמפוח הוא פיו וגרונו
sources.says: Radak says the bellows is the prophet's mouth and throat.

7:4.headline: "The Temple of the Lord" three times: why repeat it?
7:4.body: The false comfort says "the Temple of the Lord" three times. Radak and Metzudat David say the three are the porch, the hall and the inner room, each called היכל, which is why "they are" is plural. Rashi follows the Targum: three times a year you appear there. Radak also allows that repeating a word simply stresses it.

sources.quote: ואמר שלשה פעמים היכל ה׳ על האולם וההיכל והדביר שכולם נקראים בשם היכל ולזה אמר המה בלשון רבים כי שלשה המה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it repeats "Temple of the Lord" three times for the porch, the hall and the inner room, all called היכל, and so says "they are" in the plural, since there are three.

sources.quote: תְּלָת זִמְנִין בְּשַׁתָּא אַתּוּן מִתְחֲזִין קֳדָמוֹהִי
sources.says: Rashi cites the Targum: "three times a year you appear before Him".

sources.quote: ויתכן כי הכפל לחזק כי כן מנהג הלשון לכפול המלות לחזק הענין פעם בשתי מלות פעם בשלש
sources.says: Radak says the repetition may be for emphasis, since the language repeats words to strengthen a point, sometimes twice and sometimes three times.

8:4.headline: Who turns back here: Israel, God, or both?
8:4.body: The verse says ישוב, 'turn back', twice. Rashi and Metzudat David give one turn to Israel and one to God. Malbim says Israel turns from evil, then turns back to it again.

sources.quote: לִכְשֶׁיִּרְצוּ לָשׁוּב מֵרָעָתָם, לֹא יָשׁוּב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִגְּזֵרָתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi reads it: when they want to turn from their evil, God will not turn back from His decree.

sources.quote: וכי אם מי מהם ישוב בתשובה האם לא ישוב ה׳ מחרון אפו בתמיה
sources.says: Metzudat David reads it as a question: if one of them repents, will God not turn from His anger?

sources.quote: כי השב מדרך הרע לדרך הטוב נקרא שב מדרכו, ואם חוזר ושב אל דרך הרע הנהו שב שנית
sources.says: Malbim says one who leaves evil has turned once, and one who goes back to evil has turned a second time.

8:7.headline: The stork is named for its kindness
8:7.body: חסידה, the stork, sounds like חסד, kindness. The sages said it got the name because it shares its food with its companions.

sources.quote: חסידה פירשו רז"ל זו דיה לבנה ולמה נקרא שמה חסידה שעושה חסידות עם חברותיה כלומר במזונות שמחלקה להם
sources.says: Radak quotes the sages: the bird is called חסידה because it does kindness with its companions by sharing food.

8:7.headline: Which bird is the עגור?
8:7.body: The Aramaic translation makes it a swallow. Radak also reports a view that it is a bird that can be taught to chirp a few words like a person.

sources.quote: ועגור. תרגם יונתן וסנוניתא
sources.says: Radak notes the Aramaic translation renders it 'swallow'.

sources.quote: וי"מ הוא העוף המצפצף מלות מעטות כלשון בני אדם כשמלמדין אותו
sources.says: Radak reports others who say it is a bird that chirps a few words like people when it is taught.

8:13.headline: 'Gather' and 'make an end' sound alike
8:13.body: אסף אסיפם sounds like one verb said twice. Malbim says the first means gather and the second comes from סוף, end: God gathers them to finish them.

sources.quote: הראשון שרשו אסף מענין אסיפה וקיבוץ והשני מנע"ו סוף וקץ ובא לשון נופל על הלשון
sources.says: Malbim says the first word is from gathering and the second from end, a play of one word on another.

sources.quote: שניהם לשון כליון אסף מקור מן ואספת נפשך ונפש ביתך אסיפם מן יחדו יסופו
sources.says: Radak says both words mean destruction but come from two roots, אסף and סוף.

8:13.headline: What God gave them: laws they broke, or crops they lose?
8:13.body: Rashi reads 'what I gave them, they transgressed': the laws. Radak reads 'what I gave them will pass from them': the fruit will go to their enemies.

sources.quote: כָּל זֹאת תִּהְיֶה לָהֶם עַל כִּי נָתַתִּי לָהֶם חֻקִּים וְעָבְרוּ עֲלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says all this comes because God gave them laws and they broke them.

sources.quote: מה שנתתי להם רוב הפירות וברכתי פרי אדמתם יעברו מהם שיאכלום האויבים
sources.says: Radak says the fruit God blessed them with will pass from them, and enemies will eat it.

8:14.headline: Poison water: snake venom or a bitter plant?
8:14.body: מי ראש is a poisoned drink. Rashi makes ראש the venom in a snake's teeth. Metzudat Zion makes it a bitter herb.

sources.quote: הוּא אֶרֶס שֶׁבְּשִׁנָּיו
sources.says: Rashi says ראש is the venom in a snake's teeth.

sources.quote: ראש. שם עשב מר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ראש is the name of a bitter plant.

8:16.headline: His 'mighty ones' are his stallions
8:16.body: אביריו usually means mighty men. Rashi and Radak say here it means horses, and the neighing is theirs. The Aramaic translation keeps 'his warriors'.

sources.quote: וּמָצִינוּ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר סוּסִים נִקְרָאִים אַבִּירִים
sources.says: Rashi says horses are called אבירים elsewhere too.

sources.quote: על הסוסים אמר אביריו
sources.says: Radak says the word refers to the horses.

sources.quote: מִקַל פְּסִיעוּת גִבָּרוֹהִי
sources.says: The Aramaic translation renders it 'from the sound of his warriors' steps'.

8:17.headline: Snakes that have grown deaf to every charm
8:17.body: Rashi says a snake becomes a צפעוני after seventy years and blocks its ear to the charmer. The enemy will be like that: no pleading will move it.

sources.quote: לְסוֹף שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה נַעֲשֶׂה צֶפַע, וְאוֹטֵם אָזְנוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁמַע לְקוֹל חֶבֶר הַמְלַחֲשׁוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says after seventy years a snake becomes a צפע and stops its ear so it cannot hear the charmer.

sources.quote: לא תוכלו לרצות את האויב בדברים רכים ותחנונים
sources.says: Metzudat David says you will not be able to win over the enemy with soft words and pleading.

8:19.headline: God's 'anger' is spoken of only over idol worship
8:19.body: Maimonides quotes this verse to show a pattern: the Bible speaks of God being angry or jealous only about idol worship.

sources.quote: לא תמצא לשון חרון אף ולא לשון כעס ולא לשון קנאה אלא בעבודה זרה דווקא
sources.says: Maimonides says you will find words of anger and jealousy said of God only about idol worship, and cites this verse.

9:2.headline: וידרכו is the word for bending a bow by stepping on it
9:2.body: A bow is bent by treading on it, so the verb for bending a bow is דרך, "tread". The prophet pictures the tongue as a bow, and says they bent it for lies.

sources.quote: וּבָרַגְלַיִם דּוֹרְכִין אוֹתָהּ, לְכָךְ קוֹרֵא אוֹתָהּ דְּרִיכָה
sources.says: Rashi says a bow is trodden with the feet, which is why it is called דריכה.

sources.quote: ולפי שהמשילם לקשת אמר לשון הדרכה הנופל בקשת
sources.says: Metzudat David says that since the tongue is likened to a bow, the verse uses the word for bending a bow.

sources.quote: הדרך לדרוך ברגל על הקשת למתחו היטב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the custom is to tread on the bow with the foot to stretch it well.

9:3.headline: עקוב: Rashi says lie in wait, Metzudat Zion says make crooked
9:3.body: Rashi reads it as "will lie in wait". Metzudat David and Metzudat Zion read it as bending or twisting, like "the crooked shall be made straight".

sources.quote: אָרוֹב יֶאֱרֹב
sources.says: Rashi says עקוב יעקב means he will lie in wait.

sources.quote: יעקם ויעוות דרכו מול אחיו
sources.says: Metzudat David says he will bend and twist his way toward his brother.

sources.quote: ענין עקום ועיוות וכן והיה העקוב למישור
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means crooked and twisted, like "the crooked shall become straight" in Isaiah 40:4.

9:3.headline: The verse hears Yaakov's name in "every brother is a deceiver"
9:3.body: Radak says the word means deceit, like Esau's "he has supplanted me (ויעקבני)". Malbim says the verse takes its picture from Esau's words about his brother Yaakov.

sources.quote: ענין התרמית והערמה כמו ויעקבני זה פעמים
sources.says: Radak says the word means deceit and trickery, like "he has supplanted me these two times".

sources.quote: ולקח מליצתו מן האח שאמר עליו הכי קרא שמו יעקב ויעקבני
sources.says: Malbim says the verse took its figure of speech from the brother who said of Yaakov, "is he not rightly named Yaakov, he has supplanted me".

9:6.headline: צרף smelts out the dross; בחן tests for it first
9:6.body: Malbim says צירוף is melting in fire to remove the dross, and בחינה is checking whether there is dross. The test comes first, and a second test can follow the smelting.

sources.quote: הצירוף היא ההתכה באש להסיר הסיגים והבחינה הוא שמנסה אותו אם יש בו סיג, והבחינה קודם הצירוף, שאחר שבחן וראה שיש בו סיג אז מצרפו
sources.says: Malbim says צירוף is melting in fire to remove dross, and בחינה is testing for dross, which comes first and then he smelts.

sources.quote: והבחינה הבא אחר הצירוף הוא אם א"י אם נצרף כראוי בוחן שנית, ואם מוצא סיג צורף שנית
sources.says: Malbim says a test after the smelting checks whether it was refined properly, and if dross is found he smelts again.

9:6.headline: מפני: because she is my people, or because of her sins
9:6.body: Radak says God cannot leave them in their evil, since they are His people. Jonathan translates it as "because of the sins of the congregation".

sources.quote: מִן קֳדָם חוֹבֵי כְּנִישְׁתָּא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi quotes Jonathan translating מפני בת עמי as "because of the sins of the congregation of Israel".

sources.quote: כי איך אעשה שלא אצרפם מפני שהיא בת עמי לא אוכל שלא אצרפם כי איך אניחם ברעתם והם נקראים עמי
sources.says: Radak says God cannot leave them in their evil, since they are called His people.

9:7.headline: Written שוחט, read שחוט: a killing arrow, or a drawn-out one
9:7.body: Rashi says שחוט means drawn out, like "beaten gold", and gives a second reading, slaughtering. Radak says the written form means one who kills and the read form means drawn, and cites the sages' rule that שחט means to draw.

sources.quote: מָשׁוּךְ; כְּמוֹ ״זָהָב שָׁחוּט
sources.says: Rashi says שחוט means drawn out, like "beaten gold", and offers another reading, true slaughtering.

sources.quote: כן כתיב וקרינן שחוט והכתיב ר"ל כמו שוחט שהוא הורג כן הורגים הם בני אדם בלשונם הרע
sources.says: Radak says it is written שוחט and read שחוט, and the written form means a killer, as they kill people with their evil tongue.

sources.quote: ושחט אין ושחט אלא ומשך
sources.says: Radak quotes the sages that ושחט means and he drew, and so "gold שחוט" and "an arrow שחוט".

9:7.headline: Who speaks in "deceit speaks"? Malbim says deceit itself
9:7.body: Since לשון is a feminine word, Malbim says the verb should be דברה, "she spoke". He reads מרמה, deceit, as the speaker itself.

sources.quote: למפרשים היל"ל דברה כי הלשון נקבה תמיד או מרמה דברו ויסב על העם, ולדעתי המרמה הוא העצם המדבר
sources.says: Malbim says the commentators expect דברה since the tongue is feminine, but in his view deceit itself is the thing speaking.

9:9.headline: נצתו: from ציה, a dry waste, or from יצת, to burn
9:9.body: Rashi ties it to ציה, a dry waste. Radak and Malbim say the root is יצת, to burn, and Malbim says it came to mean ruin of any kind.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן ״צִיָּה״ (ירמיה ב:ו), וְכֵן ״נִצְּתָה
sources.says: Rashi says נצתו is like the word ציה, a dry waste.

sources.quote: ענין חרבן וכן נצתו כמדבר ושרשו יצת
sources.says: Radak says it means ruin, and that its root is יצת.

sources.quote: שרשו יצת ורובו בא על הכליון שנעשה ע"י האש, ומזה הושאל על כליון של חורבן ושממה
sources.says: Malbim says the root is יצת and it mostly means destruction by fire, borrowed for the ruin of devastation.

9:9.headline: בהמה adds up to 52, the years Judah lay empty
9:9.body: The sages count the letters of בהמה as 52. They read it as a hint that for 52 years no one passed through Judah.

sources.quote: חֲמִשִּׁים וּשְׁתַּיִם שָׁנָה לֹא עָבַר אִישׁ בִּיהוּדָה; מִגָּלוּת צִדְקִיָּהוּ עַד פְּקִידַת כּוֹרֶשׁ מֶלֶךְ פָּרַס חֲמִשִּׁים וּשְׁתַּיִם שָׁנָה הָיוּ, וְרֶמֶז לַדָּבָר: עַד בְּהֵמָה. חֶשְׁבּוֹנָהּ בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא חֲמִשִּׁים וּשְׁתַּיִם
sources.says: Rashi says for 52 years no one passed through Judah, and that "until בהמה" adds up to 52.

sources.quote: חמשים ושתים שנה לא עבר איש ביהודה שנאמר על ההרים וגו' מעוף השמים ועד בהמה נדדו הלכו בהמה בגימטריא נ"ב
sources.says: Radak quotes R. Yehuda that for 52 years no one passed through Judah, and that בהמה adds up to 52.

9:14.headline: מי ראש: snake venom, or the juice of a bitter herb
9:14.body: Rashi says it is snake poison. Metzudat Zion says it is the juice of a bitter plant, and Radak gives both, saying it may be named for the viper's head.

sources.quote: מֵי רֹאשׁ. אֶרֶס נָחָשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says מי ראש is snake poison.

sources.quote: מי סחיטת ראש והוא שם עשב מר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the juice squeezed from ראש, a bitter plant.

sources.quote: לפי שהוא מי סחיטת העשב שקורין רוש גם יש שהוא מראש הפתן
sources.says: Radak says it is the juice of the plant called רוש, and some say it comes from the head of the viper, which is why it is called ראש.

9:16.headline: החכמות are the skilled mourners, fewer than the ordinary ones
9:16.body: Radak and Metzudat David say the wise women are the ones skilled in laments. Malbim adds that ordinary wailing women are in every town, while the skilled ones are few and must be sent for.

sources.quote: שהן חכמות בדברי הספד וקינה
sources.says: Radak says the wise women are skilled in words of mourning and lament.

sources.quote: הן הבקיאות למהר לסדר אמרי עצבון רוח ויגון
sources.says: Metzudat David says they are the ones skilled in quickly composing words of sorrow and grief.

sources.quote: המקוננות נמצאות בכל עיר ועיר וא"צ רק קריאה, והחכמות הן מועטות במדינה שלחו, לקרותן מרחוק
sources.says: Malbim says wailing women are in every town and only need calling, while the wise women are few and are sent for to be called from afar.

9:17.headline: עפעפים: the eyelids, or the pupils of the eyes
9:17.body: Metzudat Zion and Radak say the pupils. Malbim says it is what closes the eye from seeing, the eyelid, and Jonathan has the eyeballs.

sources.quote: הוא אישון העין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says עפעפים is the pupil of the eye.

sources.quote: הם אישוני העינים
sources.says: Radak says it means the pupils of the eyes.

sources.quote: העפעף בו סוגרים את העין מראות
sources.says: Malbim says the עפעף is what closes the eye from seeing.

sources.quote: וְגַלְגַלֵי עֵינָנָא יִגְרוּן מַיָא
sources.says: Jonathan translates it as "the orbs of our eyes will run with water".

9:18.headline: השליכו: the homes threw us out, or the enemy threw them down
9:18.body: Rashi gives both: the dwellings cast out their dwellers, or the enemies threw our dwellings to the ground. Malbim says the verb refers to the enemies.

sources.quote: אֶת שׁוֹכְנֵיהֶם. וְיֵשׁ עוֹד לוֹמַר: כִּי הִשְׁלִיכוּ הָאוֹיְבִים אֶת מִשְׁכְּנוֹתֵינוּ לָאָרֶץ
sources.says: Rashi says they cast out their dwellers, and another reading is that the enemies threw our dwellings to the ground.

sources.quote: כאילו משכנותינו השליכו אותנו חוצה
sources.says: Radak says it is as if our dwellings threw us outside.

sources.quote: מוסב על האויבים
sources.says: Malbim says the verb refers to the enemies.

9:19.headline: נהי and קינה: the women sing, the girls answer "woe"
9:19.body: Malbim says נהי is the cry "woe, woe" (הוי הוי), as in Amos 5:16. He reads the verse as married women reciting the קינה and young girls answering with נהי.

sources.quote: הנשים הנשואות מדברות הקינה, והבנות הקטנות עונות נהי, שנהי הוא מה שאומרות הוי הוי
sources.says: Malbim says the married women recite the קינה and the young girls answer נהי, which is the cry "woe, woe".

9:23.headline: Maimonides: "know Me" means knowing God's ways of kindness and justice
9:23.body: He says that if only knowing God were meant, the verse would stop at "understand and know Me". It adds that I do kindness, justice and righteousness, so knowing God means knowing His actions and copying them.

sources.quote: ההתפארות היא בהשגתי ובידיעת תאריי, כלומר פעולותיו
sources.says: Maimonides says boasting is in understanding Him and knowing His attributes, which are His actions.

sources.quote: וביאר לנו בפסוק הזה (ירמיהו ט,כג) שאותן פעולות שיש לדעת ולחקות הן חסד, משפט וצדקה
sources.says: Maimonides says the verse shows that the actions to know and copy are kindness, justice and righteousness.

9:23.headline: Maimonides: "on the earth" means God's care reaches the earth too
9:23.body: He says the word is the pivot of the Torah. Some thought God's care stops at the sphere of the moon and the earth is left alone, and this verse says God does kindness, justice and righteousness on the earth.

sources.quote: הוא הוסיף עניין חשוב אחר, והם דבריו "בָּאָרֶץ" (שם), שזה הוא ציר התורה
sources.says: Maimonides says the added word "on the earth" is the pivot of the Torah.

sources.quote: ולא כמחשבתם של המתפרצים, שחשבו שהשגחתו יתעלה מסתיימת אצל גלגל הירח
sources.says: Maimonides says it rejects the view that God's care ends at the sphere of the moon.

9:24.headline: מול בערלה: circumcised in flesh but not in heart, or two groups
9:24.body: Rashi reads it as one person: circumcised, yet with a foreskin of the heart. Radak reads it as two groups: Israel, the circumcised, and the nations, who are in the foreskin.

sources.quote: עַל כָּל מוּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עָרְלָה, אֲפִלּוּ עָרְלַת לֵב
sources.says: Rashi says it means any circumcised person who has a foreskin, even a foreskin of the heart.

sources.quote: על כל מול אלו ישראל שהם מולים ועל אשר בערלה אלו האומות שזוכר
sources.says: Radak says מול is Israel, who are circumcised, and אשר בערלה is the nations he names.

sources.quote: על כל מול, ועל כל אשר בערלה ועל כל נמשך לשנים
sources.says: Malbim says it covers the circumcised and the uncircumcised both.

9:25.headline: קצוצי פאה: those at the far edge, or the ones who cut
9:25.body: Rashi, Metzudat Zion and Radak read it as people far off at the edge of the wilderness, as if cut off by distance. Malbim says it names the sons of Ishmael and Keturah, who cut off their foreskins.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן קָצֶה: הַמּוּקְצִין בִּפְאַת מִדְבָּר
sources.says: Rashi says it is from the word for edge, those set apart at the edge of the wilderness.

sources.quote: ענין חתוך כמו וקצץ פתילים (שמות ל״ט:ג׳) ור״ל נפרדים וכאלו הם קצוצים אלה מאלה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means cut, so separated, as if cut off from one another.

sources.quote: שוכנים בקצה הפאה כלומר רחוקים במדבר והדבר הרחוק יקרא קצה ויקרא פאה כי קצה ופאה רחוקי הגבול בכל דבר וקצה וקצץ בענין אחד
sources.says: Radak says they dwell at the edge, far off in the wilderness, and that קצה and קצץ are one thing.

sources.quote: כינוי בני ישמעאל ובני קטורה שכן לקמן (כ"ה כ"ג) את דדן ואת תימא ואת בוז ואת כל קצוצי פאה, ודדן מבני קטורה ותימא מבני ישמעאל, והוסיף את כל קצוצי פאה ר"ל בני ישמעאל וב"ק הקוצצים ערלותיהם
sources.says: Malbim says it is a name for the sons of Ishmael and Keturah, those who cut off their foreskins.
